When the sun goes down, the clouds under us go pink and gold, like the tips of my veils.
The sky's got bumps in it. Air bumps. You fly through one and your insides go hup!
Aure brings the dew. In the morning my veils are all sparkly with it, like I've been sugared.
Vell carries the songs. When I sing in the evening, it's Vell who takes my song off to the other villages.
When Borre's coming, the bell does the long peal and everybody hurries home. Even the koi hide.
Sefa is warm and lazy and makes the peaches smell twice as peachy. Sefa days are slow-loop days.
There are other villages in the sky! Far, far off. At night I can see their lanterns, tiny as glow berries.
I think the Cloud Koi were little clouds once that learned to swim.
Falling stars are just stars that tried a loop and couldn't hold it. Like me, my first go.
Up top, the sky's bluer than down low. I can tell. I've been in both.
Thunderclouds look like big grey whales, but they don't sing. They grumble.
My veils are woven from cirrus. That's the highest cloud there is. So a bit of me is the very top of the sky.
Inside a cloud it's all white and wet and quiet, and you can't even see your own feet. Not that I use them.
The sky is wide enough for everyone, the grown-ups say. Even walkers. Even very wide walkers.
When there's no wind at all, everyone gets twitchy. Never trust a still day. I don't even trust a still minute.
The best bit of the sky is just under the clouds, where walkers can't see you. Shh.
I followed a feather all the way down to the cloud tops once. Mum had to come and fetch me.
Night sky's the best sky. The lanterns come on and the stars come on, and it's like being inside a jar of glow berries.
The sky's got layers, like a peach. The warm bit, then the windy bit, then the cold high bit where you shiver.
When the whales sing it goes right through you. Your veils shiver. I think weather is just whale song you can see.
From the top of the Lantern Spire I can see the edge of the world curving. Or a hill. It might be a hill.
When people go up past the blue, they become part of the sky. So the sky's full of old Cirri. That's why it's so wise.
Under the village the clouds are a floor that isn't. You can see the green through the gaps.
I like watching cloud shadows crawl over the ground. They're the only things down there faster than walkers.
A bird flew right under me today. I looked down at it. It looked up at me. We were both very surprised.
Above the great lantern on the Spire, that's the highest I've ever been. It was cold and I was very proud.
Thunder sounds closer up here because it is closer. That's the worst thing about the sky.
Morning sky is pink, noon sky is blue, evening sky is gold, and night sky is every colour pretending to be black.
Sometimes a little cloud gets caught on our islet. I let it stay. It's a guest. That's the Courtesy.
The moon's the same moon over every village. I asked {friend}. We checked at the same time.
I'm saving a flower for the Wind Shrine. It's for {wind}, because {wind} has the sky today and was nice to me.
The Old Singers carry little clouds on their backs. I'm small enough to ride on one. Nobody will let me.
When it snows, the snow starts above us and falls past us. I catch the flakes before the walkers get them. Sorry.
The best thing in the sky is shooting through a cloud fast and coming out the other side all damp and shiny.
If the sky had a door, I'd knock and say fair wind and ask to see the stars getting ready.
baby.ground: Have you really touched the ground? With your actual feet? Is it warm? Does it tickle?
I think the ground is soft like a cushion and walkers bounce a little at every step. Do you bounce?
{friend} says the ground goes all the way down to the bottom of the world. What's under the bottom?
Is the ground the same everywhere, or are there squashy bits? I'd want the squashy bits.
I've never touched the ground. Not even a toe. One day I might. With a very long stick.
Does the ground move? It looks still, but things that look still are always up to something.
Do walkers get stuck to the ground? Is that why you can't fly? Is it like honey?
The ground is where the rain goes when it's finished. It must be very wet down there. Do you have to wring your feet out?
Fire lives in the ground, I heard. Do you have to keep stepping so your feet don't get hot?
If I touched the ground, would I be grounded forever? Mum says no. Mum's never tried it.
What colour is the ground up close? From here it's green and brown and sometimes white. Is it stripy?
I bet the ground smells like the inside of a flower pot.
What do worms do all day? Are they sad they can't fly? Are you?
How do you know where the ground stops and the sea starts? Do you just fall in?
Walkers live on the ground so they don't fall off. But what if the ground falls off?
I dropped a peach once and it went all the way down. Did you find it? It was a good one.
Trees just stand there on the ground. Like walkers! Are trees walkers that stopped?
The ground has holes in it called caves. What's in the holes? More ground? Ground that's hiding?
Is it true the ground's so big you can walk for days and not reach the end? Days! On feet!
If I touched the ground I'd feel heavy, I think. Like after eleven peaches.
From up here the ground looks like a quilt. Is it stitched? Who stitched it?
Do walker houses sit right on the ground? Doesn't the ground mind them sitting there?
Does the ground make noises? Grown-ups say it rumbles sometimes. Is it hungry?
The bell-villages down there have iron bells and stone houses, and they don't sink, because the ground holds them up. Clever ground.
Do you sleep right on the ground? Flat on it? Do the worms tuck you in?
Do walker babies fall over? We never fall over. We fall down sometimes, but never over.
The ground's where all the heavy things go. Bells and stones and walkers. No offence.
If I ever went down to the ground, I'd take a peach, in case it was hungry.
Is mud the ground melting? Does it turn back into ground afterwards?
Our bridges go squeak. What noise does the ground make when you walk on it? Thump? Crunch? Hello?
I saw sheep down there once. They looked like little clouds that fell down. Did they hurt themselves?
The ground holds everyone up all day long. I said thank you to it once. Loudly. From here.
Is it dark under the ground? Darker than night? Do they have lanterns under there?
If there's a ground at the bottom, is there a ceiling at the top? Who walks on that?
I think the ground is just a very big, very slow cloud that got tired and lay down.
Water down there stays still in big puddles called seas. Up here water never stays anywhere. It's much better behaved on the ground.
Does sand taste like sugar? It looks like sugar. Somebody should check. You check.
What's a hill? Is it ground that's trying to fly?
Snow lands on the ground and just stays there? Doesn't it want to go anywhere?
Our islets have roots hanging out of the bottom. I think they're reaching for the ground. I think they miss it.
Do you ever wish the ground would let go of you? Just for a bit? I'd wish that, if I were you.
Is the ground hard or soft? Both? It can't be both. ...It can? The ground is very confusing.
When walkers dig a hole, does the ground grow back over it? Or is there a hole forever?
Grown-ups say walkers are sturdy. I think it's because the ground pushes back on you all day, like a hug that never stops.
A walker told me the ground goes all the way down to a place made of fire. I'm never going there. Not even for a whale.
baby.song: 'Koi, koi, round you go, fast as Sefa, slow as snow.' I made that up. Snow isn't slow, really, but it rhymes.
'Aure in the morning, Vell at night, keep your veil whole and your heart light.' Half of it's mine and half's the grown-ups'.
'Walker, walker, heavy feet, stomp across the bridge and squeak!' Don't be sad, it's a nice song. The squeak's the best bit.
'One loop, two loops, three loops, four, Mum says no more, so I do one more.' That one's true.
'Borre, Borre, go away, come back on a sunny day.' We sing it when the bell does the long peal.
'Little cloud upon the whale, where are you going? Tell the tale!' The whales never answer. They're busy.
'Ding dong, the bellkeeper's late, the dawn's come early and has to wait.' Don't sing it near the Bell Pagoda.
'Lantern, lantern, up so high, you're the littlest star in the sky.' I sing it to the sky lanterns so they don't feel small.
'Lengthen me, lengthen me, weave my veils as long as the sky!' It doesn't rhyme yet. It's not finished. Neither am I.
'Who's the fastest in the sky? Not the whale and not the fly. ME!' You have to shout the me.
'Honey's slow and peaches sweet, glow berries are the night-time treat.' The gardener taught me. I added the night bit.
'Hush, little koi, the thunder's away, Borre's gone off to grumble and play.' Mum hums it in storms. I sing it to the koi.
'Fair wind here and fair wind there, fair wind tangled in my hair!' I sing it when my veils blow in my face.
'Ground, ground, way down low, what you're like I'll never know.' It's a sad one. I sing it fast so it isn't.
'One for Aure, one for Sefa, one for Vell and one for Borre... Borre, sorry!' Borre's hard to rhyme, so I say sorry.
'Old Singer, Old Singer, hum me a cloud, a small one, a soft one, not one that's loud.' It hasn't hummed me one yet.
'Up past the koi, up past the bell, up past the Spire, and I'm up there as well!' You sing it higher and higher. Your voice too.
'Mend my veil with moth and thread, then off to the nest and off to bed.' The weavers sing it. I sing it faster.
'Dawn, dawn, the comb goes through, cirrus white and cirrus blue.' It's the weavers' song. I'm allowed to borrow it.
'Raindrops falling past my nose, where they're going, nobody knows.' Walkers know. Where do they go? On you?
'Sky peach, sky peach, soft and round, please don't fall down to the ground!' I sing it to the peaches on the tree. So far it's working.
'Whale goes by and the sky goes hum, koi go round and here I come!' That's my going-somewhere song.
'Never trust a still, still day, the wind's just hiding round the bay.' What's a bay? I don't know. It rhymed.
'Clap for the morning, clap for the bell, clap for the walker who walks so well!' That's for you. Take a bow. A walker bow.
'Hop, skip, loop the loop, catch a cloud in a honey scoop.' A honey scoop is the spoon thing. It goes very sticky in a cloud.
'Sing the day down, gold and red, the sun's going under the clouds to bed.' The sun sleeps under the clouds. It's always there in the morning, so it must.
'Sky Scale, Sky Scale, shiny and small, I'll find you one day if I look at all.' I've looked at all. Not yet.
'Thunder's loud but the nest is warm, I'm not afraid of a silly old storm.' I am. A bit. The song helps.
'Glow berry, glow berry, light up my nose, now I can see where everybody goes.' You eat one and pretend your nose glows. It doesn't. It should.
'Lift me, Wind Stone, lift me high, bring me a walker up to the sky!' I sang it at the Lift Dock, and then you came! Eventually.
baby.song.night: 'Curl up small, curl up tight, cushion below and stars alight.' ...That's the whole song. I'm too sleepy for another verse.
'Hush now, veils, stop your flutter, the moon's come up like a pat of butter.' Dad says butter's a walker food. Is it yellow? Is it round?
'Lantern low and lantern dim, the night-moths can't get in.' Mum sings it. Then I check under the cushion anyway.
'Goodnight, Aure, goodnight, Sefa, goodnight, Vell, goodnight...' Mm. I forgot the last one. The cold one. Night.
'Sleep, little cloud, float, little cloud...' I can't remember the rest. Oh, I'm yawning in the middle of it.
'The koi are asleep in the pool, the bell is asleep in the tower...' Shh. Now I'm meant to be asleep too.
'Over the cushion, under the stars, no one's as sleepy as we are.' I'm not sleepy. I'm only singing about sleepy.
'Hum, hum, the whale goes by, carrying dreams across the sky.' Mum says the whales bring the dreams. Mine had peaches in it.
'One last loop and then to bed...' Can I do the loop? Just the one? There. That was it. Night.
'Soft as cirrus, light as down, sleep up high and never come down.' The grown-ups sing it to babies. I'm not a baby. I still like it.
'Hush-a-bye, the bell's asleep, the gardener's counting koi like sheep.' Walkers count sheep, Dad says. I count koi. I get to four.
'Moon, moon, look at me, sleeping as high as high can be.' The {moon} looked. I saw it look.
'Vell takes the songs and carries them far, past every lantern and every star.' Will Vell carry mine? It's very small. I'm singing it small.
'Drift, drift, drift...' Did I fall asleep? I think I fell asleep in the air for a bit. That's allowed.
'Night-night, nest, night-night, peach, night-night everything I can reach.' Then you touch everything. I can reach a lot.
baby.secret: Promise not to tell? The koi with the bent fin is my favourite. It's slower than the others, so I always beat it in races. That's not why. That's a bit why.
The long peal of the bell scares me. Not anything else. Just that. That's the secret.
There's a sky peach right at the top of the tallest skywood tree that nobody's noticed. It's mine. I'm waiting for it to be perfect.
The bellkeeper hums when nobody's listening. Very badly. I listen.
The windkeeper falls asleep in the wind column sometimes. Just floating up and down, snoring. I've seen it.
The weavers keep a basket of the very softest cloud for Lengthenings. I touched it once. With one finger.
{friend} can't do a loop yet. They do a turn and shout "loop!" Don't say anything.
Once, in the snow, I licked the bridge rail and stuck to it. Mum doesn't know. I got unstuck by myself. Mostly.
There's a gap under the Market Pavilion where you can hide and hear everything the Skymerchant says to walkers. They say "splendid" a lot.
My veil's got a little tear at the tip. I hide it in my sash. If the weavers find it they'll mend it with night-moth.
When I'm Lengthened I'm going to ask for one more gold thread than anybody else. Just one. Nobody will notice.
It's not the dark that scares me. It's what the dark might be thinking.
Grown-ups think we're all asleep by the end of the Evensong. Some of us are. I just shut my eyes and listen to the low notes.
The lamplighter lets me light one lantern every evening. The little one by the koi pool. That's my lantern.
Dad can't reach the high part of the Evensong. Dad just opens and shuts and hopes. I've seen.
There's a little cloud that keeps coming back to our islet. I call it Wisp. I think it comes back for me.
There's a honeycomb hidden in a basket in the Loom House. I put it there a while ago. It might be a problem now.
The koi in the far pool have a leader. It's the white one with the gold patch. It told me. Not with words.
When I fly very high on my own, I shout my name at the sky. It never shouts back, but I like it.
Mum and Dad still hold veil-tips at the Evensong. They think nobody sees. Everybody sees.
Under my cushion there's a pot of shiny things. Three buttons, a scale off a koi and a walker's key. Is it your key?
There's a Wind Shrine nobody else knows about. Far away. I'll show you when we're Veil-Kin.
Sometimes I eat a glow berry under my cushion at night so my nest glows.
The gardener talks to the skywood trees. I asked what the trees say back. "Patience," apparently.
Everybody wants to be a harpist. Not me. I want to be a windkeeper. I haven't told anyone. Now I've told you.
One of the Old Singers winked at me. Nobody believes whales can wink, so now it's a secret.
Nobody's as brave as they say. That's the real secret. Everyone's a bit pretend.
The Skymerchant keeps a special peach behind the lanterns. I know because I had a bite. A small one.
When the grown-ups talk about the Ruined Belltowers they go quiet. I think somebody's great-great-somebody lived there.
I practise walking. In the air. Like this. One, two. It's very hard. Don't tell anyone a Cirri was walking.
My first word was "peach". Mum says it was "Mum". It was peach.
The bell's got a crack, a tiny one, on the inside. The bellkeeper says it makes it sing truer. I'm the only child who knows.
Sometimes I fly under the islet and hang off the roots. You can see everything from under there. I'm not supposed to.
I've got a secret name for you. A nice one. Mostly nice. I'll tell you when you've earned it.
I'm the one who let the koi into the wrong pool. It was an accident. A big accident. They seem happy.
If you put your ear to the harp when nobody's playing, you can hear the wind thinking.
{neighbour} sings to their peaches to make them sweeter. It works. I've tried them. Several times.
I mix up the winds sometimes. So I just say fair wind to all of them and hope.
Don't tell the grown-ups, but I think walkers are the most interesting thing in the sky. More than whales. Nearly.
I told the little ones the bell is alive. It's not. It might be.
baby.family: Our nest is the one with rose veilcloth over the door. Not that we use the door. That's for you.
There's Mum, Dad, me and the koi cushion in our nest. The koi cushion counts. It's family.
At night we all curl up in the air over our cushions. Dad snores, Mum hums, and I count both.
When I'm Lengthened I'll still sleep in our nest. Until I'm very grown. Then nearby. Then probably still in it.
Our nest smells of peaches and veilcloth. Every nest smells a bit different. Ours is the best.
Mum and Dad met at an Evensong when their veils got tangled. That's the whole story. They tell it every single time.
My family's been in {village} since forever. Since before the bell, Dad says. That's very forever.
In our nest, whoever wakes first opens the round window and says good morning to the wind.
We sing the Evensong in a row, all of us. I'm in the middle so I don't drift.
Mum says I've got Dad's laugh and Mum's veils. My loops are my own, though. Nobody gave me those.
My grandparents went up past the blue before I was born. Mum says they're in the high wind now. I wave at it.
When there's thunder, the whole family squashes into the nest and hums. It gets warm, but nobody minds.
Every morning Mum and Dad say "fair wind" to me like I'm a guest. I say it back like I'm a guest too.
Every family has its own song. Ours goes hmm-hmm-hmmmm. How it ends is a family secret.
I've got a cousin in a village far away. We've never met. I wave at their lanterns, in case.
I'm the littlest in my nest, so I get the last peach. The last one's always the ripest. Being littlest is good.
Families keep their old veil scraps in a box. Ours has a bit of everyone. Mine are the shortest.
When Mum and Dad are busy, the whole village keeps an eye on me. That's how it works up here. Everyone's a bit everyone's.
Our nest's on the windiest islet. Dad says it keeps us lively. Mum says it keeps us awake.
If I'm not home by the dusk bell, Mum calls my name across the whole village. That's why everyone knows my name.
Do walkers have nests? Have you got a Mum and Dad? Do they worry about you coming up here?
Our nest is very messy. Mum says nests are meant to be messy. Dad says not that messy.
My family all have jobs. Mine's being the child. It's a very busy job.
Breakfast in our nest is peaches, in the air. Then more peaches. Sometimes berries, for a change.
There might be a baby in our nest one day. I'm going to teach it everything. Loops first. Then manners.
baby.family.mum: Mum's name is {mother}. Everyone knows {mother}, and {mother} knows everyone. It takes ages to get anywhere.
{mother} can do the slowest, most beautiful turn in the sky. Everyone stops to watch. I'm going to learn it.
If you see {mother}, don't say I was near the edge. {mother} has very good ears and very long veils.
Every dawn {mother} combs my veils. They're still short, but they're the tidiest short veils in {village}.
When {mother}'s cross, there's humming. When {mother}'s happy, there's singing. Today it's been humming. I'd better be good.
When I had a bad dream, {mother} said the whales would carry it off on their backs. They did.
I was born at dawn while Aure was blowing, {mother} says. That's why I'm always awake so early.
Nobody makes honey peaches like {mother}. No cooking. Just peaches with honey. That's the whole recipe.
{mother} says I'm the light of the nest. {mother} also says I'm the noise of the nest. I think I'm both.
{mother} lets me ride on the end of a veil when we fly home. It's like being a little cloud on a whale.
When I was a baby I tried to eat my own veil, {mother} says. I don't believe it. I believe it a little.
If you want {mother} to like you, bring flowers. Any flowers. Even ground ones. Especially ground ones.
When the bell does the long peal, {mother} pulls me close and hums. I pretend it's for me. I think it's for both of us.
{mother} always finds me. I hid inside a cloud once and {mother} just said "{name}, out." Like that. Out.
One day I'll be as tall as {mother}. Then taller. Then I'll comb {mother}'s veils for a change.
baby.family.dad: Dad's name is {father}. {father} can whistle with no hands. Dad says that's not a trick. It is.
Nobody in {village} tells worse jokes than {father}. What do you call a koi with no fins? I don't know. {father} never finishes it.
{father} took me out to see an Old Singer once. We flew beside it till my veils went cold. I'm not allowed to tell Mum how far.
Every night {father} snores like the long peal of the bell. The koi wake up.
When I'm tired, {father} lets me hold a veil and tows me home like a little boat. What's a boat? A walker thing, {father} says.
The first time I flew, I went backwards, straight into the koi pool. {father} laughed for a whole day.
{father} is brave about everything except night-moths. When one comes, {father} waves a cushion at it.
If you ask {father} about the big storm, you'll be there till dawn. It gets bigger every time.
The low part of the Evensong is what {father}'s teaching me. I go "hmmm" and it comes out "meep".
Once I fell asleep at the Evensong and started drifting off, and {father} caught me by the veil like a kite.
Peach stones are for planting, {father} says, so we plant them. None have grown. Skywood is patient, apparently. I'm not.
{father} says I've got the fastest veils in the nest. Mum says that's only so I'll fly to bed fast.
{father} and I have a secret signal. Two waves and a loop means "I'm all right." One wave means "peach, please."
When {father} laughs, both veils shake. I make {father} laugh on purpose so I can watch.
{father} is the best at hide and seek. I've never found {father}. Mum says that's because {father} goes home to nap.
baby.weather.clear: Not a cloud above us. They're all underneath, like a big white floor. Perfect for loops.
On days this clear you can see right down to the ground. I waved at a cow. It didn't wave back.
Clear days make the koi sparkle. I'll find a Sky Scale today. I can feel it in my veils.
The sun's so bright on the clouds below you have to squint. I'm squinting at you. Hello.
The bellkeeper says fine days are for flying far. I'm only allowed to fly medium.
It's so bright my veils have gone see-through. Look, you can see your boots through them!
Not even a wisp up top. {wind} is being gentle today. On gentle days you can hear the koi blowing bubbles.
On sunny days I lie on my back in the air and let the sun warm my belly. Like a very long, very flat koi.
baby.weather.rain: The rain's falling past us. Look, it goes right by, all the way down to the walkers. Sorry, walkers.
I fly up into the rain and catch drops on my tongue. They taste of high places.
Rain makes my veils heavy. I have to fly low and slow, like an old whale.
Mum says I'm not to fly in the rain or I'll get soggy. I'm already soggy, so I might as well.
When it rains the koi go silly. They leap up after the drops, and I leap up after the koi.
The bridges go slippy in the rain. Not for me. For you! Careful, groundling.
Rain on the veilcloth awnings goes pitter-pat. It's the Loom House singing. It doesn't know the words.
Everyone's gone in except me and the koi. The rain's ours now.
baby.weather.thunder: Did you hear that? That was thunder. I'm not scared. I'm only holding your sleeve so you're not.
Borre's grumbling. I have to stay near the nest. Can you stay near the nest too? Just a bit?
The lightning lit the whole cloud below us. It looked like a lantern that got cross.
When it thunders the whole village hums. If you hum too, the thunder can't get into your ears. Try it.
I counted between the flash and the boom. I got to two. That's close. That's very close. Hmmmm.
The bell did the long peal and everyone's in their nests, and I'm still here. I should go. Soon. In a light breeze.
The Old Singers don't sing thunder. Thunder's what happens when the weather gets cross because nobody's listening.
Lightning's the thing the sky's most scared of. Then fire. Then fireworks. Lightning's the worst one.
baby.weather.snow: Snow! It's coming down past us like feathers. One landed on my nose and went away.
Snowflakes are bigger up here, because they haven't been squashed by falling yet.
My veils have gone all frosty. If I shake them it snows a little bit off me. Look! I'm weather!
Do your feet get cold in snow? Feet are a bad idea in snow. You should fly.
The koi pool's got a skin of ice on top. The koi are underneath, looking up, all puzzled.
There's snow on the Lantern Spire. The lantern looks like it's wearing a little cloud for a hat.
I made a snow-koi on the bridge rail. It's got two berry eyes. It's watching you.
When it snows, the whole sky goes quiet. Even the wind whispers. Snow's the hush weather.
baby.time.dawn: The bell's rung! That means dawn, which means I'm meant to be getting up, and I am. I'm up. Mostly.
Aure's out, and everything's damp and pink. My veils are full of dew. I'm all sparkles.
The weavers are out combing cirrus already. They go before the sun to get the soft bit. I came to watch.
Dawn's the best because nobody's used the sky yet. It's all fresh.
It's so early the koi are still sleepy. I tickled one. It only blinked.
Look, the clouds under us are going gold underneath. Dawn starts at the bottom of the clouds and works its way up.
baby.time.morning: Morning's for flying fast before the grown-ups need me for anything.
I've had two peaches and a berry for breakfast. And a flower. The flower was a mistake.
The gardener feeds the koi in the morning. If you're quick you can get there first and pretend you fed them.
The Market Pavilion's open! The Skymerchant always says good morning to me like I'm a walker with emeralds.
Everyone's busy in the morning, so it's the best time for hiding. Nobody's looking.
The harps are tuning up for the day's wind. It sounds like a koi gargling.
baby.time.noon: Noon! The sun's right on top of us. My shadow's hiding under me like a shy koi.
Middle of the day means lunch. In the air. With peaches. Again.
At noon the clouds below go so bright you can't look at them. Walkers have it easy. They're in the shade.
Everybody rests at noon except me. I'm too full of loops to rest.
Noon's when Sefa likes to blow, on Sefa days. Warm and lazy. I get lazy at noon too.
Half the day's gone already! I haven't done half my plans. I've done one. It was a loop.
baby.time.afternoon: Afternoons are long and slow. The koi swim slower, I fly slower, even the clouds go slower.
In the afternoon the light goes golden and my veils look like they've been dipped in honey.
I've been playing since lunch. I'm not tired. My veils are tired. Look, they're drooping.
In the afternoon the grown-ups have little naps in the air. You can hear them breathing from the bridges.
Is it afternoon already? The day goes so fast up here. Is it slower on the ground? It looks slower.
The afternoon wind's the best for kites, Dad says. Kites are walker things. Little Cirri on strings!
baby.time.evening: The sky's going gold and pink. Those are the Evensong's colours. We'll be singing soon!
The lamplighter's lighting the lanterns. I count them as they come on. One... two... ninety.
Vell's bringing in the songs from the other villages. If you listen hard, you can hear them.
The dusk bell! Everyone's coming to the Veil Court. Are you coming? You can just stand. Standing counts.
I'm not tired. I'm only yawning because it's evening and everybody else is.
In the evening the koi go to the bottom of the pool in a ring. Like their own little Evensong.
baby.time.night: I'm meant to be in my nest. I am in my nest. Nearly. It's just over there.
The stars are out! More than last night. Or the same. I always lose count after the bright ones.
At night the clouds below go silver and the ground goes dark. Are you scared down there at night? I would be.
Night-time is night-moth time. Stay near a lantern. I'll stay near you. You're near a lantern.
Shh. Everybody's asleep in the air. Look, you can see the veils going up and down with the breathing.
The {moon}'s out. I'm not supposed to be. Don't tell the moon.
baby.time.late: It's so late. The lanterns are going sleepy. I'm not. My eyes are. My eyes are going sleepy.
Everyone's asleep. Even the koi. Even the bell. Even the wind, nearly.
Why are you awake? Walkers sleep lying down. Can't you find somewhere flat?
I woke up and couldn't get back to sleep for thinking about whales. Big ones. Bigger ones.
I'm very, very not tired. That was a yawn. It doesn't count.
It's the middle of the night! I've never been up this late. What happens now? Is there anything good?
baby.routine.play: I'm in the middle of a game! I'm hiding. You've just told everyone where I am by talking to me.
We're playing koi-tag and I'm the koi. You can't catch a koi. Nobody can. Not even the gardener.
What was the game? I've been playing so long I've forgotten. Tag, I think. Or Whales.
I'm winning! I don't know at what yet, but I'm winning.
Playing is serious business. Tag has rules. They're mostly about who's fastest. Me.
You can play too, but you have to do the counting. Walkers are very good at counting, everyone says.
Shh, I'm hiding from {friend}. Talk quietly. Talk like a cloud.
Round the Bell is a game where you loop the Bell Pagoda. I just won it. There wasn't anybody else.
baby.routine.follow: I'm following Mum. Mum's going somewhere important. I don't know where. That's why I'm following.
Keep close to Mum's veils, that's the rule. Look, they're just there. I can still see them. Mostly.
Mum flies so fast! Short veils can't keep up. After my Lengthening I'll be the one in front.
Hello! I can't stop, I'm following. Well, I can stop a bit. Mum stops to talk to everybody anyway.
Wherever Mum goes, I go. That's the rule till I'm grown. Then I'll go wherever I like, and Mum can follow me. Ha!
Mum needs help today. I'm helping by being nearby. That's my whole job.
Mum's talking to the gardener. They'll be ages. Grown-up talk is very long.
I'm flying in Mum's slipstream. The wind's easier there. It's like being carried.
baby.routine.evensong: It's the Evensong! Shh, you have to sing. Walkers can sing, can't they? Hum, then. Humming's allowed.
I'm in the children's row at the Evensong. We do the high bits. The grown-ups do the long bits.
Sing the day down! That's what we do. Look, the sun's going. It's working!
I'm not singing this bit because I'm talking to you. That's allowed. It's a rest.
The harpists lead and we follow. I follow very loudly.
When we all sing together my veils shiver. Can you feel it in your feet?
At the end, everyone holds the last note until the bell. I can hold it for ages. Watch. Hmmmmm... ages!
Shh! This is the slow part. I always nearly fall asleep in the slow part.
baby.routine.shelter: I'm in the nest because of the thunder. You can come in. Duck your head. Walkers are tall.
Mum's humming to keep the thunder out. It's working. Mostly. Hum with us?
We have to stay in till the storm's gone. I'm counting cushions. There are four. Still four.
I'm not hiding. I'm sheltering. That's different. Sheltering is brave.
Is it scary on the ground in a storm too? Or does the ground hold on to you so the lightning can't find you?
The nest smells of peaches and warm cloud. It's the best place to be in a storm. Under the cushion's even better.
When the thunder's right on top of us, I put my veils over my ears. They're short, but they help.
We stay here till Borre's finished. Borre always finishes, Dad says. Eventually.
baby.routine.idle: Doing nothing is my favourite thing. It's harder than it looks.
I was just hovering here thinking about peaches. Now I'm thinking about you. And peaches.
Something was bound to happen if I waited long enough. Then you happened! Good.
The koi are asleep, the grown-ups are busy and the clouds aren't doing anything interesting. I'm so bored.
I was practising hovering really, really still. You've spoiled it by being interesting.
Floating about is a real thing to do. Ask anyone. It's what I've been doing all day.
That cloud was about to turn into something. Then I looked at you. Now I'll never know what.
I had nothing to do, and now I've got you to talk to. That's much better than nothing.
baby.village.whale: A whale! A whale! An Old Singer! Can you hear it? It's humming. It's humming at us!
The whale's got three little clouds on its back today. One of them looks like a peach.
A whale's a blessing, Mum says. I'm going to fly out and say fair wind to it. Close-ish.
Shh! If you listen hard you can hear the whale singing the weather. That bit's rain. I think.
I want to ride on its back with the little clouds. Mum says not till I'm Lengthened.
The whale's so big it makes its own wind. My veils go all ripply when it swims past.
Do you have whales on the ground? Big ones? Do they sing? Ours sing.
I sang back to the whale and it hummed lower. That means it heard. Dad says it didn't. It did.
baby.village.koi: Look at the koi! That one's the cheekiest. It nibbles my veils.
The gardener counts the koi every morning. I count them every afternoon. We never get the same number.
Koi swim so wiggly. I fly straight. I've been trying to learn the wiggle. It's very hard with short veils.
If a koi sheds a scale near you, that's luck. I've been waiting here ages. Nothing yet. Any moment.
The koi always come when I hum. Or when the gardener has food. Mostly the food.
The gold one's my favourite. Don't tell the others. They get jealous. You can tell by their fins.
I'm not chasing them. Look, I'm hovering very politely. They just keep swimming away.
Do koi sleep? With their eyes open? That one's staring at me. Is it asleep?
baby.village.children: That's my best friend over there. We're having a race later. Don't tell anyone, it's a surprise race.
All the children are out! We're playing Old Singers. Want to be the whale? You'd be good at it.
The little ones always want to play with the big ones. I'm a big one. Well, a middle one.
We're a gang. A loop gang. We do loops. That's all we do. It's a very good gang.
Shh, the others are hiding and I'm counting. Seven... eight... I lost count talking to you.
We're all getting Lengthened one day. Then we'll be grown-ups. We've all promised not to be boring.
Everyone's showing off for you. Look, they're all doing loops now. Mine was better.
The little ones think walkers are giants. I told them you're only a medium giant.
baby.village.harp: That's a wind harp. When the wind goes through it, it plays all by itself. Like the wind is singing.
The harp's tuned to {wind} today. The harpist does it every morning. It sounds different every day.
I'm not allowed to touch the harp strings. I can blow on them, though. That's not touching.
Stand right by the harp and the music goes through your feet. Feel it? I bet walkers feel it more.
I can play one note on the harp. Just one. It's a very good note.
The harp's humming! That means the wind's happy. When it whines, the wind's grumpy.
When I'm grown I'm going to play the harp at the Evensong. Or ring the bell. Or both at once.
The harpists can make the harp sound like a whale. I tried. It sounded like a koi with hiccups.
baby.village.evensong: The Evensong's starting! Come and sing! Everyone's coming!
I love the Evensong. Everyone sings and the sky goes gold and then it's bedtime. I don't love that bit.
Look, everyone's gathering over the Veil Court. The harps are going. It's the best bit of the day.
You can sing with us. Nobody minds if you're out of tune. The grown-ups are, sometimes.
At my first Evensong I sang the wrong song the whole way through. Nobody noticed except Dad.
When the Evensong ends, the sky's gone dark and the lanterns are lit. It's like the song did it.
I sing loudest when the Evensong's for someone who's gone up past the blue. So they can hear.
Vell carries the Evensong to the other villages. Somewhere far away a child's hearing me right now.
baby.held: Ooh, your {item}! Can it fly? Everything should be able to fly.
What's your {item} for? Is it a walker thing? Show me how it works!
Can I hold your {item}? I'll be careful. I'll use both hands. And my veils.
Is your {item} heavy? Don't drop it off the edge. Villages have sunk for less.
I've never seen anything like your {item}. Where did you get it? The ground?
Your {item} looks very important. Is it important? It looks important.
If I had your {item} I'd show everybody, and then I'd hide it in my nest.
Does your {item} smell like the ground? Can I sniff it? ...It does! A bit!
I'll swap you a peach for your {item}. Two peaches. A peach and a half.
Mum says not to grab walkers' things. I'm not grabbing. I'm just looking at your {item} very hard.
That {item} is the best thing I've seen all day. Apart from the whale. And you.
Everything from the ground is so solid. Your {item} looks like it would sink through a cloud. Plop. Gone.
What does your {item} do? Does it do tricks? Make it do a trick!
Don't let your {item} near the koi pool. The gardener gets cross about things in the pool.
When I'm grown I'll have one just like your {item}. Only lighter. Everything up here has to be lighter.
Does your {item} have a name? I'd give it a name. Something brave.
You carry your {item} everywhere? Even up the Wind Stone? Your arms must be very strong.
Is your {item} a present? For me? ...No? Could it be, one day?
Hold your {item} up so the koi can see. They like looking at new things.
Grown-ups would say your {item} is walker business. I say it's everyone's business. What is it?
baby.player.hurt: You're hurt! Does it sting? I'll blow on it. Fooo. Better?
Oh no, what happened? Did the ground bite you? I always knew the ground bit.
You've got a scrape! The gardener has salve for scraped koi. It might work on scraped walkers. Go and ask!
Are you all right? Walkers are sturdy, everyone says. You don't look very sturdy just now.
Sit down. Oh, you can sit! Sit down, and I'll hover over you like a little cloud of shade.
Have a peach. Peaches fix most things. Not big things. Medium things.
baby.player.wet: You're soaking! Did a cloud fall on you? That happens to me all the time.
Ha! You're dripping on the bridge. Drip, drip. The koi think it's raining.
Shake like a koi! Like this! ...Walkers don't shake? You should. It's very good.
You're as wet as me after cloud-diving. Did you dive? From where? Not from here, I hope.
You'll catch a cold, Mum would say. I've never known what you catch. Something wet, I think.
Stand where the wind's blowing and hold your arms out. It'll dry you like a veil on the line.
baby.player.elytra: Are those borrowed wings? Elly-tra? Can you really fly in them? Show me! Show me!
You've got walker wings! They're very stiff. Mine are floaty. Yours are sort of crunchy.
Dad says walkers with wings are the bravest walkers of all, and the worst at landing. Is that true?
Your wings look like a beetle's. A very big beetle. A beetle-walker! Can I touch them?
If you can fly with those, race me! ...You have to jump off something first? That's cheating. And scary.
Where do walker wings come from? Do they grow somewhere? Can I find some? I'd give them to a koi.
baby.player.veil: You've got a veil! A real Cirrus Veil! Are you a Cirri now? A bit? You're a walker-Cirri!
Your veil's longer than mine! That's not fair. I'm the one who's supposed to have veils.
You look so nice in a veil. Do a twirl! Twirl! Look, it goes round with you!
Keep your veil whole. A Cirri is only as high as their veil is whole. That counts for walkers too.
With a veil you could almost come to the Evensong as one of us. Almost. You'd have to stop walking.
Did the weavers make your veil? They make mine too. That makes us veil-cousins.
baby.player.flying: You're flying! You're actually flying! Wait for me! Wait!
Look at you up here! You fly very stiffly. Like a plank. A happy plank.
A flying walker! I'm telling everybody. They won't believe me. Fly past the koi pool so they can see.
You're in my sky! Our sky, I mean. You can share it. Just don't bump the lanterns.
How are you doing that? You haven't got veils! Is it magic? Is the ground pushing you up?
Fly lower, you're making me dizzy. No, fly higher! I want to see how high a walker goes.
baby.player.edge: Careful! You're right on the edge! Walkers don't bounce, Mum says. Step back. Please?
Don't lean over! If you fall I can't catch you. You're much too big.
Ooh, you're near the edge. That's where I'm not allowed. Step back so I don't get told off for watching.
Look down! It's a long, long way. Now stop looking down and step back. Thank you.
Edges are for flyers. Come away, groundling. Come over here where the grass is.
Mum says the edge is where walkers get brave and silly at the same time. Which are you?
baby.first_meeting: A walker! A real live walker! I'm {name}. I've never met a walker before. Have you met a Cirri?
Hello! Who are you? Where did you come from? How did you get up here? Can you fly? Why not?
Oh! You're much bigger than walkers in stories. In stories they're about my size.
Mum told me about walkers. Kind and sturdy and a bit slow, Mum said. Hello, kind, sturdy, slow walker!
Fair wind! I'm {name}! I live here! It's the best village in the sky! Have you seen the others? Ours is better.
A groundling came up the Wind Stone! That's you! Welcome! That's the Courtesy. I know all about it.
I'm not meant to talk to strangers, but walkers are guests, so you're a guest-stranger. That's allowed. Hello!
You're new! I'm {name}. I know everybody here, and now I know you. Nearly. What's your name? {player}! That's a good one.
Are you real? Can I poke you? Just your sleeve. ...You're real!
Ooh. Both your feet are touching the floor. At the same time. Does that feel strange?
Fair wind and welcome to {village}! I'm the welcoming child. There isn't really one. I've decided it's me.
I've been waiting all my life to meet a walker! Well, since the day before yesterday, when I heard about walkers.
Is that what walkers look like? I thought you'd have more legs. Two is quite a lot, I suppose.
Hello! Don't be scared. I'm small and I'm friendly. There's peach on my face, but that's not dangerous.
A walker! Stay right there, I'm getting everyone! No, wait. I want you to myself for a bit first. Hello!
You came all the way up from the ground? Was it windy? Did you scream? I'd scream. The good kind.
Hello. I'm {name}. I'll call you groundling, because I don't know your name yet. And because it's fun to say.
Welcome! You've come at exactly the right time. Something exciting's about to happen. It's you. You're the exciting thing.
Oh, hello! I've drawn walkers before, but I got the feet wrong. Yours are much bigger. I'll fix it.
Fair wind, stranger! I'm {name}, of {village}. That's how grown-ups say it. Did I sound grown-up?
baby.hurt: Ow! Why did you do that? I didn't do anything!
That hurt! I'm telling Mum! I'm telling everybody!
You hit me! Walkers are supposed to be kind! The stories said so!
Ow, ow, ow. My veil's all bent. What was that for?
Stop it! I'm only little! Go and hit a cloud!
That wasn't a game! Games don't hurt! You don't know how to play at all!
I thought you were my friend. Friends don't do that. Not even walker friends.
Don't! I'll fetch the windkeeper! The windkeeper's very big. Well, tall-ish.
Why? I was being nice! I was going to give you a peach!
That hurt my arm and my feelings. Both of them.
Mum! Dad! The walker hit me! ...They can't hear. I'll shout louder. MUM!
You're a mean walker. A heavy, mean walker. I'm not talking to you.
baby.night: Mmf... is the bell ringing? It's not ringing. Then why am I awake?
Shh! You'll wake Mum! ...You woke me. That's nearly as bad.
I was dreaming about a whale and you made it swim away.
Walker? It's dark. Walkers should be asleep, lying flat, the way you do.
Hmm? I'm asleep. I'm talking in my sleep. Go away, sleep-walker.
Is something wrong? Is it a night-moth? Don't let the night-moths in!
I was curled up so nicely. Now my veils have all come uncurled. Thanks very much, groundling.
Too early. Or too late. One of those. Goodnight.
You woke me up! ...Well, now that I'm awake, can I have a peach?
Mmm. Five more loops. I mean five more minutes. I mean sleeping. Goodnight.
Who's there? Oh, it's you. Your boots are very loud at night.
I'm not meant to talk after the dusk bell. You're making me break the rules.
baby.walk_off: I don't want to talk to you. I'm going to find the koi. They're nicer.
Hmph. I'm flying away now. Very fast. Don't follow. You can't anyway.
You were mean before. I haven't forgotten. Children have very good memories. Bye.
No. I'm still cross. I'll be cross until the Evensong at least.
I'm telling Mum on you. Again. Bye!
My veils are still bent from last time. I'm going home.
Not talking. Not talking. Still not talking. Bye.
Walkers who hit don't get to play. That's the rule. I just made it.
Go away. No, I'll go away. I'm faster.
I'm going up where you can't reach. See? Can't reach me.
baby.busy_off: I've got to go! The others are waiting for me. We're playing whales. Bye!
Fair wind! Back soon. Well, back sometime. Back!
Oh! Mum's calling. Or a koi's splashing. I'll go and see which. Bye!
I have to go and find my peach stone. I dropped it somewhere. It's very important. Bye!
Sorry, I can't stay. I'm in the middle of a game. I'm supposed to be hiding! Bye!
That's enough talking. Now it's time for loops. Watch me go! Wheee... bye!
Got to fly! The koi are doing something interesting. Fair wind, groundling!
Bye! I'll tell you the rest later. I'll forget, but I'll try.
I'm off to the Cloud Garden. You can't come, you're too slow. Joking! You can come. Later. Bye!
I just remembered I was going somewhere. I'll remember where on the way. Bye!
Fair wind, walker! Don't fall off anything while I'm gone!
That was a good talk. Now I need to go and do three loops to celebrate. Bye!
baby.apology_accepted: All right. I forgive you. But you have to say sorry to my veils too.
You said sorry properly, with your whole face. All right. Friends again?
That's all right. Mum says everybody makes mistakes. Even walkers. Especially walkers.
I forgive you. I'm not cross any more. My veils are, a bit. They'll get over it.
You're sorry? Really sorry? ...All right. I believe you. You've got honest boots.
Fine. You can be my friend again. But I'm watching you. With both eyes.
Apology accepted! That's what grown-ups say. I've always wanted to say it.
All right. Let's start again. Fair wind! I'm {name}. ...See? All fresh.
baby.apology_wary: Hmm. You said sorry. I'll think about it. I'll think for a long time.
Sorry's nice, but my arm still hurts. Say it again tomorrow.
Maybe. I'm still keeping a bit away. Just this much.
Mum says sorry is a start. Only a start. What's the rest?
I don't know. You could be pretending. Walkers are good at pretending, I heard.
All right... but don't do it again. I'll be watching from up here.
I want to forgive you. I'm just not finished being cross yet.
Sorry? Hmm. Bring me a peach and I'll believe you more.
baby.gift.loved: For me? Really? I love it! I love it more than loops!
Oh! Oh! This is the best present anybody's ever given me! Ever! In the whole sky!
I'm keeping this {gift} in my nest forever. Under my cushion. Right next to me.
Thank you! Thank you! I'm doing a loop for you. Two loops. Three!
I'm so high! That means happy! I'm the highest I've ever been!
How did you know? How did you know I wanted this more than anything?
You're the best walker in the world. In the sky. In both!
I'm going to show everyone. Every single person. Even the koi.
Mum! Dad! Look what the walker gave me! ...They're not here. I'll show them later. Twice.
I'll remember this {gift} when I'm Lengthened and old and have the longest veils in the sky.
You're my favourite walker. You'd still be my favourite if I knew a hundred walkers.
Thank you! I've gone teary. Happy teary! Don't look!
baby.gift.liked: Thank you! That's very nice of you. I like this {gift} a lot.
Ooh, for me? Thank you, walker! It's going with my shiny things.
That's a nice present. I'll show {friend}.
Thank you! I like it lots. Not as much as peaches. But lots.
Lovely! You're very kind, for a groundling. For anyone, really.
That's what you say, isn't it? Thank you very much. I really mean it, too.
For me? You're nice. I'm doing a small loop for you. There!
I like it! What do I do with it? I'll work it out.
Thank you! It's going on the high shelf in my nest, where it's safe.
That's very good. Thank you. Now I owe you something. I'll think of something.
baby.gift.neutral: Oh. Thank you. What's it for?
Thank you. I don't know what it is, but thank you.
Hmm. It's very... ground-ish. Thank you anyway.
Is this a present? It's a present! Thank you. It can live under my cushion.
Oh! Um. Thank you. Mum says always say thank you, even when you don't know what it is.
What does it do when nobody's looking? Thank you, anyway. I'll watch it.
Thank you. I'll give it to Mum. Mum likes odd things.
It's... nice? It doesn't fly. But it's nice.
baby.gift.disliked: Ew! What is it? Take it back! No, wait, be polite. Thank you. Take it back!
That's heavy! Too heavy! Things like that sink villages!
Why would anybody want this {gift}? Do walkers really like these?
No, thank you. I don't like it. Sorry. It smells of ground.
It's horrid. I mean, thank you. But it's horrid.
Are you teasing me? This is a teasing present. I can tell.
I'm not touching it. You keep it. It suits you better.
Mum says don't make a face when someone gives you something. I'm trying not to. It's very hard.
That's not a present, that's a punishment! What did I do?
Fire things and heavy things and smelly things are the worst presents. Which one is this?
baby.gift.limit: You've given me so many presents today! Mum says that's enough. Save some for tomorrow!
No more! My hands are full and my nest is full and I'm full of being happy.
That's too many for one day. I'll get spoiled. Mum says spoiled children go soft like old peaches.
Stop, stop! Keep it for tomorrow. Then I'll have something to look forward to.
I can't take any more today. That's a rule. I don't know whose. But it's a rule.
You're very generous. Too generous! The grown-ups will think I've been begging.
Thank you, but no more today. One present a day is nice. Lots is too much to carry.
Keep that one. Tomorrow it'll be a surprise again.
baby.level_up: I like you more now! I don't know how it happened. It just did.
You're not just a walker any more. You're my walker. Well, one of my favourites.
We're friends now. Real friends! Not pretend ones. I'm telling everyone.
All high, that's how I feel when you come. That means happy. Very happy!
Guess what? You're my best walker friend. Don't tell the other walkers.
You know what? I'd share my last peach with you. That's very serious. Ask anyone.
I'll teach you a loop when you've got a veil. You're good enough to learn now.
There's a spot at the Evensong saved for you, right next to me. It's a very good spot.
You're my friend now. That means you're allowed to know my second-favourite koi.
Every time you come up, I'm happier than the last time. Is that how friends work?
My veils go all fluttery when you visit. That means something good. I think.
Want to know my real name? It's {name}. Oh, you knew. Well, now it's more real.
When I'm Lengthened, you have to come. I'll show you my long veils first. Before anyone!
Mum says you're a good walker. I said I knew that ages ago.
You're nearly family now. Like a cousin. A heavy cousin. The best kind.
baby.gift.bring: I brought you something! A pebble of cloud. It won't last, so look at it quick!
Here! A koi scale! A real one. A small one. It fell off by itself, I didn't pull.
A flower from the Cloud Garden, for you. The gardener said I could. I asked afterwards.
This is for you. It's a feather. A bird dropped it, and I caught it before it reached the ground.
Hold out your hand. Shut your eyes. ...It's a peach! I didn't even take a bite. Not a big one.
Veilcloth scraps make very good bracelets. This one's for you. It's a bit wonky. It's lucky, though.
Here, have a glow berry. Keep it for when it's dark. It'll help.
Look, a smooth stone from the bottom of the koi pool! I've carried it all day for you. The koi didn't want it.
The best petal, for you. The pinkest one. It matches my veil-tips, so now you match me.
This is a bit of cloud I combed off my veils. Weavers' fluff. Keep it in your pocket for luck.
I wrapped this up in a leaf for you. It's a berry. The sweetest one. I tested all the others.
A present! I didn't know what walkers like, so I brought a bit of everything. A leaf, a petal and a peach stone.
news.born: Have you heard? {other} has a baby! Little {who}, born at dawn with the bell. Tiny veils, no longer than a peach leaf.
{who} is the newest Cirri in {village}. {other}'s little one. I've only seen a nose and a bit of veil so far, but it's a very fine nose.
The weavers are already measuring cloud for {who}'s first little veils. {other} says there's no hurry. The weavers say there's always a hurry.
{other} hasn't slept since {who} arrived. Nobody in that nest has. You can hear {who} from the Bell Pagoda, bless those little lungs.
A new baby! {who}, {other}'s. The whole Veil Court sang the welcome-song last night. You should have heard it. {who} slept right through, of course.
I flew past {other}'s nest this morning and there was {who}, bobbing over the cushion like a seed on the wind. Brand new. The sky's never had a {who} before.
The old ones are already arguing about which wind {who} takes after. {other} says {who} takes after the cushion, mostly. Sleeps all day.
Did you hear? {other} has a little one now: {who}. Bring a peach if you visit. Not for the baby. For {other}.
There's a new name in the Evensong: {who}. {other}'s baby. Born small, with a great big voice. We'll have to make room in the ring.
{who} has arrived, and {other} is so high nobody can get them back down to the court. Everyone's been by with honey and flowers. I took a Sky Scale. For luck.
news.grew_up: {who} had the Lengthening! The weavers wove those long veils all night, and at dawn {who} flew the full ring of {village} without stopping once. Grown, just like that.
Have you seen {who}'s new veils? Long as a bridge. {who} keeps looking back at them, as if they might fly off on their own.
It was {who}'s Lengthening this week. Only yesterday a little thing with veils like hair ribbons, and now look. The sky does that. Blink and they're grown.
{who} is grown now. The Lengthening was lovely: the whole village round the Loom House, the weavers singing, the new veils lifted out on the wind. I cried. Everyone does.
{who} grew up! First thing {who} did with the long veils? A loop round the Lantern Spire. Second thing? Got tangled in a skywood. A proper grown-up already.
Big news: {who} has the long veils now. Sky blue at the root, rose at the tips, a thread of gold all down the edges. The weavers outdid themselves.
You'll see {who} flying higher than usual for a while. New long veils do that; you can't help showing them off. I did it for a whole month.
{who}'s grown up and wants a job already. Harpist, gardener, windkeeper, all of them, by turns, before noon. We'll see where the wind puts {who}.
The children are sulking: {who} had the Lengthening and won't play their games any more. Too grown for 'mind the clouds', apparently. That'll last about a week.
{who} grew up. It feels like yesterday {who} was asking me why walkers don't fall over. Now {who} talks about the winds as if they were old friends.
news.passed: {who} went up past the blue. Quietly, at dusk, while the Evensong was being sung. Of all the times to go. I think {who} would have liked that.
We lost {who}. Gone up past the blue. The weavers took {who}'s veils out to the Wind Shrine, the way we do. The sky feels a size bigger, and not in a good way.
{who} has gone up past the blue. I keep looking for {who} at the koi pool. Old habits are the last to fly off.
Did you hear about {who}? Gone up. Past the blue. Don't be sad for {who}; there's nothing heavy up there. Be a little sad for us.
The bell rang slow for {who} this morning. Gone up past the blue. 'Keep your heart light,' {who} always said, usually with a mouthful of peach. I'm trying.
In the night, {who} went up past the blue. The wind was very gentle. The old ones say it always is, for the good ones.
Nobody's sung much since {who} went up. The harps keep playing on their own, though. The wind remembers {who} too.
{who}'s gone, up past the blue. If you knew {who}, sing something tonight. It doesn't matter what. It all goes up the same way.
{who} went up past the blue. The last thing I said to {who} was something about peaches. I wish it had been more. Peaches will have to do.
We said goodbye to {who}. Gone up past the blue, on a fair wind. The children asked if {who} can see us from up there. I said yes. I said: wave.
news.whale: An Old Singer came by! A great Cloud Whale with three little clouds on its back. {who} flew out to sing with it and came back hoarse and glowing.
Did you see the whale? {who} swam beside it half the morning, singing. Says it sang back. {who} hasn't stopped humming since.
A whale passed {village} at dawn, and {who} was first off the rim. I've never seen anyone fly so fast. Blessed for the whole day, you can see it all over {who}.
{who} sang with a Cloud Whale! Out past the Lift Dock, the two of them, one great voice and one small. The whole village stopped to listen.
The Old Singer that came by was huge. Bigger than the Loom House. {who} flew right up to its eye and sang the welcome. Brave, or silly. Both are lucky.
{who} went out to the whale and didn't come back till nearly dark. Says they were singing up a cloud together. See that new one, over there? Probably that one.
A whale went by low enough to touch, and {who} touched it. On purpose! Says it was warm, like a loaf from the market. I can't stop thinking about that.
{who} flew out to meet the Old Singer that passed us and came back with one of its little clouds caught in a veil. Lucky thing. We're all jealous.
Did you hear the singing yesterday? That was {who}, out with a Cloud Whale. The whale did the low part, {who} did the high part, and I did the crying part, from the rim.
That's {who} for you: a whale on the horizon and {who}'s off the rim before the bell. This one sang along for an hour, they say. {who} won't come down from it.
Two whales! A big one and a little one, and {who} sang with both. Says the little one sang off-key. Says it was the best thing {who} has ever heard.
The whale that passed was so slow it took all afternoon to cross. {who} sang with it the whole way, and now {who} can only whisper. Worth it, {who} says. In a whisper.
news.storm: Did you hear the storm last night? Borre came through banging every shutter in {village}. We all hummed in our nests till dawn. Nobody slept a wink.
The storm took two lanterns off a bridge and a whole awning off the Market Pavilion. That awning is three villages away by now. Lucky them.
Lightning so close yesterday you could smell it. At least the bellkeeper gave us plenty of warning. Everyone's still jumpy. Don't clap behind anyone.
After the storm the whole village came out to count: veils, lanterns, koi, children. All there. Then everyone laughed for no reason at all. That's what we do, after.
A storm went over {village} last night. The weavers are mending three torn veils this morning. Somebody tried to fly home late. You can guess how that went.
The thunder was so loud the harps rang on their own. The Hall of Echoes sounded as if it were screaming. It's quiet now. The harps sound tired.
The storm's gone, but the koi are still hiding under the lily pads. The gardeners are coaxing them out with crumbs. Koi hold a grudge.
Were you caught in it, down there? Walkers get our storms after we've had them, you know. It goes down to you when it's done with us. Sorry about that.
The children were so brave in the storm. They hummed the whole time and only cried a little. The grown-ups cried more. Don't tell the children.
Never trust a still day: it was still all morning, and then the storm. The old ones said so and nobody listened. Now everyone's listening. For a week, anyway.
news.visitor: A walker came up the Wind Stone: {who}! Stood on the Lift Dock holding the rail with both hands for a long while. We all came to look. Very politely.
Have you met {who}? Another walker, up from the ground on the Stone's wind. The windkeeper was so pleased. The Courtesy doesn't get used nearly enough.
{who} came up lately. A walker! Asked where the stairs were. We pointed at the sky. {who} didn't find that as funny as we did.
The windkeeper says {who} came up the Wind Stone and went straight back down. Then up. Then down. Some walkers just like the ride.
There's been a walker about, {who}. Very heavy feet. You could hear {who} on the bridges from the Bell Pagoda. We liked {who} at once.
{who} came up the Wind Stone, and the children followed {who} all day, asking to see the bottoms of {who}'s feet. {who} showed them. A good walker.
A walker called {who} came up lately. Brought string for the Skymerchant and asked a hundred questions. Walkers are all questions. We like that.
{who}, the walker, came up for the Evensong and stood in the middle of the Veil Court with both eyes shut. Didn't sing. Just listened. That's allowed. That's lovely, really.
We had a walker up lately, {who}. Looked over the rim and went very pale. Sat on the dock for an hour. The windkeeper brought a peach. Walkers need peaches after heights.
The windkeeper is still talking about {who}: up the Wind Stone, said fair wind to everyone, kept every bit of the Courtesy. Somebody taught {who} well.
news.gift: {other} gave {who} a gift! The very thing {who} loves best. {who} has been showing everyone. Twice.
Did you hear? {other}, the walker, brought {who} a present. {who} was so high afterwards we had to fetch them down for the Evensong.
{who} has been floating about all day with a little gift from {other}, smiling at nothing. That's what a well-chosen gift does. Walkers can be very thoughtful.
{other} found out exactly what {who} likes and brought it all the way up the Wind Stone. All that way, on those feet. {who} nearly cried.
{who} got a gift from {other} and gave one back, so {other} gave another, and now neither knows how to stop. The sweetest quarrel in {village}.
A gift from a walker means more, you know. It's come up so far. {other} gave one to {who}, and {who} swears it's still a bit warm from the ground.
{who} keeps the gift {other} brought in the nest, right over the cushion, so it's the first thing {who} sees at dawn. Love, that is. For the gift, I mean.
Everyone's a bit jealous of {who}: {other} brought the perfect present. Hint, hint. If you happen to be passing with something nice.
{other} gave {who} something lovely. {who} won't say what. Very mysterious. I've seen the shape of it under {who}'s stole, though. I have my guesses.
{who} told the whole Veil Court about {other}'s gift. Then the whole Market Pavilion. Then the koi. The koi didn't care. Everyone else was very happy for {who}.
news.struck: Did you hear? {other} struck {who}. A walker, striking a Cirri, in {village}! We keep the Courtesy for walkers. Walkers are meant to keep one for us.
{who} is still shaking. {other} struck {who}, right by the Veil Court, for no reason anyone could see. We opened the Wind Stone for walkers. Is that the thanks?
{other} struck {who}. Out of nowhere. {who} flew straight up and hid behind the Bell Pagoda for an hour. We don't hit, up here. We barely bump.
Have you heard what {other} did to {who}? Struck them. I won't say more; it makes my veils go stiff. Walkers aren't all like that. Are they?
The windkeeper is thinking of watching the Wind Stone more closely, after {other} struck {who}. The Courtesy is an old promise. It's hard to keep with a sore arm.
{who} won't talk about it, but everyone saw: {other} struck {who} on the bridge. On the bridge! The one we built for walkers.
The children are frightened of walkers again, because {other} struck {who}. It took years to make them curious instead. I'm low about it. Very low.
{other} hit {who}. I keep saying it and it still doesn't sound true. A whole wide sky to be kind in, and {other} chose that.
If you know {other}, tell them this from all of {village}: we saw what happened to {who}. We forgive slowly up here. But we remember quickly.
Poor {who}. {other} struck them, and {who} had only flown over to say fair wind. That's what hurts most, I think. {who} was being kind.
news.story: Did you hear what {other} did for {who}? Helped with the thing that mattered most to {who}, start to finish. A walker! We all think the world of {other} now.
{who} had been carrying a worry for ages, and {other} helped put it down. Just like that. {who} came to the Evensong singing louder than anyone.
{other} helped {who}, and not with something small. With the thing {who} loses sleep over. Walkers have strong hands. It turns out they have kind ones too.
{who} told me everything about how {other} helped. Twice. With a great deal of waving. I'd like to meet {other} one day, and say thank you for all of us.
You'll hear {other}'s name a lot round here now. {other} helped {who} when nobody else could. Up here, that sort of thing gets made into a song.
{who} is high as a lantern since {other} helped out. It mattered so much to {who}. We'll put {other} in tonight's new verse of the Evensong, I expect.
What {other} did for {who}... well. {who} cried at the koi pool, the good kind of crying. The koi came up to see what all the fuss was about.
A walker helping a Cirri with their heart's business: {other} and {who}. It's like something from the old stories, when the Wind Stones were new.
{other} helped {who}, and {who} has been trying to repay it ever since. Peaches, honey, a Sky Scale. {other} keeps saying there's no need. That only makes {who} try harder.
{who} says {other} is the best walker who ever came up the Wind Stone. I said, better than every one? And {who} said yes, without even stopping to think.
news.none: News? The koi had a disagreement this morning. Nobody won. That's the biggest thing that's happened all week.
Nothing much. A quiet sky. The bell rang at dawn and it'll ring at dusk, and in between we all ate peaches.
No news in {village}. Clouds came, clouds went. Somebody lost a ribbon. Somebody found a ribbon. It might have been the same ribbon.
Quiet days are good days, up here. No storms, no whales, no fuss. Just the wind and the harps and the koi going round.
Nothing's happened. I keep waiting for something to, but the sky's just being the sky. It isn't a still day, mind. Only a quiet one. There's a difference.
News? Let me think. The weavers ran out of gold thread and found some more. The lamplighter yawned during the Evensong. That's all I have, I'm afraid.
It's been very calm. Even the children are calm, which is suspicious. Somebody's planning something.
No news, only a rumour. Someone saw a whale's shadow, far off. Probably a big cloud. Probably. Keep an eye out.
Nothing to tell. That's the joy of the sky. You can go a whole week with nothing to tell, and every day of it is still worth flying.
The biggest news is that the peaches are ripening. Every year, the same news. Every year, we're thrilled.
Nothing new. The same faces, the same winds, the same songs. It sounds dull to a walker, I suppose. Up here we call it a fair sky.
News? You're the news, walker. Nothing else has happened. You'll be the talk of the Veil Court tonight. Sorry about that.
A skywood dropped a branch on a bridge yesterday. Nobody was under it. That was the excitement. We talked about it all afternoon.
Oh, nothing, nothing. A quiet run of dawns. The bellkeeper's count is up to {day} now, and most of them have been just like this one.
Nothing worth a song. Not even a hum. Come back after the next whale; there's always news after a whale.
Nothing new. The lift's been quiet; no walkers but you. The windkeeper has started chatting to the Wind Stone for company.
Hardly anything. A swallow got into the Hall of Echoes and sang along with the harps for a while. It wasn't very good. We clapped anyway.
No real news. Someone swore the clouds were going backwards this morning. They weren't. We all watched for an hour, to be sure.
heart.partner: {partner} and I have shared a nest for years, and we still fly the Evensong side by side. I could find {partner} in the ring with my eyes shut. By the humming.
My {spouse}? {partner}. The kindest pair of veils in {village}. When mine tore in a storm, {partner} held it closed all the way home.
{partner} hums in their sleep. Every night. I used to think it was annoying. Now I can't sleep without it.
I fell for {partner} at a Lengthening. Not ours, someone else's. I watched {partner} watching the new veils go up and thought: I'd like to be looked at like that.
{partner} brings me the first peach of every morning. Never says a word, just leaves it on the cushion. I haven't picked my own in years.
We tied our veils together at the Veil Court, {partner} and I, with the harps playing. The knot slipped at once and everyone cheered. Too tight a knot can't fly, they say.
My {spouse} is {partner}, and that's the best thing about me. Don't tell {partner} I said so. It'll go straight to their veils.
Love? It's {partner} flying beside me on a long day, saying nothing. That's it. That's all it is. That's everything.
{partner} and I argue about the winds. I'm for Aure; {partner} says Sefa. We've been at it for years. It's the best argument I've ever had.
When I'm low, {partner} sings me the silly verse of the Evensong until I laugh. It takes about four goes. {partner} is very patient.
A secret: I still get a flutter when {partner} comes home at dusk. All these dawns, and still. Isn't that something?
{partner} is braver than me. In a storm once, {partner} flew out to bring the children home while I kept the nest humming. I'll never forget it.
My {spouse}, {partner}, can't hold a tune. Not one note. I married {partner} anyway. That's how you know it's love, up here.
Every Cirri needs someone to untangle their veils after a long flight. Mine is {partner}. Gentle hands. A little slow on purpose, I think.
{partner} and I met on the bridge to the Cloud Garden, feeding the same koi from either side. That koi got very fat that month.
I think I'd go grounded without {partner}. Not truly. But in the heart. You know.
Our nest is small, but {partner} fills it. With humming, with laughing, with peach stones. Mostly peach stones.
Did you know {partner} courted me with a Sky Scale? Searched the koi pool for days. Found one in a skywood, of all places. Koi are mysterious.
Ask {partner} about me and you'll get a very long answer. Ask me about {partner} and I'll just go pink. There. I've gone pink.
When we're old and our veils are thin, {partner} and I are going to drift out to a Wind Shrine and listen to the harps all day. We've planned it. It's a good plan.
{partner} and I fly home the long way every evening, right round the rim. It adds a light breeze to the trip. Neither of us has ever once suggested the short way.
Before {partner}, I thought the sky was enough. It was a great deal. It wasn't enough.
My {spouse} keeps every peach stone I've ever given them in a little bowl. Every one. {partner} says it's a calendar. I say it's a lot of peach stones.
heart.single: No one yet. The sky's wide; I'm in no hurry. Someone will fly alongside one day and simply keep flying.
Me? Nobody. A nest for one, a cushion for one, a whole sky for one. Some evenings it's plenty. Some evenings it's a lot of sky.
Not yet. The weavers keep asking when they'll get to weave a nest-hanging for me. I keep telling them: weave slowly.
Love? I'm waiting for the right wind. Everyone says you know it when you feel it. Like a whale passing: you hear it in your chest before you see it.
Nobody special. The koi love me, if that counts. They seem to think it does. I'm less sure.
I'm on my own, and that's all right. It's a lot of sky for one, but I've learned to fill it. With songs, mostly.
No one. I tell myself it's because I'm too busy. Then I fly past the couples at dusk and I'm not busy at all.
Love is a bit like weather, isn't it? You can read the signs all you like. It still turns up when it wants.
Anyone special? Not yet. But there's a nest-shaped space beside mine, if you see what I mean. I keep it tidy.
I tried courting once. I sang outside a nest at dawn, very bravely. It was the wrong nest. They were very kind about it.
I'm too fond of flying far to stay put in one nest. Maybe one day someone will fly far with me. That's the dream: someone restless enough.
Not yet. I'm still learning to love my own company. It's going well. I'm very charming, it turns out.
There's no one. Don't look sad for me. Sky peaches, good friends, the Evensong. My heart is full. It just isn't full of one person.
Love? I think about it. Who'll hum me back to sleep when I'm old. Then I think: someone will. Someone always does, up here.
Not yet, and that's fine. The best things up here come slowly: peaches, veils, friends. Love's probably one of the slow ones.
No one. I'm a bit shy about it, to tell the truth. Every time someone nice flies near, my veils go stiff and I talk about the weather.
No sweetheart for me. I always fall for the ones who fly off: walkers, travellers, whales. I've a weakness for anything that's leaving.
Have you got someone, {player}? Down there? I hope so. Somebody to come home to, at the bottom of all those stairs.
Nobody. But the old ones say love comes on Vell, the evening wind, the one that carries songs. So I sing at dusk. Just in case Vell's listening.
Not yet. I'm saving my best Sky Scale for whoever it turns out to be. It's in a little pouch by the cushion. Waiting. Same as me.
Nobody, and my parents remind me of it at every Evensong. 'Look, so-and-so's on their own.' I look. I wave. I go back to singing.
I had someone once. We flew different ways in the end. No harm in it; the sky's like that. I still hum our tune sometimes, on quiet days.
Is there anyone? No. Is there anyone you'd recommend, walker? I'm only half joking. A third joking.
heart.crush: Special? N-no. Well. There's {crush}. Don't say anything! {crush} just has the loveliest humming in {village}, that's all. That's all it is.
Can I tell you something? I'm sweet on {crush}. I've been feeding the koi at the same time every morning so I'm there when {crush} is.
{crush}... oh, did I say that out loud? Forget it. Fly off. No, wait, come back. Do you think {crush} likes me? Even a little?
I flew into the Lantern Spire yesterday. Because {crush} waved at me. Don't laugh. All right, laugh a little.
Every Evensong I end up next to {crush} in the ring. It's an accident. Every time. Very lucky accidents.
I've been trying to write a song for {crush}. I have the first line. It's {crush}'s name. I'm stuck on the second.
There's someone. {crush}. When {crush} flies past, my veils go all fluttery and I forget the names of the winds. All four.
Don't tell, but I braided a bit of gold into my veil-tips this week. In case {crush} noticed. {crush} didn't. I'll try rose next.
{crush} said my veils looked nice. Three days ago. I've been very careful with them since. I've hardly flown.
Is it silly to be sweet on someone who doesn't know? I'll tell {crush} one day. One windy day, so the words blow away if they come out wrong.
Shh. {crush} is just over there. Don't look! ...You looked. Now {crush} is looking. Oh, sky.
My heart has gone and flown off after {crush}, and I can't call it back. It doesn't listen. Hearts are worse than koi.
I asked the windkeeper which wind is best for courting. Vell, they said. So on the next Vell day I'll... say hello to {crush}. Properly. That's the plan.
{crush} likes glow berries. I know that. I don't know why I know that. I just happen to have picked some. They're in my sash.
You know {crush}? What do you think of {crush}? No reason. I'm asking for a koi.
When {crush} sings at the Evensong, I forget my part. Every time. The harpists have stopped asking why.
{crush} borrowed my veil-comb once and gave it back the next day. I haven't used it since. Is that strange? That's strange.
heart.parent: {child} is the light of my nest. Yesterday {child} asked me where the sky ends. I said it doesn't. {child} said, then where does it go? I'm still thinking.
My little {child} did a loop today! A whole one! Then flew straight into a peach tree. But a whole loop first.
I worry about {child} near the rim. All Cirri parents do. Those little veils are so short, and the ground's so far. I know {child} will be fine. I still worry.
{child} has started asking about walkers. Everything about walkers. Your feet, your stairs, your fires. I think {child} is going to be trouble. The good kind.
Every night I hum {child} to sleep, and every night {child} hums back, half a note behind, until we're both asleep. The best part of my day.
Being {child}'s parent is like holding a wind harp in a gale. Beautiful noise, all the time, and you can't put it down.
I already dream about {child}'s Lengthening. The long veils, the whole village watching. I'll cry. I'm practically crying now. Look away.
{child} goes shy with walkers, then asks about you after you've gone. Every time. 'Where's the walker now? Do walkers dream about falling?'
{child} brought me a flower from the Cloud Garden this morning. Pulled it up by the roots. The gardeners weren't pleased. I was.
Love? It's {child} curled over the cushion, veils tangled up in mine, breathing little puffs. I didn't know I could love like that.
{child} keeps a Sky Scale under the cushion for good dreams. It works, {child} says. I keep one too. Don't tell {child}. We're a family of believers.
{child} is going to be a harpist. Or a windkeeper. Or a whale. That last one was this morning. We're keeping our options open.
When {child} was born the whole village sang. I didn't. I couldn't. I just held on to {child} and listened to everyone singing for us.
{child} laughs exactly like {partner}. It catches me every time, right under the ribs.
I'm teaching {child} the Evensong. {child} knows all the words. In the wrong order. It's my favourite version now.
One day {child} will fly off, the way young ones do. I'll wave from the rim. Then I'll follow a little way. Then I'll stop. I think.
{child} is braver than I ever was. Flew right up to an Old Singer and said hello. The whale said nothing. {child} has decided it was shy.
If you see {child} near the edge, would you call out? Not to scold. Just so {child} knows someone's looking. That's all a little one needs.
{child} asked why we never land. I said: because the sky would miss us. {child} thought about it and said, 'Then the ground must be lonely.'
