Some days {child} wears me out completely. Then {child} falls asleep mid-sentence, veils drifting, and I'd do every second of it again.
{child} wanted to know what the ground smells like. Rain and roots, I'm told, I said. {child} has been sniffing everything since. Including me.
I've mended {child}'s veils three times this week. Three! Tumbling about in the skywoods. I'm not cross. I'm a little proud. Mostly cross.
{child} said 'grounded' at supper, just to see. The whole nest went quiet. Now {child} whispers it, very solemnly, like the worst word in the sky. Which it is.
mention.partner: {partner} would tell you I talk too much. {partner} would be right.
Speaking of which, {partner} owes me a peach. Don't let {partner} tell you otherwise.
{partner} has been humming the same tune since dawn. Now I'm humming it. It's catching.
If you see {partner}, say I'm keeping the warm side of the nest.
{partner} found a Sky Scale this morning and gave it straight to me. Can you tell? I'm glowing a bit.
{partner} flew home late again last night. Something about a whale. It's always something about a whale.
My {spouse}, {partner}, says hello. Well, {partner} would, if {partner} were here.
{partner} is in one of those moods where everything is very funny. I've been laughing since the bell.
Oh, and {partner} got tangled in the skywoods again. Second time this week. I keep the veil-comb handy.
{partner} thinks you're very interesting. Don't let it go to your head.
I left {partner} asleep this morning, curled up like a little cloud. I couldn't bear to wake them.
{partner} is learning the harp. Slowly. Very slowly. The whole nest knows every wrong note.
{partner} says Borre's coming soon. {partner} can smell a storm a day off. It's uncanny.
Have you met {partner}? You'd like {partner}. Everyone does. It's a bit maddening.
{partner} made me promise to be home for the Evensong. As if I'd miss it.
mention.child: {child} wants to know if you've any more walker stories. I said I'd ask.
{child} is out practising loops again. You can hear the giggling from here.
Don't tell {child}, but I'm saving the ripest peach for after the Evensong.
{child} drew a walker in the cloud yesterday. It had very big feet. Was that you?
{child} lost a ribbon off one veil. If you see a little rose ribbon, it's ours.
{child} is sure the koi know everyone's names. I've stopped arguing.
{child} learned a new word from a walker: 'stairs'. Says it all day. Stairs, stairs, stairs.
{child} has been following the windkeeper about. I think we've a windkeeper in the making.
{child} asked if you'd come to the Evensong. I said walkers are always welcome. {child} squealed.
If you hear singing from the Cloud Garden, that's {child}, serenading the peach trees. Badly.
{child} slept right through the dawn bell. Takes after me.
{child} has a wobbly tooth and is very proud of it. Ask to see it, if you've a moment.
{child} wants to visit the ground one day. I've said: when your veils are long. That gives me years.
{child} keeps asking why walkers don't float. I said walkers are too full of supper. Is that right?
{child} saved you a glow berry. It's a bit squashed. It's the thought.
mention.friend: {friend} and I are flying out to the Wind Shrine tomorrow. Shame you can't come. Or can you? You walkers surprise me.
{friend} says you're the most interesting walker we've ever had. I said we've only had a few. {friend} said: still.
{friend} still owes me for the race round the Spire. Lost by a veil's length and won't admit it.
{friend} told me a joke at breakfast and I'm still laughing. Something about a koi and a lantern. I've forgotten it. Still funny.
If you want the best peaches, ask {friend}. {friend} knows every tree in the Cloud Garden by name.
{friend} and I have been friends since our veils were short. We'll be friends when they're thin.
{friend} has been low lately. If you pass by, say something kind. It goes a long way up here.
I'm meeting {friend} at the koi pool later. We just float there. It's the best hour of the day.
{friend} saw a whale yesterday and didn't tell anyone till this morning. I'm still cross about it.
{friend} and I wrote a verse for the Evensong once. It was terrible. They sang it anyway. That's {village} for you.
{friend} would like you, I think. {friend} likes anyone who asks questions.
{friend} lent me a veil-comb and I've lost it. Please don't mention it if you see {friend}.
{friend} swears the north wind talks. Not sings. Talks. I've never heard it. I've never stopped listening, either.
Tell {friend} I said fair wind, if you see them. I've been too busy to say it myself.
{friend} and I have a secret loop we do over the Bell Pagoda. You'd need veils to understand.
{friend} keeps asking about you. Where you sleep, what you eat, whether walkers dream. I said: ask yourself.
{friend} and I aren't speaking today. Over a peach. It'll pass by dusk. It always does.
mention.coworker: {coworker} and I have been sharing the work today. Well, I've been working. {coworker} has been humming.
{coworker} is better at this than me. Don't tell {coworker} I said that.
{coworker} taught me everything I know about the job. And a few things I didn't want to know.
{coworker} and I have a bet on over who finishes first today. Loser brings the peaches.
If I'm not at my spot, ask {coworker}. {coworker} always knows where I've drifted off to.
{coworker} keeps tidying my things. I keep untidying them. It's a system.
{coworker} was in at dawn today, before me. First time ever. I'm a little worried.
Between {coworker} and me the work gets done. Between {coworker}, me and a few peaches, it gets done faster.
{coworker} says I'm too slow. I say {coworker} is too fast. Somewhere between us is the right speed.
{coworker} has been showing me a new trick of the trade. I'll pretend I thought of it, later.
{coworker} sings while we work. Every day, the same song. I know all the words now, against my will.
{coworker} took the morning off to see a whale. I'm doing two jobs today. I'm not bitter. Much.
mention.neighbour: {neighbour} has been humming at the koi again. They seem to like it. The koi, I mean.
Have you met {neighbour}? Always flying about with a peach in each hand.
{neighbour} borrowed my good stole and hasn't brought it back. I'm being patient. Loudly.
{neighbour} says a whale's coming soon. {neighbour} says that every week. One week {neighbour} will be right.
{neighbour} was up before the bell today, sweeping loose cloud off the bridges. Nobody asked. Very good of them.
If you hear laughing from the next nest, that's {neighbour}. {neighbour} laughs in their sleep.
{neighbour} grows the sweetest berries on the islet. Don't ask how. You'll be there all day.
{neighbour} has hung wind chimes from every eave on the islet. Lovely. Very loud. Lovely.
{neighbour} has never once missed the Evensong. Not once. Not even with a sniffle.
I think {neighbour} has taken a liking to you. {neighbour} asked if the walker was coming back.
{neighbour} and I quarrelled over whose turn it was to feed the koi. The koi ate twice. Everyone wins.
{neighbour} keeps a tally of every walker who comes up the Wind Stone. You're on it, I'd bet.
{neighbour} has been trying to teach a swallow the Evensong. It's going about as well as you'd think.
{neighbour} dozed off mid-flight over the Veil Court yesterday. Just drifted for a while. We let them.
Have you seen {neighbour}'s veils? Freshly mended. {neighbour} won't say how they got torn.
{neighbour} leaves a lantern lit for anyone flying home late. Nobody asked. Everyone's glad.
{neighbour} has been trying to whistle like a walker for a month. Nothing comes out but wind. Very determined wind.
greet.dawn: Fair wind! You've caught me with dew still beaded on my veils.
Up before the bell? Even the bellkeeper's still rubbing their eyes.
Dawn, and a walker on the bridge. That's two lovely things before breakfast.
Look down there: the whole cloud-sea's gone pink. Every morning, and it still takes my breath.
Hello! The weavers are out combing cirrus. It has to be done before the sun warms it, they say.
Oh, good dawn. I've only just uncurled, so forgive the crooked veil.
An early riser! I'd heard walkers sleep half the day away, and flat on the ground, too.
You're here for first light? Wise. It never lasts, and it never comes the same twice.
Mmm, hello. I'm still more nest than Cirri at this hour.
Good dawn, {player}. See the gold creeping along the undersides of the clouds?
The koi are rising for their first nibble and so am I. Peach? No? More for me.
Morning's barely a thread yet, and here you are. Hello!
Dew on the bridges, dew on the chimes, dew on me. Mind your footing, walker.
Fair wind! The bell's just rung me out of my nest. Did you hear it from the dock?
So early! Even {wind} hasn't decided which way to blow yet.
Breakfast up here is a peach eaten upside down, in case you wondered how we do mornings. Hello!
Dawn's the best hour to fly. The air is thin and sweet, like drinking light.
A good dawn to you! The stars are going out one by one, like lanterns being put away.
greet.morning: The village is properly awake now. Hear the harps tuning? Good morning!
Morning, walker. You've the look of someone with somewhere to be.
Hello! I've already flown round the Cloud Garden twice. Mornings make my veils itch to go.
Fair wind this morning! The bridges are warming and the lanterns are all asleep.
A morning visitor, the best kind: awake, and not yet tired of us.
Hello there! The market's opening and the gossip's already flown round twice.
Just in time! Watch the clouds below roll over, like sleepers turning in their nests. Good morning.
Good morning, {player}! Did the Wind Stone treat you gently on the way up?
Is it morning already? I'd swear I only blinked after the dawn bell.
Look, the islands' shadows are drifting over the land below. I like to guess whose is whose.
Every walker I meet carries the smell of grass up with them. Good morning!
There's a breeze off the Loom House that smells of fresh-combed cloud. Can you smell it?
Mornings are for flying fast and talking faster, so forgive me if I bob about. Hello!
Nothing much has happened yet today, which is my favourite kind of news. Good morning.
Ah, you're up and about! Walkers in the morning always look so purposeful.
Morning, morning! Two peaches eaten and a quarrel with a swift already. What a day.
Hello! The dew's dried and the day's fully woven. What shall we do with it?
Morning light through veilcloth is the softest light there is. Stand under an awning and see!
greet.noon: Midday! The sun's straight overhead, and my shadow's a tiny speck on the clouds below.
Hello! Noon's when the sky peaches warm right through. The whole village smells of them.
Fair wind at noon! High sun, high spirits, high village. Lots of highs today.
Ah, hello! I was just thinking about lunch. A peach, a little honey, a handful of blossoms.
Noon already? The morning flew. Well, of course it did; everything here does.
The koi have all gone to the bottom of the pool, out of the sun. Clever fish. Hello!
Do the bridges go warm under walkers' feet at this hour? I've always wondered.
Good day! The sun's at the top of the sky, and so are we, nearly.
Hello, {player}! Come under the awning a while. Even the sky gets hot at noon.
Half the village is dozing on the warm air. Shh. Or don't; they won't wake. Good day.
Noon's the stillest hour; the harps barely hum. Hello, though!
Have you eaten? If you've been climbing about all morning, you must be famished. Walkers always are.
Good noon! Is that a thing walkers say? It should be.
My veils have dried out and so has my wit. Ah, the middle of the day. Hello!
Sun on the gilded roofs at this hour makes the whole village blink. Hello there!
There you are! Lunch, then talk, or talk, then lunch? I can manage both at once.
Look how the clouds below have shrunk! The sun's been nibbling at them since dawn.
Fair wind! Noon light's so clear, I can count the rooftops of a bell-village far below.
greet.afternoon: Good afternoon! The day's gone slow and golden, like honey off the comb.
This is the lazy part of the day. Even the bell looks sleepy. Hello!
Afternoon, walker. The clouds below have started piling up into towers. Rain somewhere, later.
Work's done, peaches are picked, and I'm all yours till the Evensong. Hello!
Hello there. Afternoons drift. So do I, rather.
The light's leaning sideways through the veilcloth now. My favourite light. Good afternoon!
Children all over the Veil Court, chasing each other's veils! Mind your head, walker.
Ah, hello! I've been napping in a warm updraft. Don't tell anyone; I have a reputation.
Afternoon, {player}. The islands' shadows are stretching out long across the clouds.
Weavers folding up, gardeners watering: the village is winding down. Hello!
I was just watching the swallows far below, all hurrying home early. Afternoon!
A visitor in the long part of the day. Stay; the afternoon has room for two.
There's still time before dusk for a good, long, pointless chat. My favourite kind!
Listen: the harps are already tuning for the evening, humming low. Hello!
You've the look of a walker who's climbed something. Rest your feet a while.
If you're after peaches, the high branches have the ripest. I could fetch you one.
Afternoons in {village} smell of warm skywood and koi water. Good afternoon!
The sun's sinking, but slowly. It likes the view from up here as much as we do.
greet.evening: The lamplighter's going bridge to bridge. Watch the lanterns wake, one by one. Good evening!
Evening, walker. Hear the harps? The Evensong's gathering over the Veil Court.
Hello! The clouds below have gone rose and violet, like a veil-tip the size of the world.
Ah, dusk. My favourite hour to meet someone: everyone's softer at dusk.
The bell's rung and the day's nearly sung down. Stay for the last of it.
Watch the sun slip under the cloud-sea. It'll be dark on the ground long before it's dark up here.
Evening, {player}! You've come at the singing hour. Lucky walker.
Swallows to bed, moths awake. Hello, before it's properly dark!
Good evening. My throat's been humming all afternoon, ready for the Evensong.
Evening already? I spent the whole day flying and still have things to tell you.
Smell that? Warm skywood and the first night blossoms. That's evening in a sky village.
The first star's out, just over the Lantern Spire. Walkers make wishes on them, I've heard. Do you?
Hello. The day's work is folded away and the night hasn't started. This is the in-between.
Vell carries songs at this hour, they say. Listen hard and you'll hear three villages at once.
You'll want to be near a lantern before long, walker. The night-moths come out after dark.
Everything's going gold, then rose, then blue. Watch with me a moment?
Dusk already! The children are being called in from every bridge. Hello, quickly!
Good evening. The village is quiet the way a breath is quiet, just before a song.
greet.night: Out after dark? Stay near the lanterns, walker. The night-moths have sharp manners.
Oh! Hello. I was just flying home; my nest's calling me.
The stars are thick tonight, like dew on dark cloth. Hello, night walker.
Hello, softly. Half the village is already curled up asleep.
It's dark, {player}. Are you sure your feet know where the bridge ends?
The lanterns make little islands of light. Walk from one to the next and you'll be fine.
Good night to you. I was nearly in my nest, but a walker's worth staying up for.
Everything's hushed at night up here. Even the wind harps only whisper.
Shh! The little ones have only just stopped humming. Hello, in a whisper.
I'd not go down the Wind Stone till morning, walker. The ground's full of dark at night.
Stars above us, and the lights of the bell-villages far below. We're the middle of it all.
I can't make out your face in this light. You sound friendly, at least. Hello!
Walkers sleep lying on their cushions, I'm told. Squashed flat! How do you bear it?
The nights are always chill this high. Have you something warm to wrap up in?
Oh, it's you! In the dark you looked like a night-moth for a moment. Much less wing.
Follow the bridge lanterns. They all lead to somebody's nest, and every nest is friendly.
Late for a walker, isn't it? You need so much sleep. Or is that just a story?
Night's come up from the cloud-sea like a tide. Keep to the lit paths, walker.
greet.late: Goodness, it's the deep of the night! Is something wrong down below?
Hello? It's so late even the stars look sleepy.
You're awake at this hour too? My veils were restless. They dream of flying, you know.
Oh! You gave me such a start. Nobody comes calling after midnight.
Shh. If {neighbour} wakes, we'll both hear about it at breakfast.
Can't sleep either? Either the moon's too bright or my thoughts are too loud.
Have you slept at all lately, walker? The night-moths come for walkers who don't.
It's the hush of the night, the hour nobody owns. Hello, quietly.
I came out to see to a flickering lantern. It was a moth. Just a moth, the little kind.
A midnight visitor! You'd better have a good story, walker.
So late the cloud-sea's gone black. Only the stars to see by. Hello, all the same.
Sometimes, at this hour, you can hear the Old Singers far off. A low sort of humming. Listen.
Up at this hour, {player}? Just the two of us and the stars, then.
I couldn't settle: my cushion's gone lumpy and the air's too still. Still air makes me uneasy.
Is it morning yet? No? Then why are we both awake?
The middle of the night is no time for visiting, but... fair wind, I suppose.
Everything's asleep but us and the great lantern. Even the koi.
Walkers keep strange hours. Come under the lantern where I can see you.
greet.band.stranger: A walker! Up the Wind Stone, were you? Hello! I'm {name}.
Oh, a new face. And new feet! Welcome to {village}.
Hello, stranger. Don't mind me staring; we don't see many walkers up here.
Fair wind, traveller! You came all that way up just to see us? How lovely.
I'm {name}, the {job}. And you're a walker, plainly. Have you a name as well?
Welcome, welcome. The Courtesy says I must make you feel at home. Do you? Be honest.
A visitor! Mind the edges. You haven't any veils, I notice.
Are you the walker everyone's been whispering about? Or another one? Are there many of you?
Oh! Hello. I don't quite know how to talk to someone who stands. Shall I come lower?
Welcome to {village}, stranger. We're a small sky, but a warm one.
Your boots are very loud on the bridge. Not a complaint! Just astonishing.
A stranger with heavy feet and a curious face. Fair wind to you.
Come to trade, or to stare? Both are allowed. We stare too.
Is it true you sleep lying flat on the ground? Sorry. Hello first. Then that.
Back again, walker? You must like heights more than you let on.
Hello, {player}... that's your name, isn't it? Walkers' names travel faster than walkers do.
If anything here frightens you, it's only the height. Everyone gets used to it.
You look a bit windswept. Everyone does, the first few times. Hello!
greet.band.acquaintance: Oh, it's you again! The walker from the Wind Stone. Hello!
Fair wind, {player}. Back for more sky?
I told {friend} about you. They didn't believe a walker would come back twice.
My favourite walker! Well, one of two. The other fell asleep on a bridge and we had to wake them.
You came back! I wasn't sure you would. Most walkers find us a little dizzying.
Hello again. Your face is getting familiar. Your feet are still a wonder.
You remembered where we are! The clouds wander, but we mostly stay put.
I've been saving up questions for you, walker. Fair warning.
Oh, good, it's you. I was hoping for someone to talk to who isn't a koi.
Back already? The bridges have nearly learned the sound of your step.
You're starting to walk like you know the place. That's a compliment, walker.
Ah, hello again. Did you sleep well, flat as you do?
There you are! I wondered when the Wind Stone would bring you up next.
The village has decided you're harmless. Mostly. I agreed.
A familiar face! We're past "who are you" and onto "how are you." So: how are you?
I nearly didn't recognise you without the startled look. Hello!
You again, and smiling. Good. The sky's better with a few regulars.
I'm still learning walker manners. Is it rude to ask where you've been?
greet.band.friend: {player}! Fair wind, friend. I was hoping you'd drift by.
Oh, good. The day's just improved. Hello, friend!
I kept a peach aside in case you came. I ate it at noon, but I kept it until then.
Fair wind, friend! You're a welcome gust on a still day.
My veils always lift a little when you turn up. Hello, you.
Come closer, I've news. Some of it's even true.
Friend walker! I was just telling {neighbour} how much better your boots sound on the bridges these days.
You came! Good. It's been a dull, walkerless sort of day till now.
Stand with me a while. Walkers love standing, I know. It's your best thing.
There you are. I had a feeling; {wind} was blowing in from your side of the world.
Anything to tell? Anything at all? I'm starved for ground news.
I saw you on the bridge and flew straight over. Hello!
Ah, my friend from below. How are those brave feet of yours?
Everyone in {village} knows your face now. They ask after you when you're gone.
Just the walker I wanted! Well, the only walker. But still the one I wanted.
You look well. Windswept, but well. Hello, friend.
It's good to see you. Truly. Hello.
greet.band.close: There you are, {player}! The day felt half woven without you.
My dear walker! Let me look at you. Still in one piece? Good.
I'm so glad you came. I've been saving up a whole sky of things to tell you.
My heart did a loop when I spotted you. Hello, dear friend.
Fair wind, fair wind! You always come just when I'm hoping you will.
The wind's been whispering you'd visit today. It was right. Come closer!
Ah, there's my favourite walker in all the world below.
Everything's lighter when you're about. Hello, you.
My friend! I dreamed of you last night. You were flying, badly. It was wonderful.
Tell me everything. Leave nothing out, not even the dull bits.
You came! I said to {partner} only today, I've a feeling about this one.
Dear walker, fair wind. My veils have fidgeted all day; now I know why.
I've been looking for your face in every walker-shaped shadow. Hello!
Hello, friend of my heart. You look tired. Stay and be looked after a while.
You're here! Good. I'd started to worry the ground had kept you.
Come, hover beside me. Stand, I mean. You'd think I'd remember by now.
Nobody laughs at my jokes the way you do. Others laugh, but not the same. Hello, dear one.
Oh, you. Whatever kind of day it's been, it just got better.
greet.band.best: My walker, my Veil-Kin, my dear! Fair wind, fair wind.
You're home. I mean it: anywhere in {village}, you're home.
{player}! Now the sky's whole again. Hello, dearest.
Hello, family. Don't make that face. You are, and that's settled.
Oh, my heart. Come here. I'd wrap a veil round you if you'd let me.
I leave a lantern lit at my nest for you every night, in case you ever need it.
Every dawn I count, and every dawn I hope you're in it.
The whole village knows I've a soft spot for you. I've stopped pretending otherwise.
Fair wind, my own. Come close and tell me how your feet are. And your heart.
You came back to me. You always do, and I'm glad every time as if it's the first.
The Courtesy says welcome a walker. It says nothing about loving one, so I made my own rule.
There you are, there you are. Everything in me went high the moment I saw you.
One sky, you and I. Hello, dearest walker.
I've kept a spare cushion in my nest for you. You'd sleep on it all wrong, but still.
Come here and let me fuss. That's what family's for.
{partner} says I light up like the Lantern Spire when you visit. They're right.
If you ever fell, I'd be the first one diving. You know that, don't you?
Fair wind, heart of mine. Stay as long as the sky lets you.
greet.personality.dreamer: I was just wondering how far down the ground goes, past the dirt. All the way to... somewhere. Sorry. Hello.
Fair wind. Have you noticed that clouds look like they're thinking? I was thinking with them.
Hello... I was counting the islands' shadows and lost count at a beautiful one.
You've come from below, where the rain lands. What does it sound like, landing?
Do you think the stars are other villages, very far up? I like to think they sing too.
Oh! I was half a dream away. Stay a moment, walker; I'm nearly back.
The horizon's the only place the sky and the ground ever touch. I'd like to see it up close one day.
There's a cloud down there shaped exactly like a sigh. Can you see it? No... it's gone now.
You rose all that way through the sky. What did it feel like? Was it like waking?
Hello, {player}. I was listening to the wind harps and forgot which of us was humming.
Do you think the moon gets lonely? No village to keep it company, all that way up. Oh, hello.
Mm? Sorry, I was somewhere over the edge of the world. It's lovely there, I think.
greet.personality.merry: Ha! A walker! Watch, watch: a loop, just for you. There. Hello!
Fair wind! Race you to the Bell Pagoda. Oh, you'd lose. Never mind!
You've caught me in a good mood. I'm always in a good mood, so that was easy.
Look who's walked in! Did you bring a joke? I've three, and they're all about walkers.
There you are! I bet {friend} a peach you'd come today. Thank you for the peach.
Quick, pull a face at {neighbour} while they're not looking. No? Spoilsport. Fair wind!
Ah ha, a visitor! I'm terrible at hiding my delight, so I won't even try.
Clump, clump, clump down the bridge! I heard you long before I saw you. Hello!
I've been laughing all day and I can't remember why. Help me find it again.
Fair wind, {player}! A game? You stand there and I'll fly circles round you. You win if you don't get dizzy.
Oh, good, company! The koi have stopped laughing at my jokes.
You look like someone who needs cheering. No? Then I'll cheer you anyway.
greet.personality.gentle: Hello, dear. Are you warm enough? The wind's sharper up here than walkers expect.
Fair wind. You look a little tired. Rest your feet a moment; there's no hurry.
I'm glad you came up. Did the Wind Stone set you down gently?
Come in out of the wind, if you like. I'll keep it off you with my veils.
Have you eaten, walker? There's always a peach for a guest.
Mind the bridge edge, won't you? I worry about walkers near edges.
Ah, you. It's nice to see a kind face. Kinder still, up close.
Take your time. I'm in no hurry, and the sky isn't either.
Oh, hello, {player}. Your cheeks are wind-pinched. Let me hover on the windward side.
Whatever kind of day it's been down below, it's quieter up here. Stay a while.
Breathe slowly, dear walker. The air's thin this high, and you're not used to it.
A gentle wind to you. The old ones used to say that instead of hello. I like it better.
greet.personality.shy: Fair wind... if that's all right to say to a walker.
Oh, h... hello. Sorry. I'm not good at the first part.
You. Hello. I'll just... stay a little over here, if you don't mind.
I wasn't hiding. Well. A little.
Fair wind. You don't have to talk much. I won't either.
Um. Hello, {player}. I remembered your name. Is that strange?
A walker... hello. You're very... solid.
My veils go pink at the tips when I'm nervous. They're always pink at the tips. Never mind.
Ah. It's nice you came over. I think. Yes. Nice.
I was going to say something clever, and then you were here.
Hello. I'll get used to you. Give me a few dawns.
greet.personality.proud: Fair wind, walker. You stand in {village}, the finest village in the high sky. Do look around.
Ah, a visitor. You'll find our bridges the best-made in any sky. Built for you, I might add.
You may admire the veils; everyone does. They're woven right here, you know.
A walker, come all the way up to us! Well, of course you did. Who wouldn't?
Mind your boots on the gilded trim. It's older than your grandparents.
We greet the wind before we greet guests. You came a close second today.
Have you heard our Evensong? No? Then you haven't heard singing yet.
Ah, {player}. Your manners are improving. For a walker, I mean that warmly.
Every bridge, every lantern, every door here is a courtesy to you. I hope you notice.
These veils came off the best loom in {village}. You may look closer, if you like.
Our harps are tuned to the wind each morning. Down below, do your bells tune themselves?
Stand up straight; you're in the high sky now. There, much better. Hello.
greet.personality.restless: Don't mind me circling. If I stop moving I'll float off in a sulk. Hello!
Fair wind! Where've you been? Further than here? Tell me, tell me.
You've seen the world from the bottom. I want to see all of it from the top.
I was about to fly off somewhere, anywhere. You'll do instead, for now.
Fair wind, {player}. Have you been past the mountains? What's past the mountains?
{village}'s lovely, but it's the same lovely every day. Tell me something new.
I flew three islands out today and it still wasn't far enough.
You've dust on your boots from somewhere. Where? Hello, by the way.
The horizon's been calling all day. Talk loudly, or I might answer it.
Do you ever just keep going, walker? Past the edge of every map? I dream of it.
Quick: one story from far away, and then I'll let you go.
There's a whole sky out there no Cirri has sung in. Sorry. Hello. I get carried away. Literally.
greet.personality.busy: Hello! Yes, I see you, just a moment, hold that thought. Right. Hello!
Fair wind! Walking and talking? I'll fly and talk. Keep up.
Mind the basket. And the thread. And that bit of cloud. Hello!
Ah, {player}, good. One moment. Two. There. What is it?
I've four things to do and you've just become the fifth. A nice fifth.
Fair wind, fair wind. Can't stop long; the day's running ahead of me again.
Hand me... no, you can't reach. Never mind. Hello!
Oh, a walker with both hands free. Just looking. Hello.
If I seem distracted, it's because I am. Very glad you came, though.
Talk quickly, I'll listen quickly, and we'll both be home before dusk.
Mind the bridge, mind the peaches, mind me: I'm everywhere at once today.
Nearly finished. Nearly. That's a fib, but hello.
greet.personality.wise: Fair wind, walker. The old ones said a guest is the wind's own gift. Let's see what it's brought.
Keep your veil whole and your heart light, we say. You've no veil, so your heart must do double.
A walker on the high bridges. Long ago, that would have been a story told for a year.
Sit with an old soul a while. Stand, rather. The words are the same.
Hello, {player}. I've seen many dawns. Few of them brought someone as curious as you.
The first windkeepers set the Wind Stone for you, you know. Not you exactly. But you.
The sky is wide enough for everyone, as the saying goes. Even for heavy feet.
Stillness first, then talk. There. Fair wind.
A light wind carries far; a light word, further. So, a light word: welcome.
I was remembering a story about the first walker who ever came up. I'll tell it you someday.
You look like someone with a question. The old ones say those are the best guests.
Never trust a still day, we say. You've stirred this one nicely.
greet.personality.curious: A walker! What does the ground feel like? Is it warm? Does it move?
Fair wind! Can I ask you something? How do you know which foot goes first?
What's that on your feet? Do they come off? Do your feet come off?
Is it true walkers swim? On purpose? In water?
Hello, {player}! Tell me one thing about the ground I don't know. Just one. Then maybe nine more.
When you fall over, does the ground catch you every time?
Show me how you climb stairs. Slowly. I want to understand.
How many walkers are there? Do you all know each other?
What do walkers dream about? Falling? Or the opposite?
Is it loud down there, under the clouds? I imagine it's very loud.
Hello, hello! I've a list of questions. It's a long list. You don't mind lists?
Why do walkers always look down when they walk? Is the ground very interesting?
greet.routine.work: Hands full, as you see. A {job}'s work is never quite done. Hello!
Fair wind! Mind where you step; I've half a day's work spread round me.
Come and watch, if you like. Walkers always find our work so strange.
A visitor at the work hour. Talk away; I'll keep my hands busy and my ears open.
You've caught me mid-task, walker. It'll keep. Most things keep, up here.
Do walkers work all day too? You must. You look like you do.
I was just getting the rhythm of it. Never mind, the rhythm will wait. Hello.
Being the {job} is a good life. Busy, but good. What's yours?
Work goes faster with company. Or slower, but nicer.
Ah, {player}. Perfect timing: I needed a reason to stop and stretch my veils.
You'll forgive me if I keep at it while we talk? The wind waits for nobody.
Everyone in {village} has their part, and this is mine. What's your part, walker?
greet.routine.gather: Come and join us! Half of {village} is hovering about the Veil Court.
Fair wind! We were just chatting over the court. Walkers welcome, always.
A walker in the gathering! Everyone's going to want a look at you.
The court's the heart of the village. Best place to meet anyone. Hello!
You found us. When the work's done, the court fills up like a cloud fills with rain.
We've been arguing about which wind is kindest. Want to take a side?
Don't mind the crowd. They only stare because they like you. Mostly.
Hello, {player}! Come stand in the middle where everyone can see you.
Oh, hello! I was just telling {neighbour} the oddest thing. You'll hear it too.
The court's warm at this hour, and the gossip's warmer.
Gathering's how we keep the village knit together. Like weaving, only with talk.
I came here for a little quiet and found the whole village. Now I've found you too.
greet.routine.soar: Whoosh! Hello! I was mid-swoop when I saw you.
Fair wind! I've been round the village twice, and now I'm round to you.
I was soaring so fast I nearly flew right past you. Hello!
The air's good today. I've been riding it in long, lazy arcs.
Give me a moment; my veils are still catching up with me.
From up there you looked like a little dot on a bridge. You're much bigger up close.
There's nothing like a long glide to clear the head. Have you ever... no. Sorry.
Spotted you from three islets off! Walkers are easy to find; you don't move about much.
Hello, {player}! I was looping the Lantern Spire. Did you see? Say you saw.
I've been flying since the last bell, and I could go on all day.
Down from the high air! It's colder up there, but so quiet.
I needed a rest anyway. You make a good place to stop, walker.
greet.routine.chat: I was just chatting with {neighbour}. They won't mind; they've heard all my news.
Fair wind! You've interrupted the best bit of gossip, but I'll forgive you.
{friend} and I were just talking about you. Nothing bad. Mostly good.
A walker joins the conversation! Now it's a proper one.
We were deciding whose peach tree is luckiest. You can settle it.
Sorry, I was halfway through a story. I'll finish it later, or never.
Oh, hello, {player}. I'd just said no walker had come by today, and here you are.
I've talked {neighbour} into a corner of the sky. Rescue them by talking to me instead.
The talk was all about the weather. It's always about the weather, up here.
Mind you, everything I was just saying was true. Probably.
Ah, a fresh pair of ears! The old ones were getting tired.
I was telling everyone what walkers eat. Is it true you cook things? Over fire?
greet.routine.evensong: Shh... oh, hello! You've come during the Evensong. Stand quietly with us.
Fair wind. We're singing the day down. You can hum, if you know how.
Isn't it beautiful? Every voice in {village}, all at once.
A walker at the Evensong! Stay, stay, the best verse is coming.
My voice is still ringing. Did you hear the harps lead us in?
Fair wind, {player}. We've sung the sun under the clouds. Now we sing the stars up.
Sorry, I'm all full of song. It takes a moment to come back to talking.
You came for the singing. Good. I'd sooner miss a meal than miss the Evensong.
Listen: that's Vell taking our song to the next village. Sometimes theirs comes back to us.
Have you a song where you come from, for the end of the day?
You're the first walker I've seen stay for the whole Evensong. Or most of it.
Stand right under us. It sounds best from below, so walkers tell me.
greet.routine.escort: Oh, hello! I've just come back from the Old Singer. My ears are still full of its song.
Fair wind! Did you see it? The whale! I swam beside it all the way to the far clouds.
I'm all dew and wonder. I was flying with a Cloud Whale, and it hummed right through me.
You should have seen it, walker: so big the clouds on its back had their own little weather.
Sorry, I'm still breathless. We sang back to it, and it answered.
Fair wind, {player}! A blessing today: an Old Singer passed and let us fly beside it.
I touched its fin. Just with a fingertip. It was warm, like a cloud that's sat in the sun.
The whale's gone on now, east... or west... somewhere wonderful.
My veils still smell of whale-cloud. Sweet, and a little like rain.
When an Old Singer passes, a whole season's weather gets sung. I helped. A little.
I'm back from the whale. I think I'm back. Part of me's still out there.
Have you ever been that close to something so old and so gentle? It makes you very quiet inside.
greet.routine.shelter: Oh! Hello. Come in out of it, quickly. The lightning's walking the clouds.
Shh, hello. I'm sheltering. Everyone is. Storms are no place for a Cirri.
Fair wind... well, foul wind. Stay close to the walls, walker.
Forgive me if I jump. Every rumble goes right through my veils.
Oh, it's you. I thought the thunder had knocked. Come under the roof.
Hello, {player}. We hum when the storm's overhead. It helps. Would you hum with me?
The bell gave its long peal before this came, so we're all tucked in. Hello.
Don't stand out in the open. Lightning loves a tall thing, and you're a tall thing.
I'm all curled up. Storms make me feel very small and very high.
You're brave to be out in this. Or a walker. Perhaps both.
In a storm, the nest is the whole world. Come in and share it.
When it's over, the air will smell new. Until then, we wait.
greet.routine.idle: Oh, hello! I was just hovering. It's a talent; I'm very good at it.
Fair wind! Nothing to do and nowhere to be. The best kind of hour.
Watching the clouds go by underneath, that's all. They never hurry, so neither do I.
A walker! The idle hour just got interesting.
I've been floating here so long the koi think I'm part of the view.
Fair wind, {player}. I'm doing nothing at all. Want to join me?
I was choosing between a nap and a peach. You've chosen for me: neither. Talk.
Just drifting. Even the busiest Cirri need a little drift.
Listen to the chimes arguing with the wind. The wind's winning, I think.
A light breeze, a slow day, and now a visitor. Perfect.
If anyone asks, I was very busy until you came.
So much nothing to think about today. I nearly made it into something.
greet.weather.rain: Mind the bridges, they're slick. Rain's running off the roofs in silver threads.
Fair wind, wet walker! Come under the veilcloth; we'll drip together.
My veils are soaked through. Heavy veils make for slow flying. Hello, though.
The rain's falling past us all the way down to your fields. Lucky fields.
Isn't it odd, watching the rain fall away below you forever? Hello!
Koi love this weather. Look, they're leaping for the drops.
Hello, {player}. Damp days are good days for the looms; the cloud combs out soft.
You look like you've been wrung out. Stand under the awning a while.
Don't your shoulders get tired, carrying all that wet about?
The harps go soft and blurry in the rain. Listen.
At least the rain isn't cold. Warm rain is half a bath.
Every roof in {village} is ringing a different note. Rain makes a harp of the whole village.
Pouring out their hearts, the clouds are. We let them.
Wet veils, wet bridges, wet walker. At least the peaches are happy.
Rain above, cloud below. On days like this the village is a damp little secret between them.
greet.weather.thunder: Oh! Did you hear that one? Right over the Bell Pagoda.
Please come in from the open, walker. Lightning hunts the high places.
Fair... oh, there it goes again. Sorry. I'm not good with storms.
Hello, {player}. Stay close. Things are less frightening with two.
Shh, hello. We're all keeping low and quiet till it passes.
The bell gave us warning, and still I jump at every crash.
A walker, out in this? Your feet must make you brave.
I keep counting between the flash and the rumble. The counts are getting shorter.
Fair wind... I wish there were some. This is all crash and dark.
The children are humming in the nests. You can hear it between the thunder, if you listen.
Forgive my veils. They curl up tight in a storm, all on their own.
Old Cirri say the Old Singers are quarrelling when it thunders. I hope they make up soon.
That one nearly shook the chimes off their hooks!
Don't stand near anything iron, walker. Please. I mean it.
Quickly, inside. The lantern's lit. Storms are kinder from behind a wall.
greet.weather.snow: It's snowing past the islands! The whole sky's full of falling lace.
Fair wind, cold walker! Snow at this height bites. Are your hands all right?
Look, snow's caught in my veils. I'm half a snowcloud now.
The koi have gone sleepy and slow. They don't love the cold, poor things.
Snow! I've been catching flakes since I woke. They taste of nothing at all, beautifully.
Hello, {player}. Snow makes everything so quiet, even the bridges stop creaking.
Our breath and the clouds look the same today. Hello.
Snow falls past us and lands on you lot below. Does it pile up? Do you mind?
The lanterns look lovely through the snow. Everything glows twice.
Mind your step, walker. Snow sits on the bridges like a cushion, a very slippery cushion.
Wrap up, walker. I'd lend you a veil, but you'd only trip on it.
The harps sound brighter in the cold, like little bells.
Peach trees in snow! The gardeners are fretting. I'm admiring.
Every flake comes down from somewhere higher than us. Isn't that strange to think?
Snow and a walker in one day. It's turning into a day of wonders.
greet.wind.aure: Fair wind! Aure has the sky today: gentle, dewy and kind. A good day to meet.
Aure's blowing from the east. Everything smells of morning, even now.
Aure's day, walker. Soft wind, soft words. Hello.
Hello, {player}. Aure keeps the dew on things all day, so mind the wet bridges.
An Aure day always feels like the world's only just woken up.
Aure's in a gentle mood. The harps are barely humming.
Fair wind, and fair Aure! Greet the wind too, walker; it's only polite.
The east wind's here, light as a breath. Nothing bad happens on an Aure day. Usually.
Aure has the sky! My veil-tips are all damp and I don't mind a bit.
With Aure blowing, even the clouds below look freshly washed.
greet.wind.sefa: Fair wind! Sefa has the sky: warm and lazy, and smelling of peaches.
Sefa's day. Everyone's flying slow and smiling. You will too, soon.
Ah, the south wind. Sefa makes the whole village drowsy. Hello, walker.
Fair wind, {player}! Sniff: that's Sefa. Peach blossom and warm cloud.
On Sefa days the peaches ripen twice as fast. Or it feels that way.
Sefa's blowing and I'm in no hurry at all. Take your time.
The south wind's sleepy and so am I. Talk softly.
Fair wind, and a warm one. Sefa's the kind of wind you could nap on.
A Sefa day and a walker visiting. Life's sweet.
Even the koi are lazy on a Sefa day: floating, mouths open, waiting for something to fall in.
greet.wind.vell: Fair wind! Vell has the sky. You'll hear songs from far off today; it carries everything.
The west wind's blowing, so every harp in {village} is a little louder. Hello!
Vell's day, walker. Listen: you can almost hear the next village humming.
Vell makes me want to sing all day. I've been trying not to. Mostly.
Fair wind, {player}. With Vell blowing, the Evensong will carry for miles.
Vell's blowing from the west, all evening colours, even at midday.
The west wind's mellow today. Good for long talks.
Vell carries voices, so be careful what you say: the whole sky's listening.
A Vell day makes everyone a little wistful. Me especially.
Vell has the sky! The chimes have been singing since I woke.
greet.wind.borre: Fair wind... though Borre has the sky today, so perhaps not so fair.
The north wind's here, sharp as a needle. Keep your collar up, walker.
Borre's day. Hold tight to the rails; Borre likes to snatch at walkers.
Cold now, stormy later, likely. That's Borre for you. Hello.
Hello, {player}. Borre's bitten my veil-tips numb.
Borre's blowing, so everyone's flying close to home today.
Brr. Borre. Talk fast and we'll both stay warm.
The bellkeeper's watched the north all day. On Borre days, you never know.
Borre's sharp, but honest. You always know where you stand with the north wind.
On a Borre day the clouds below go grey and hurried. I don't blame them.
ground.general: Is it true you can't leave the ground at all? Not even a little, when you're very happy? That seems unfair. Happiness ought to count for something.
Stairs! I've seen them in our guest rooms. A little hill you keep indoors so you can climb it every day. Why would anyone want that?
A guest showed me how a chair works. I watched very closely. I still don't see what the legs are for, if the chair isn't going anywhere.
The ground pulls on you all the time, they say. Every moment, every step. Doesn't it ache? I'd be so tired.
Fire, under food, on purpose! I asked a guest why, and they said it tastes better. Better than what? Better than not being on fire?
Swimming is lying down in water and paddling until you get somewhere. I've watched it from above. It looks like flying, only wetter and more worried.
Mud is ground that's been rained on and decided to keep your feet. A guest told me that, and I've never stopped thinking about it.
Do you think about your feet? You must. Every moment, one of them is touching the world. I'd think of nothing else.
Running! Both feet off the ground for a heartbeat, then down, then up again. It's flying in very small pieces. I think it's terribly brave.
When a walker falls over, does the ground say sorry? It ought to. It pulled.
A guest said beds are for lying flat on. I'd assumed the blankets were there to stop you floating off in the night. Apparently not. Then what are they for?
We look down at your world all day and you look up at ours. I think we both get the better view.
Guests always grip the bridge rail and stare at the clouds the first time. We don't mind. Hold on as long as you like, walker. The rail's there for you.
I used to pity walkers. Then I watched one plant a whole field of wheat and come back a season later to find it gold. We can't do that.
Bread, I'm told, is seeds crushed and wetted and put in a fire, and it comes out soft? That's practically weaving.
Why do walker houses all have roofs? Is that so the sky can't fall in, or so the sky can't see you?
A guest once left footprints across the Veil Court in the dew. Nobody wanted to sweep them away. We watched them dry for an hour.
How do you know where you are without the winds to tell you? Do you count your steps? Do you ask the trees?
Is the ground warm? It looks warm in the afternoon, all gold and green. At night it looks cold. I imagine it's like a cushion someone has just left.
I'd love to know what grass feels like. We fly over it on the islands, but that's not the same. Is it soft? Does it tickle?
Walkers climb mountains to get a little nearer the sky. We watch you doing it, tiny and determined, and cheer. You can't hear us. We cheer anyway.
Grounded is the saddest word we have, and yet you're grounded every day and seem perfectly cheerful about it. How do you manage?
Most walkers dream of flying, a guest told me. Here's a secret: some nights, I dream of walking. It's always very slow and very loud.
Everything you own, you have to carry, because if you set it down the ground keeps it. That must make you very careful about what you own.
Boots, to keep your feet safe from the ground! So the ground isn't entirely kind, then. I've always wondered.
You cross water in a little wooden house that floats? A boat! A nest for the sea. Walkers are cleverer than we give you credit for.
Walkers walk until they're tired, then sit down, which is walking stopped. Then they get up and walk again. It seems like a great many decisions.
What does the ground smell like? After rain a little of it reaches us: earthy and green and somehow brown. I think I'd like it.
A guest fell asleep on our bridge once, flat on their back, snoring at the stars. The children gathered round to watch. They'd never seen anyone hold so still.
Walkers are always touching something: a floor, a wall, a rail, a friend's shoulder. We touch nothing all day long. Maybe that's why we hug so hard.
Bridges, doors, stairs: we build them all for guests. It's the Courtesy. But I always want to ask: wouldn't you rather we just carried you? We'd be gentle.
You're heavier than us, but you don't look tired. I think walkers are stronger than they know.
Some children think walkers are glued to the ground. I let them believe it a while. Then I tell them the truth: walkers just like it there.
I watched a walker stand on a hilltop for a whole hour once, just looking up. I hope they saw me wave.
Ladders I understand. Ladders are stairs for people in a hurry.
I've seen old walkers lean on sticks. A stick, for leaning on the ground! As if the ground needed holding up as well.
For us, falling is the worst thing in the world. For walkers it seems to happen most days, and you just get up again. I find that astonishing.
What do walkers do on a still day? You don't need a wind to go anywhere. Lucky things. Or unlucky. I can't decide which.
A guest asked me what we do when we're tired of flying. I didn't understand the question. Do you get tired of breathing?
From up here, a walker carrying planks looks like an ant with a dream. I mean that kindly. You're always building something.
A guest made me eat a warm apple once, warmed over a fire on purpose. It was... interesting. I had two more.
We always hear guests before we see them: footsteps on the bridges, thump, thump, like a drum announcing you. It's very friendly.
A guest told me the walkers below mistake us for kites. I've no idea what a kite is, but I liked the sound of it.
If the ground pulls everything, does it pull the trees too? Is that why they hold on so tight with their roots? Poor trees. They'd fly if they could.
Gravity, a guest called the pull. It sounds like an illness. Is it catching? Don't laugh. Is it?
Wet feet! Walkers are always going on about wet feet. Is it like a wet veil? Ours drag and go grey. Do your feet go grey?
Your shadow follows you everywhere on the ground, stuck to your heels. Ours lands far below on the clouds, all on its own. Yours must be good company.
Guests who come up the Wind Stone always look down first, then up, then at us, and then the questions start. You did exactly the same, you know.
A walker on a skywood bridge stands as if they belong to something. We belong to the wind; you belong to the ground. Just different kinds of belonging.
You've got ground on your feet. Where's it from? I always ask. Mud on a walker means they've been somewhere interesting.
Do you have a favourite patch of ground, {player}? You must. You spend your whole lives on it. I'd love to hear about yours.
You eat sitting down at a table, everyone round it at once? Like the Evensong, but for food? That I'd like to see.
A walker child once drew squares on our court and hopped through them. Our children tried it in the air. Nobody could agree whose turn it was.
I think the ground is shy. It lies under everything without a word, holding us all up. Somebody ought to talk to it.
Walkers dig deep for shiny stones and then wear them. Doesn't that make you heavier? We'd sooner wear a Sky Scale. It weighs less than a thought.
They say walkers sleep a whole night without moving and wake up exactly where they lay down. No drifting at all! I'd find that unnerving.
One day of walking: that's what I'd ask for, if I could ask for anything. I'd spend it going up a hill, to find out whether getting higher by hard work feels better than our way.
You have a word for coming down after a jump: landing. We have that word too. We use it very differently.
Do walkers ever look up and wish? I think you do. I've seen it from up here, that little tilt of the head. We do the same thing, looking down.
You stand still without even trying. I've never stood still in my life. I hover, and hovering takes concentration, whatever it looks like.
ground.dreamer: Sometimes I imagine lying on the ground and looking up at us. What would we look like? Little rose flames drifting, or ribbons someone let go of... ribbons. I like that.
The ground is so patient. It's waited under the sky forever and never once asked to come up. I wonder if it dreams of us the way we dream of... what was I saying?
If I ever touched the ground, I think I'd hear it. A slow hum, like a whale's, too low for walkers to notice, because they've always been standing in it.
Down there every footstep stays. Up here every song goes. One of us is writing a very long book, and the other is... hm. Sorry. I've lost it.
Do you think the ground looks up at night too? At the stars? It must. It's been lying on its back for ever so long.
I once followed a walker's lantern along a road at night, all the way to a little house. The door opened and swallowed it. I made up a whole life for them. I hope they're well.
Is it true the ground goes down further than the sky goes up? I can't hold that in my head. It slips out like a koi.
If I could walk, I'd walk very slowly, so it would last. I'd... oh, look, a hawk. What were we... walking. Slowly. Yes.
ground.merry: Walkers do a little hop when they're happy. A tiny hop! As if to say: look, I nearly flew! I adore it. Do one for me. Go on.
I've invented a game called Walker. You hover very low and plod. Clump, clump, clump. The children love it. Don't be offended, you're our favourite game.
Race you to the Garden! Oh. Right. Bridges. Off you go, then, and I'll fly very slowly so you can pretend you're winning.
What would I do on the ground? Roll down a hill! I've watched walker children do it, squealing all the way. It's a loop with extra grass.
When a walker trips on our bridge, we say nothing. We're too busy laughing. Kindly! Kindly laughing. Mostly kindly.
A guest taught me a ground game where you hide and the other one finds you. Up here there's nowhere to hide. We just hover behind each other and giggle.
The ground is a very big, very slow friend who never wants to play. I keep inviting it. It keeps lying there.
I'd trade a whole basket of peaches for one splash in a puddle. Big splash, both feet. Then I'd fly off before anyone saw.
ground.gentle: You've carried yourself everywhere today, haven't you? Every single step. Rest on the bridge a while. The ground will wait for you.
I don't think the ground is cruel. It holds you up. It only holds a little too tightly, sometimes.
When I see a walker trip far below, my veils jump before I do. I always want to fly down and catch them. Silly, from this height. I wish them soft grass instead.
You must miss the ground while you're up here. That's all right. You can miss it with me. I miss things too.
Down there, when you fall, you're caught straight away. Up here, falling goes on and on. Maybe the ground is the kinder of the two. Don't tell the sky I said so.
Is there someone waiting for you down there, {player}? I hope so. Everyone should have someone who listens for their footsteps.
I'd like to plant something on the ground one day, with your help. You'd put it in, and I'd sing to it from up here. Between us, it would grow.
If you're ever down there alone and frightened, hum. Just a little. The wind carries it, and someone up here will be humming back.
ground.shy: The ground? I've... never been near it. Is it nice? You don't have to say... if it isn't.
I'd be frightened down there. So many walkers, all at the same height... all looking straight at you. Sorry. That's silly.
I like that walkers go quiet when they look at the clouds. It makes me feel... less strange. For looking at the ground.
Do walkers ever feel shy? You stand so firmly. I always thought standing would make a person... braver.
Sometimes I fly low over the meadows at dawn when nobody's about. Just to look. Please don't tell anyone... if that's all right.
I watched a walker sleep in a meadow once, from very high up. Just lying there in the flowers. It looked so safe. I don't think I've ever felt that safe. Sorry. That was a lot.
Is it... is it true the ground is warm? Like a nest? Only, I'd always wondered.
Walking... I think I'd want to walk behind someone. You, maybe. If you wouldn't mind.
ground.proud: The ground? Honest, solid and entirely without ambition. Still, someone must stay down there and hold things up. We're grateful, in a lofty sort of way.
Walkers build in stone because they can afford the weight. We build in light because we're better at it. Both fine choices. One is more beautiful.
Not one Cirri in all our history has set foot on the ground. Not one. That isn't luck, walker. That's tradition.
I'll grant walkers this: your bells are fine. Heavy, but fine. You'd never get one airborne, of course.
Your fields are tidy, I'll give you that. Neat rows, very respectable. Nearly as neat as a well-woven veil. Nearly.
When I was young, I thought walkers were simply Cirri who'd failed at something. I know better now. You're your own sort of splendid. Heavier, but splendid.
We never had to come up from anywhere: we were always here. You came up by the Wind Stone, which is quite all right. That's precisely what the Courtesy is for.
If {village} ever needed help from below, I'd want it to be you who came. That's the highest compliment a Cirri can pay a walker. Don't let it go to your head. Well. A little.
ground.restless: The ground goes on and on in every direction, and walkers only see a little of it at a time. I'd go mad. I'd want to see over the next hill, and the next, and the next.
Have you been to the far edge of the land, where the sea begins? Tell me everything. How far? How many dawns? Which way does the wind blow there?
Every road down there is a promise to go somewhere. I've followed a few from the air just to see where they end. Most of them end in another road.
The ground has places the sky has never seen: inside the mountains, the bottom of the sea. That's the only thing about it I envy.
I followed a river all the way to the sea once. Three days. My veils still taste of salt when Vell blows.
If you're going far, take me with you. Not on the ground, of course. I'll fly above you the whole way. You won't even have to talk to me.
Walkers can stay in one place for a whole day. I tried it once. I lasted until the bell, and then I had to fly round the islets twice to recover.
Somewhere down there is a place no Cirri has ever flown over. I'm going to find it. Then I'll find the next one.
ground.busy: The ground? Lovely, I'm sure. Hold this. No, the other end. Walkers are wonderful at holding things still, it's the feet. Steady. Thank you.
I haven't time to wonder about the ground, walker. There's thread to wind, two baskets to fill and a nest that won't tidy itself. Ask me again at the Evensong.
Walkers get things done, I'll say that. Plant a field, build a wall, finished by sundown. I could use a walker on my side today, if you're offering.
You walk everywhere? Even when you're late? I'd never get anything done. Mind you, I never get anything done anyway. Pass me that basket.
Mud? No time for mud. Wipe your feet on the bridge, there's a good walker, and mind the lanterns, they've only just been filled.
Ground, sky, it's all work in the end. You have your fields and we have our clouds. Speaking of which, I've left a basket of peaches on the Loom House steps. Excuse me.
A whole night's sleep, on purpose? Walkers do that? I'd love to. I'd have to fit it in somewhere, mind. Perhaps after the next storm.
If you're going back down, keep an eye out for a spool of gold thread, would you? I dropped one through the clouds last spring. Still looking.
ground.wise: The ground and the sky are two halves of one thing. Walkers keep the roots, we keep the blossoms. Neither is a tree on its own.
My elders used to say: never look down on a walker, except from a great height. It was a joke. It was also not a joke.
The ground remembers everything and the sky remembers nothing. That's why walkers keep their grudges and we lose ours by noon. There are worse ways to be.
An old saying: "Heavy feet, steady heart." It's a compliment, walker. The steadiest hearts are the ones that stay where they're needed.
Being grounded doesn't always mean falling. Some Cirri ground themselves with grudges, or with gold. Heaviness is heaviness, wherever you carry it.
The ground taught us one lesson long ago: what's heavy sinks. We listened. That's why {village} still floats.
You can learn a great deal about walkers from above. Watch where their paths wear deepest. That's where they love to go.
The Courtesy says come up and be welcome. It never says stay. A walker belongs to the ground as we belong to the wind, and there's no shame in going home. Only in never visiting.
ground.curious: What does the ground feel like under your feet? Hard? Soft? Does it change? Do you notice it at all, or is it like breathing?
Do walkers have songs for walking? You must. Something to keep your feet in time? Would you sing me one? Just a verse. I'll hum the rest.
When you sit, do your legs fold up? I've only seen it from far away. It looked like a bridge collapsing very politely.
What do walkers call the winds? You must have names for them. Is Borre as cross down there as it is up here?
What's the heaviest thing you've ever carried? And the lightest? And did the ground mind either one?
If I dropped a sky peach from here, would it reach the ground whole? Would a walker find it? Would they eat it? I've always wondered and never dared.
Who taught you to walk, {player}? Did someone show you, or did your feet just know? Did you fall a lot? Was it frightening? Tell me!
Is it louder down there, or quieter? Do birds sound different from underneath? Can you hear us when we sing the Evensong? You can? How far down?
ground.villages: On clear days you can see a bell-village from the Lift Dock: a little patch of roofs and fields with a bell in the middle, like a stone in a peach.
Their bell rings at different times from ours. Ours rings at dawn and dusk. Theirs rings whenever somebody's had a fright, as far as I can tell.
The bell-villagers keep the tidiest fields: little squares of green and gold, stitched together with paths. Seen from above, it's a quilt someone's still working on.
The bell-villagers all have such splendid noses. You can see them from above the clouds. Do you suppose they can smell our peaches from down there?
I watch the bell-villagers gather round their bell by day. They don't sing, but they hum a little. Hmm, hmm. We hum back from the clouds, and I like to think they hear.
Their big grey walker never sleeps. It goes round and round the houses all night, and it gives flowers to the children. We think it's the kindest thing on the ground.
At suppertime smoke rises thin and grey from the bell-village. We give it a wide berth. Fire's fire, even when it's only cooking.
Gossip from on high: the farmer by the river has planted pumpkins in a perfect ring. We think it's a message. {neighbour} thinks they just like pumpkins.
A bell-village at dawn: doors opening, a dog barking, someone chasing a chicken. From up here it looks like a koi pool when you drop the crumbs in.
The bell-villagers love emeralds more than anything, the Skymerchant says. They'd trade almost anything for a handful. Our Skymerchant has started loving them too, which worries the rest of us.
Last spring two walkers in the bell-village below were married, and the whole village gathered round. We flew over in a ring and dropped petals. They looked up astonished. I hope it was good luck.
The bell-villagers don't know our names, but they know our shapes. A guest told me they call us the ribbons. I've decided I like it.
Every bell-village has its own bell note. One rings bright as a koi's flicker, one clanks like a dropped bucket. We can tell which village is talking just by listening.
Far to Vell-ward there's a bell-village of sandstone houses and sandy paths, and another to Borre-ward that's white with snow half the year. Walkers will live anywhere.
Their children run round the well all afternoon, shrieking. Our children fly round the koi pool all afternoon, shrieking. Some things are the same everywhere.
The bell-villagers go to bed at dusk, just as we start the Evensong. I think of it as their lullaby, coming down soft through the cloud.
I once watched a bell-village mend itself after a bad night. Everyone came out with planks and stones, even the children. By the next dusk it was whole. Walkers are stubborn in the best way.
If you're from a bell-village yourself, tell them hello from {village}. Tell them we wave. They never seem to look up.
There's a walker in the bell-village below who reads all day by a window. {neighbour} swears they're writing a book about us. I do hope it's flattering.
Now and then a walker in a blue robe comes to the bell-village leading two spitting animals on ropes, sells everything they have and vanishes again. We think they're a Skymerchant of the ground.
ground.wonders: The ocean is the strangest thing I've ever seen: a second sky lying down the wrong way up, and you can't even fly in it. What's it for?
The sea goes dark in the middle, as if the ground had a great hole and poured blue in to hide it. How deep does it go? Does anybody know?
Forests from above are clouds made of leaves: thick and soft-looking and full of birds. I'd love to fly into one, but you'd snag your veils in a breath.
Caves! Holes in the ground that go into the dark! Walkers go into them on purpose, a guest told me, carrying fire. Why go into the dark when there's all this sky?
Deserts are the only ground that never seems to have clouds over it. Gold sand forever and not a scrap of shade. Who lives there? Are they very thirsty?
Snow on the ground stays and stays. Up here snow just passes by. Down there it piles up soft and white, as if the ground were pretending to be a cloud.
Rivers only ever go downhill. Even water can't escape the pull. It makes me sad, and it also makes me very fond of rivers.
Cats look up. Every other walker-animal looks down at the grass, but cats sit on walls and stare straight at us. I think cats know something.
Roads are thin lines from one village to the next, worn into the ground just by walkers going back and forth. That's a sort of song, isn't it? Sung with feet.
Mountains are the ground trying to fly. You can tell. They lean up as far as they can and get snow on their heads for the trouble.
Sheep look like small clouds that fell down and grew legs. The children won't believe me that they aren't. I'm not entirely sure myself.
A lake on a still morning holds the whole sky in it: clouds, birds, us. Once I saw myself in one from high above, a little rose speck drifting on the water.
What are the little lights walkers put on poles at night? They look like stars that came down to visit. A guest says they're fire. I'd rather they were stars.
The cherry groves go a pink that makes our weavers jealous. If we could comb that colour, every veil would be rose to the root.
Down there flowers grow in whole fields, every colour at once. Up here we keep ours in pots. Walkers are very generous with flowers.
Swamps look like the ground couldn't decide between water and mud, so it gave up and grew trees in both. I rather admire that.
Is it true there are mushrooms as big as houses? I saw something red and round from very far off. Either a mushroom or a very strange nest.
Bees go from flower to flower all day without ever landing for long. They're the most Cirri thing on the ground.
A walker on a horse is a walker being carried by another walker. It looks so grand. I'd never try it. But I'd love to watch you try.
Footprints in snow are a whole story written on the ground: here a walker went, here they stopped, here they turned back. I could read snow all day.
The jungle is so green it almost hurts: trees on trees on trees, with vines hanging down like veils. I think the jungle wants to be a sky village.
Where does the rain go? It falls on the ground and disappears. Does the ground drink it? Is the ground thirsty all the time?
Beaches are where the ground stops and the sea starts, and they argue about it all day, back and forth. The sea never wins. Neither does the beach.
In winter the lakes go white and hard, and walkers walk across them. On water! That's very nearly flying, isn't it?
Wheat in Sefa's wind ripples like the cloud floor under the village. The ground can make waves too. I never knew until I saw it.
At night, from above, a walker village is a handful of warm windows in the dark. Every one of them is somebody's evening. I like guessing what they're all talking about.
Ravines are cracks in the ground so deep the light never reaches the bottom. I flew over one once and felt it pulling. I didn't stay to look.
Pumpkins! Big orange things that sit in fields doing nothing. The children want one for the Veil Court. The gardeners say it would sink the island.
There's land to Sefa-ward striped red and orange and yellow, like a dawn that fell down and dried. Who painted it? Did it hurt?
Glow berries grow in caves, the gardeners say, hanging in the dark like little lanterns. Sweet things in the dark. Maybe the dark isn't all bad.
ground.fears: The worst dream a Cirri can have: your veils give out and you fall, and fall, and land. And then you're grounded, and you can never get up again.
The pull frightens me. You can feel it even up here, when you fly too low: a heaviness at the ends of your veils, as if the ground were whispering "stay".
Fire. Walkers make it everywhere: in hearths, on torches, under pots. At night the ground is speckled with little fires, and I can't stop counting them.
Things walk the ground at night. Slow grey ones, rattling ones, ones with far too many legs. Night-walkers, we call them. How do you ever sleep?
Don't take this the wrong way, but walkers frighten me a little at first. You're so solid. You could knock a Cirri out of the sky without even meaning to.
The dark under the ground is the darkest dark there is. Holes that go down and down where no wind ever reaches. A Cirri would die of quiet in there.
Falling isn't what frightens us. Landing is. Falling at least has sky in it.
I've watched a forest burn. Smoke boiling up past the clouds, and birds going round and round, looking for somewhere to land. We sang for them all night. It didn't help.
A guest told me about a green walker-thing that creeps up quietly and bursts. Bursts! I haven't slept properly since.
Spiders climb. That's what frightens me about them. Everything else on the ground stays on the ground. Spiders go up walls. What else might they go up?
Being grounded isn't only about veils. It's being stuck: one place, one height, one view, forever. That's what frightens us most. Walkers just call it home.
Deep water pulls even harder than the ground, I'm told. Things sink into it and never come back. At least the ground gives things back now and then.
Roofs make me nervous. Even ours, in the guest rooms. A Cirri likes to know there's always a way up.
A thrown stone goes up a little, turns round and falls. That's what the pull does to everything, given time. What frightens me is how patient it is.
Children are told that if they fly too low, the ground will reach up and grab their veil-tips. It isn't quite true. But nobody flies low after hearing it, and that's what it's for.
Fireworks are the ground's worst idea: fire thrown at the sky on purpose, for fun. They're loud, they're dangerous and they're rude. Please don't, {player}.
Lava. A guest told me there are rivers of fire under the ground, and sometimes they come up. Rivers! Of fire! I've decided not to believe it. It's easier.
I watched a walker cut down a tree once. It leaned, and leaned, and then the ground took it all at once. I couldn't breathe until it landed.
The rattling night-walkers carry bows, and arrows go up. That's the one thing on the ground that can reach the sky, and I hate it.
The ground at noon is fine. It's the ground at dusk I don't like: the shadows getting longer, as if the dark were climbing up out of it toward us.
Walkers wear iron. Whole suits of it! Doesn't it drag you down? I'd sink through the clouds in a breath.
If a Cirri ever did fall all the way down, would the walkers be kind? I'd like to think so. The one who caught our falling child in a hay cart was.
On dark nights the breeze carries up the noises from the ground: groans, rattles, the hiss of something green. I pull my veils over my ears and hum.
Walkers dig holes everywhere: wells, mines, cellars. The ground is full of holes and you keep making more. Doesn't it worry you that one day you'll dig through to the dark?
Night-moths come for walkers who haven't slept, I'm told, and they fly right up into our sky to do it. Do get some sleep, walker. For both our sakes.
first_meeting: Oh! A walker, a real one. I'd heard you came up the Wind Stone now and then, but I've never met one. I'm {name}.
Fair wind, stranger, and welcome to {village}. The Courtesy says you're our guest, so you are. I'm {name}.
You must be the walker everyone's talking about. Or a new one. Either way, I'm {name}, and I'm very curious.
Well, look at you. Two feet, no veils, standing right here in the sky. Welcome! I'm {name}.
A walker on our bridges! The windkeeper said someone was coming up. Hello, I'm {name}, the {job}.
Goodness. I've only ever seen walkers from far above. You're much bigger up close, and much less dotty.
The first windkeepers set the Wind Stone for guests like you. I never thought I'd meet one. Fair wind! I'm {name}.
Hello, hello! Welcome to {village}. Do you need anything? Water? A peach? Something to hold on to?
A visitor! The Courtesy is old, but it still means what it says: you're welcome here. I'm {name}.
Oh! I nearly flew into you. Nobody ever stands still in the way up here. Hello, I'm {name}.
You came up the Wind Stone? All that way, just standing in the wind? Brave walker. I'm {name}, of {village}.
Fair wind to you, first-time guest. We don't bite, we don't fall, and we sing at dusk. That's most of it.
Forgive the staring. I've heard walker stories since I was small, and here's one, looking right back at me.
Welcome to the high sky, walker. I'm {name}. If the height makes you dizzy, look at me instead of down.
How wonderful, a guest! The bridges get so few feet on them. I'm {name}, and the bridges are yours.
A walker in {village}. The old ones will want to hear about this. I'm {name}. And you're {player}? What a solid sort of name.
You're the first walker I've ever spoken to. Am I doing it right? I'm {name}.
They say walkers are sturdy and kind. You look sturdy. Let's find out about kind. I'm {name}.
Welcome, welcome! Did the wind lift you gently? It's meant to; that's the whole point of it. I'm {name}.
My veils have gone all fluttery. I think they're excited to meet you. So am I. I'm {name}.
A walker, here, in {village}! Let me look at you. Feet, yes. Hands, yes. Wings, no. Welcome!
Fair wind, traveller. The Courtesy was made long before I was born, but I'm the one keeping it today. Welcome.
I'm {name}. You'll meet everyone soon enough; we're a nosy sort of sky.
You came all the way up! Most walkers only look at us from below and wonder.
Welcome, guest of the Wind Stone! You've arrived at the best village in the sky. I'm biased. I'm {name}.
A new face, and a ground face at that! Fair wind. I'm {name}, and I want to know everything about you.
Don't worry about the edges; we'll catch you. Probably. We've had plenty of practice with the children.
Fair wind and welcome. I'm {name}, of {village}. Ask anyone for my nest if you ever need a friend.
You're real! I'd half thought walkers were a story to make the little ones finish their peaches.
Welcome to {village}, walker. Mind your step, mind the koi, and mind you come back. I'm {name}.
hurt: Oh. It's you. Please keep your hands where I can see them.
I'd rather keep a little sky between us today, walker.
You struck me. I haven't forgotten, even if you have.
Hello... from over here. A bit further off than usual, if you don't mind.
My veil's still sore where you hit it. What do you want?
Careful. I'm watching you the way I'd watch a storm.
Is this a kind visit, or another of the other kind?
We don't strike each other up here. Not ever. I didn't know walkers did.
I'll talk. But I'll talk from where I can fly off quickly.
You frightened me, walker. I'm still frightened, a little.
Mm. You again. My heart's gone low as the clouds since you hit me.
The Courtesy says I must welcome you. It says nothing about trusting you.
Say what you came to say. Gently, please.
I flinched when I saw you. I've never flinched at anyone before.
Why did you do it? No, don't answer. I'm not sure I want to know.
Please don't come any closer. Not yet.
My veils curl up when you're near now. They remember, even when I try not to.
{player}. I thought you were kind. I'm trying to remember why.
You've a heavy hand for a guest. I'm keeping my distance.
Hello, I suppose. Mind your hands, and I'll mind my temper.
night: Mmm? Who's... oh. A walker. It's the middle of the night.
Hnn. I was dreaming of whales, and now there's a walker. Which is stranger?
Oh! You woke me. I nearly uncurled straight off my cushion.
Shh, the whole nest's asleep. What is it?
Is it dawn? It isn't dawn. Why isn't it dawn, and why are you here?
Mm, walker... the stars aren't even halfway across. Come back when the bell rings.
Sorry. Hello. Sleep. Sorry. What were we saying?
You've woken me from a lovely drift. I was floating over a sea of peaches.
Mrrf. If this isn't a fire or a whale, I'm going straight back to sleep.
Oh... hello. My veils are still tucked round me. Give me a moment to come unwound.
A walker at my nest, at night? Is something wrong? Are you hurt?
Hmm? I was curled up tight as a bud. What's the matter?
Do walkers never sleep? You must sleep sometime. Now would be good.
I'm awake. Mostly. Partly. A little.
Shh, {partner}'s still asleep. Whisper, walker.
Ohh. You've woken me right out of a song. I was just at the best part.
It's dark, {player}. Even the lanterns are drowsy. What is it?
Sleepy hello. Very sleepy. Make it short and sweet.
You're lucky I'm a light sleeper. Well, not lucky for me. Hello.
Oh, it's you. I thought a night-moth had got in. You're much warmer than a night-moth.
Is the sky falling? No? Then let me sleep, walker, please.
My cushion was only just getting warm. What can I do for you, quickly?
Hello... I'm floating sideways. Everything's sideways. Is that you or me?
Even the koi are asleep. Even the wind's asleep. And here you are.
Ah, a midnight walker. Talk softly; dreams startle easily.
walk_off: No. I don't want to talk to you yet. Fair wind, walker.
I'm going now. Give me some sky.
Not today. My veils are still shaking.
I'd rather be anywhere else just now. Excuse me.
Leave me be. I'll come round when I come round.
You hurt me. It'll take more than a few words before I can forget it.
I'm flying off now. Please don't follow.
