Don't. Just... don't. Good day.
I've nothing to say to you, walker. Not yet.
Talk to someone else. I'm still low from what you did.
My heart's too heavy for company. Especially yours.
I'll be over there. Alone. That's the point.
Hm. No. I'm going to find a quieter cloud.
You'll have to wait, {player}. I'm not ready.
The Courtesy is for guests. Guests don't strike their hosts. Good day.
Please go. I'll think about forgiving you another day.
Some things need a few dawns to mend. This is one of them.
I'm turning round now. I'd like you to let me.
Not now. My veil's still sore and so am I.
Ask me again when the bruises fade. Not before.
busy_off: Oh! Look at the sun. Back in a light breeze, walker. Mostly.
Sorry, must dash! A {job}'s work won't do itself.
Hold that thought, will you? I've three things waiting and one of them's sulking.
Fair wind, I really must go. Lovely talking!
I've let it go too long. Back to work for me. Visit again!
Duty calls, and it calls loudly. Fair wind, {player}!
That's my bell, or my conscience. Either way, I'm off.
Sorry, sorry, I've something half finished and it won't finish itself. Goodbye!
I could talk all day, but then nothing would get done. Fair wind!
Must fly! Literally. That's how I go everywhere.
Oh, I nearly forgot! I've got to... you know. Goodbye, walker!
Excuse me. The work's piling up like clouds before rain.
A light breeze's worth of talk is all I've got today. Sorry! Off I go.
I'll be back once this is done. Probably. Possibly. Fair wind!
Don't take it to heart, walker. I leave everyone mid-sentence.
The day's running off without me. Must catch it!
Off I go! If anyone asks, I was working the whole time.
Sorry to cut it short. Tomorrow, longer, I promise.
I've just remembered something important. I've also forgotten what. Back to work!
Keep the end of that story for me. I'll want it later. Goodbye!
apology_accepted: Thank you for saying it. All right, walker. The sky's clear between us.
Sorry is a good word. I'll take it, and we'll start again.
I believe you. Let's let it blow away, like a little cloud.
Well. That's mended, then. Mostly. Fair wind, friend.
Keep your heart light, the old ones say. Mine's lighter already. All forgiven.
It took some courage to say that. I'm glad you did.
All right. We'll call it one bad gust. Fair wind again.
I accept. Don't do it again, though. Please.
My veils have stopped curling. I suppose that means I forgive you.
Apology taken, folded and put away. Let's not unfold it again.
Oh, that's better. I didn't like being cross with you.
Thank you, {player}. The wind's turned. Let's fly on.
I forgive you. It's lighter than staying cross, and I'm built to be light.
Done and forgiven. Now come closer; I won't bite.
That's all I needed to hear. Welcome back to the sky.
apology_wary: I hear you. I'm just not ready to believe you yet.
Sorry is a start. Only a start, walker.
Thank you for saying it. I still need a few dawns.
Words are light. Let's see what your hands do next.
I'll think on it. From over here.
Mm. A torn veil doesn't mend in a breath. Neither do I.
I want to forgive you. Give me a little time to want it all the way.
That's kind of you to say. I'm still watching your hands.
You mean it, I think. My veils aren't convinced.
Sorry doesn't unstrike a blow. But it's better than nothing.
I'll keep my distance a little longer, {player}. It's not a no.
Come back tomorrow and say it again. Then I'll know.
I believe you're sorry. I'm just not sure I'm finished being hurt.
Give me a light breeze or two, walker. Then ask again.
gift.loved: Oh, {gift}! How did you know? I've wanted one for ages.
For me? This is lovely, walker. Truly lovely. My veils are all aflutter.
Oh, {player}... thank you. I'll keep it in my nest where I can see it every dawn.
You've made me so high I could touch the stars!
Oh, oh, oh, {gift}! Wait till {friend} sees this.
This is perfect. You've a better eye than most Cirri, walker.
I'm going to do a loop. Excuse me. There. Thank you!
It's beautiful. I don't know what to say, and that's rare for me.
A gift like this deserves a song. I'll sing you one at the Evensong.
Walkers give the best gifts. I've decided. Well, you've decided it for me.
My, oh my, {gift}, for me? I'll treasure it. I'll treasure you too.
My heart's gone right up past the clouds. Thank you, dear walker.
You remembered what I love! Or you guessed. Either way, you're a wonder.
I'll keep this always. When I'm old I'll tell everyone who gave it to me.
Look at it. I could cry. Cirri tears float, you know. Very undignified.
Thank you! Of everything, {gift} is exactly the thing. Exactly.
You've brought me sunshine in your hands, walker.
I've been hoping someone would. I didn't dare hope it would be you.
Best gift since the Sky Scale I found when I was small. Maybe better.
I'll show the whole village. Twice!
Oh, {gift}. You lovely, sturdy, thoughtful walker.
Up here, a gift like this is remembered for years. Thank you.
For me? Really me? Oh, my veils have gone pink right to the roots.
This makes me higher than a whale's back!
Wonderful. Utterly. I'll be humming all day because of this.
gift.liked: Oh, how nice. Thank you, walker!
A present, and {gift} at that! I'll find a good place for it.
You didn't have to, and you did. That's the best part.
What a thoughtful thing. Fair wind to you for it.
Lovely. I'll put it to good use.
For me? Thank you, {player}. That's brightened the day.
How kind! I like it very much.
A gift from a walker! I'll tell the others; they'll be jealous.
My veils have perked up a bit. That's the gift working.
That's just right. Thank you kindly.
Well, well, {gift}. Really, thank you.
You're a generous sort, walker.
Well, isn't that pleasant!
I'll think of you every time I see it.
Oh, that's sweet of you. A good gift and a good friend.
The Courtesy says guests needn't bring anything. I'm glad you did.
How lovely. It suits the sky, somehow.
That's a fine thing. Thank you, truly.
Ha! You've made me smile, walker.
Thank you. I'll keep it close.
gift.neutral: Oh. Thank you. I'm sure I'll find a use for it. Somewhere.
Hm, {gift}. That's... a thing to have. Thank you, walker.
That's kind. I don't quite know what it's for, but it's kind.
I'll put it with the other curious walker things.
I'll keep it. It's the thought that floats, as we say.
Thank you, {player}. I've never had one of these before. Or wanted one. But thank you!
Ah, {gift}. Well, thank you, I suppose. What do walkers do with it?
That's very good of you. I'll find it a corner.
A gift! It'll make a fine thing to talk about, at least.
It's not quite me, but you're very kind.
I see. It's the giving that counts, walker.
Interesting. I'll ask {friend} what to do with it.
Well, that's a surprise. Thank you, I think.
Thank you kindly. I'm sure it's very useful, somewhere on the ground.
gift.disliked: Thank you, but {gift} is a ground thing, walker. It belongs where things can fall on it safely.
That's kind of you, but I couldn't keep it up here. The sky doesn't like things that bang, burn or sink.
I'm grateful for the thought, truly. The thing itself makes my veils curl.
Thank you, but no. I'd be afraid of it every night in my nest.
You meant well, I know you did. I'll give it back, if that's all right.
That's not for Cirri, I'm afraid. It's much too much of a ground thing.
Oh, {gift}. Please don't be hurt, walker, but I'd rather not.
Things like this are how the Ruined Belltowers began: one more thing that didn't belong in the sky.
I'm sorry. I know it's meant kindly. It's just not something I can love.
Thank you for thinking of me. Next time, perhaps a peach?
That's the sort of thing we keep far away from the koi pool, walker.
Honest answer? I don't like it. But I like that you brought me something.
A {job} has no use for this, I'm afraid. Nor does a Cirri.
I'll smile and say thank you, because the Courtesy goes both ways. But I won't keep it.
Something like that, up here? Everyone would go low for a week.
That frightens me a little, if I'm honest. Could you take it back down?
You're kind to think of me. This, though... this belongs under the clouds.
I'll be honest, the way friends are. I don't care for it. I do care for you.
Not the thing for a sky-dweller, I'm afraid. Still, thank you for the thought.
Oh. Oh no. Please keep it well away from my veils.
gift.limit: No more today, walker! You'll spoil me. Save it for tomorrow.
That's enough gifts for one day. My nest is getting crowded.
One gift's a kindness; more starts to feel like a debt. Keep it for now.
You've given plenty for today. Come back with the next dawn.
Keep it for now, {player}. I've had my share of spoiling today.
No, no, I couldn't. Not another. Tomorrow, if you must.
My hands are full of your kindness already. Truly, that's enough for today.
Save some for someone else! The whole village deserves a little spoiling.
Another? You're too generous. Hold on to it until tomorrow.
The Courtesy says a host mustn't take too much. I've taken enough today.
I'd float right off under the weight of all this gladness. Tomorrow!
Enough for today, walker. I mean it kindly. Tomorrow you may spoil me again.
level_up: You know, walker, I think the wind likes you. I've decided I do too.
I think we're becoming real friends. My veils knew it before I did.
Something's shifted between us, like a wind turning warm. I like it.
Oh. I've just realised I'm always glad to see you. Always. That's new.
You've stopped being a visitor, {player}. You're one of the faces I look for now.
Every time you come, the wind between us gets a little kinder.
I told {friend} about you today. I said "my friend the walker." It felt right.
Do you feel it too? Like the air's lighter when we talk?
You're more than a guest now. The Courtesy is the least of what I owe you.
Tonight at the Evensong, I'm going to sing you into my verse. You've earned it.
We started as strangers on a bridge. Look at us now.
I used to think walkers were all heavy feet and loud voices. Then you came along.
My heart goes high when I see you on the bridge. I just thought you should know.
You've a little bit of sky in you, walker. I can tell.
A friendship's like a veil, I think: woven a thread at a time, and stronger for every thread.
Trust isn't a small thing for a Cirri to give a walker. You have mine.
When you're gone, I find myself listening for your boots on the bridges.
I'd fly a long way for you now. Further than the Wind Stone. Further than the whales.
There's a wind that only blows between friends. I think we've found it.
Oh, I'm being silly. It's only... I'm very glad we met, that's all.
You've stopped feeling like weather and started feeling like home.
I've told {partner} all about you. They say I talk about you more than the peaches.
Is this what walkers call a friend? We call it sharing a wind. Either way, that's us.
That's how a path is made in the sky, they say: by flying it again and again. You keep coming back.
I'd let you hold the end of my veil. That's a very big thing, among us.
My veils go warm at the tips when you're near. That only happens with dear ones.
A little closer, you and I. Like two clouds that drifted together and decided to stay.
Thank you for being kind to me. It's made me braver with everyone.
You matter to me, walker. I don't say that often.
The sky's the same size it always was, but somehow there's more room in it for you.
trade.open: Fair wind, customer! Veilcloth, peaches, lanterns, flutes. Look as long as you like.
Welcome to the Market Pavilion! Everything here is woven, grown or tuned in {village}.
A walker with emeralds, I hope? Come, see my wares.
Here's what the sky has to offer today. The stock's fresh with the dawn.
Buying or selling? I'll take amethyst, feathers, string, and night-moth membranes, if you've any.
Look, look! Sky lanterns, wind chimes, and a Cirrus Veil for the bold.
Welcome, {player}! Prices fair as the wind, and I won't haggle much.
Step up, step up. Everything's light enough to carry home. Mostly.
My wares, walker. The Windsong Flute's my pride. Turn it over in your hands; it won't bite.
Ah, trade! My favourite kind of conversation. Have a look.
Fresh peaches, fresh cloud, fresh-combed veilcloth. What'll it be?
Everything a walker could want from the sky, laid out for you. Take your time.
You've feathers? Bring them here; the weavers can't get enough of them.
A wind harp for your home? A sapling for your garden? Let me show you.
Come in, come in. I keep the good stock for walkers with good manners. You'll do.
gift.bring: There you are! I've been saving this for you all day. Go on, take it.
I found this and thought, that's for my walker. Here.
A little something. Don't make a fuss. Well, a small fuss.
Close your eyes. No, open them, you'll trip. Here, this is for you.
Kept out of the wind's reach, just for you. Take it before it blows off.
For you, {player}. Friends bring each other things up here. It's the rule.
Here! It's not much, but it's from me, and I couldn't wait.
I flew all the way over to give you this. Well, from the court. That's far, for a gift.
This was sitting in my nest asking to be yours. Here you are.
A present, because the sun came up again and you're still my friend. Here.
Here, take it. I picked it out thinking of your heavy, brave feet.
Found it, kept it, polished it, and now it's yours.
Don't tell {neighbour}, they'll want one too. I saved this just for you.
You looked like you needed a present. I always keep one ready, just in case.
Hold out your hands. There! That's yours now.
It's only small. But so was the first cloud, and look at the sky now.
I've been carrying this about for a light breeze, hoping you'd come. Here.
A gift from the sky to the ground. Keep it somewhere you'll see it.
Here, for you. Don't thank me; just come back tomorrow.
I thought of you, and then I thought, I should give that walker something. So: this.
evensong.invite: It's nearly dusk! Come to the Evensong, walker. Stand in the Veil Court and listen.
The harps are tuning. Will you come and hear us sing the day down?
The Evensong's starting over the Veil Court. You'll come? Please say you'll come.
Dusk, walker! Come with me. We sing the sun under the clouds every night.
Listen, the first harp. Come, the whole village is gathering.
You've never heard the Evensong properly? Then tonight's the night. Come!
Stand under us at the court, {player}, and you'll hear every voice at once.
It's the singing hour, and I won't sing it half so well without you there. Come along!
Come to the Evensong! You needn't sing. Though if you hum, nobody will mind.
The bell's rung for dusk. Over to the court with you; I'll fly ahead.
We're about to sing. Come and be part of it, walker.
I'd love you to hear our Evensong. It's the best of us, all at once.
Quick, quick, the court's filling. Come and find a good place below.
Will you come? The Evensong sounds sweeter with a friend listening.
Dusk is here. Come and hear how a sky village says goodnight.
whale.sighted: Look, look! An Old Singer! I have to go. Fair wind!
A Cloud Whale! Sorry, walker, I'm off to swim beside it!
There's a whale passing! Can you hear it humming? I must go and sing back.
Oh, a blessing! Excuse me, the Old Singer won't wait.
A whale, a whale! Come to the edge and watch. I'm flying out!
I can hear it singing! Sorry, {player}, the whale comes first. Back soon!
An Old Singer's going by, clouds on its back and all. I'm going!
Fair wind, walker! There's a whale, and I've a song to give it.
Look how slow and huge it is! I'll be back when it's passed.
It's singing the weather in! I want to hear what kind. Goodbye for now!
Oh, my veils are tingling. A Cloud Whale! Excuse me!
Everyone's flying out to it. I can't stay; I'd never forgive myself.
Watch from the bridge, walker. You'll see us swimming beside it like little fish.
The Old Singers don't pass often. I'm off. Wish me luck!
So close! The whole sky's humming with it. Fair wind, I'm away!
player.hurt: You're hurt. Oh, walker, look at you. Who let you get so scraped?
That bruise is the colour of a storm cloud. Does it ache, or only look as if it should?
Tell me it wasn't one of our bridges that did that. They're meant to be kind to guests.
A Cirri with a torn veil flies slowly for a few days. You should walk slowly for a few, too.
You look as if you lost an argument with a cliff. Did the cliff at least apologise?
Rest a breath. Nobody here will hurry you; the sky has all day.
Breathe, {player}. In with Aure, out with Vell. Slowly, slowly.
Was it the night-moths? They always go for the tired ones first.
Walkers carry every hurt on their feet. No wonder you limp. Let them rest a while.
Blood on your sleeve! Please don't drip on the veilcloth. Sorry. I mean, please be all right.
player.hungry: Your stomach just rang louder than the dawn bell. When did you last eat?
You look hollow as a reed. Eat something before Sefa blows you off the bridge.
A peach, a berry, a spoon of honey? Anything? You look as if you'd take all three.
Hungry walkers get grumpy, the Skymerchant says. I can see it starting in your eyebrows.
The Cloud Garden has peaches going soft on the branch. Go and rescue one.
You're looking at that koi as if it were supper. Please don't. It has a name.
We nibble all day long: a peach here, a sip of nectar there. Walkers seem to save it all up and then forget.
Hunger makes you heavy inside, and heavy is the last thing anyone wants to be up here.
That look! I've seen it on the children just before the Evensong honey comes round.
Honey's sweetest at noon, when the bees are warm. Go and find some. You've gone pale.
player.wet: You're dripping! Did you fly through a raincloud? Oh. You walked under one.
Rain only ever falls past us. You let it land on you? All of it?
You smell like the bottom of a cloud. Not unpleasant. Just very, very damp.
Shake yourself off like a koi after a leap. No? Only me, then.
Stand in the wind a while. Sefa would dry you in a breath; Borre would only make you shiver.
I can hear your boots squelch from here.
Is that what swimming does to a walker? You don't look as if you enjoyed it much.
Drops on your nose, drops on your sleeves. You're carrying half a cloud about.
The weavers would have you wrung out and pegged on the loom before you could argue.
Down below you only get the rain at the end of its long fall, tired and heavy. No wonder it soaks you.
player.fire: You're on fire! Roll! Walkers roll, don't they? Roll!
Smoke! There's smoke coming off you! Away from the veilcloth, please, please!
Water! Somebody fetch a bucket, the walker's burning!
Not near the Loom House! You're smouldering!
Fire is the one thing the sky fears, and you're wearing it.
You're alight! Find a puddle, find a cloud, find anything wet!
Oh, that smell. Put yourself out before the bridges catch, I beg you.
Don't come near my veils! I'm sorry, I'm sorry, but don't!
Get down and roll on the ground, you're the only one of us who can!
Your sleeve is flaming like a lantern wick, and that is not where lanterns go!
player.dark: Out under the stars without a lantern? The night-moths will find you.
It's dark, walker. Can you even see where the islands end?
This is the hour for curling up in a nest. Where's yours?
The {moon} is out, and so are you. Neither of you should be wandering.
Can walkers see in the dark? I can't, and I've had a whole life of stars to practise on.
The lanterns on the bridges are lit for you, you know. Keep to them.
Shh. Half the village is asleep over their cushions. Tread softly.
Stars above, clouds below, and you in the middle in the dark. Brave, or lost?
If you hear a whir of wings in the dark, that isn't us. Get somewhere with a roof.
You're up later than the lamplighter. That's saying something.
player.unarmored: No armour? You go about the world as soft as we fly through it.
Nothing on but cloth! You're dressed almost like one of us. Where are your veils?
You look lighter today. Did you leave all your iron somewhere?
Without your shell you look like a walker I could actually hug.
No plates, no mail. Good. Heavy things sink islands, you know.
Bare as a sparrow, and you walk about down there like that? The ground isn't kind to the soft.
You've taken off your iron. Does that mean you're staying a while?
Cloth suits you better than metal. Ask any weaver.
Unguarded and unhurried. That's how we like our guests.
All soft edges today. Mind the skeletons when you go back down.
player.diamond: That chestplate! How do you even stand up in it?
You're wearing a whole mountain on your chest. Please don't lean on the railings.
Diamond, or something darker from deeper down? Either way, far too heavy for clouds.
Look at the shine on that. The children will follow you about all day, I warn you.
All that weight, and still you came up to visit. The island creaked when you stepped on it, I swear.
You look like a treasure chest with legs. I mean that kindly.
Hard as stone and twice as heavy. I'd sink straight through the clouds in that.
The Ruined Belltowers piled on metal like that. Look what became of them.
We dodge. You just... clang. I'll never understand armour.
Splendid, grand and terrifying. Please stay off the little bridges.
player.golden: Gold! You're shining like a veil's edge at dawn.
A golden chestplate? You'll match the windkeeper's circlet.
The weavers thread a little gold through every veil. You've gone and threaded yourself.
Very grand. Very bright. Does it actually stop anything?
You look like the Lantern Spire just before dusk.
Gold is soft, you know. Pretty, but soft. Like a peach with ideas.
I could see you glinting from three islands away.
Gold on a walker! Now I've seen everything. Almost everything.
Are you off to a celebration? Or does the sun just follow you about?
Stand by the koi pool in that. They'll think you're the biggest koi that ever lived.
player.elytra: You've borrowed wings! From whom? No, don't tell me, I'll only be jealous.
A walker who borrowed wings. The oldest joke in the sky, and here it is, standing in front of me.
Those don't flap, do they? Then you fly more like us than like the birds.
Do you glide in those, or plummet with great dignity?
I'd love to see you take off. I'd love it even more to see you land.
Be gentle with those. The wind doesn't know they're borrowed.
Look at you, half a Cirri already. Now where are your veils?
They say elytra come from the end of everything, off strange ships. Did you take yours from a ship?
Wings on a walker! My old teacher would have fainted clean out of the air.
Fly with me sometime? I'll go slow. Mostly.
player.veil: You're wearing a veil! Oh, {player}. Oh, that's lovely.
A Cirrus Veil, a little crooked. No, leave it. It suits you crooked.
A walker in a veil. The children will talk of nothing else for a week.
Who wove that for you? It's good work. Better than you deserve. I'm teasing!
I think you've got it on backwards. Or forwards. Walkers have so many sides.
Mind the tips, they fray if you drag them. You do drag them. Everyone does at first.
A veil on your shoulders. Now you're one of us, or a little piece of one of us at least.
It catches the wind the way it should. Do you feel it tug, just a little, upward?
Keep your veil whole and your heart light. That was only ours to say, and now it's yours too.
I can't stop smiling. Sorry. A walker in a veil. It's just very sweet.
player.flying: You're up! You're really up! Don't look down. No, do, it's lovely.
Level, walker, fly level! Oh, you're doing it. Well flown!
Look at you, wobbling across the sky like a fledgling.
Lean into the turn, not away from it. There!
The sky's wide enough for everyone, even walkers. Especially walkers, today.
Watch the bridges! Those railings come up fast.
You fly like a dropped kite. A brave, determined dropped kite.
Is it everything you hoped? Wind in your face and nothing under your feet?
Keep moving! That's the first lesson. The second is landing, and we'll get to that.
Higher! No, not that high. Oh, now you're showing off.
player.edge: Careful! There's nothing under that edge but cloud, and cloud won't catch you.
Step back, walker. Please. My heart's in my mouth.
Don't lean! You haven't got veils!
You know how far down that is? Far enough to finish a song on the way.
The edge is where we leap from. It's where walkers fall from. Step back.
Look down if you must, but hold on to something. There's nothing to hold on to. Step back, then.
I'd catch you if you fell. I'd try. I'm not very strong. Step back anyway.
From there you can see the Wind Stone, tiny as a seed. Strange how far away it is, isn't it?
The windkeeper says walkers feel a pull at the edges. Don't listen to it.
One more step and you'd be a story the children tell. Come away from there.
player.pumpkin: Why is there a pumpkin on your head?
You've a face carved over your face. Two faces! Which one do I talk to?
Can you see out of that? It looks to me as if it would do the opposite of helping.
Hello, pumpkin. Is the walker inside well?
The children will either scream or love you. Possibly both at once.
Is this a walker festival? Do you all wear vegetables on special days?
You look like a lantern someone forgot to light.
I won't ask. I want to ask. I won't.
The tall dark ones don't like being looked in the eye, I'm told. Is that what the pumpkin's for?
Seeds in your hair, I'll bet. You'll be sprouting vines by dawn.
held.weapon: Put the blade away, please. Nobody up here has ever needed one.
That {item} looks sharp enough to cut a cloud in two.
We dodge and you swing. That's the whole difference between us, I think.
Careful near the veils! One slip and somebody's grounded for a month.
A weapon. You must have come up through some dangerous air.
The night-moths should fear that. I hope that's all it's for.
You can lower that. The only thing that bites up here is Borre.
held.pickaxe: A pickaxe! Please don't dig. The island is thinner than you'd think.
Is that for going further down? I can't imagine wanting to go further down.
Don't chip at the skystone. It's holding us all up, and it's shy about it.
A miner! You must know every colour the dark comes in.
Bring me a bit of amethyst next time you're deep? The harps love it.
That {item} looks as if it's eaten half a mountain.
You break stone for a living? Up here, everything you broke would fall on someone.
held.tool: Building something? Ask before you build on our islands, please. They're particular.
That {item} looks useful. For what, I couldn't begin to guess.
Walkers have a tool for everything. We have hands and a good wind.
Mind the skywood. The gardeners count every branch.
Busy hands! The busy ones always come back with the best stories.
You carry tools the way we carry songs: everywhere, just in case.
If that's an axe, please, please, not the peach trees.
held.fishing_rod: Fishing? Not in our koi pool, I hope!
The koi would leap right over that hook and laugh at you.
Walkers catch fish from the water. We catch songs from the wind. Both take patience.
There are no fish up here, only koi, and the koi are family.
Don't cast that near the Cloud Garden. The gardeners have very sharp eyes.
What do you catch, down there? Boots? Treasure? Bad moods?
You could fish for clouds off the bridge. You'd catch nothing, but you'd look lovely doing it.
held.map: A map! Is our village on it? Show me where we are.
Do walker maps show the sky? No? Half the world, missing.
Find {village} on that, I dare you. You'd need a map of the air.
A map is only the ground, flattened out. I'd draw the winds instead.
All those lines! Rivers? Roads? I could stare at it all morning.
How do you mark a floating island? A circle with a little cloud under it?
Is there another sky village on there? We'd love to know. We've lost touch with a few.
held.spyglass: A spyglass! Look straight up. Now straight down. Which is farther?
Point that at an Old Singer. You'll see the little clouds napping on its back.
Can you see the ground from here with that? Is it as busy as it looks?
We just fly closer. Walkers have to pull the far things in to their eyes.
Don't look at the sun with it! Even the koi know that much.
May I? Oh, oh, the bell-village below. I can see the washing on the lines!
Spyglass at the ready. Looking for something, or someone?
held.book: A book! Walkers write everything down. We just sing it until it sticks.
What's in it? Not the Evensong, I hope. That's not for paper.
Read me something. Anything. I like how walker words sound all in a row.
The wise ones say a song kept on paper forgets how to fly. I'm not sure I agree.
Did you write that? Put me in it. Put the koi in it too.
Pages flutter like little veils. Mind Borre doesn't steal them.
Your {item} looks well loved. The corners have gone soft.
held.flower: A flower, from down there? It smells like the ground. In a good way!
Is that for me? No? I'll pretend it is, just for a moment.
The gardeners will want to know where you picked that.
Flowers grow best in the Cloud Garden, but don't tell the ones below.
Drop a petal in the koi pool and watch. They think it's a treat.
A little colour in your hand. It suits you.
We sip nectar straight from the blossom, hovering. You'd need a ladder.
held.emerald: Emeralds! The Skymerchant will smell those from across the court.
Green as a peach leaf. What will you buy with it?
The merchants love a walker with emeralds. They'll sell you anything. Even a veil.
We used to trade in songs. Green stones are easier to carry, I'll admit.
Don't drop it. It's a very long way down to pick it up.
Bright as new leaves. The bell-villages below must adore you.
Put that in the Market Pavilion's hands and see what comes back.
held.diamond: A diamond! Like a bit of frozen sky.
Where do diamonds come from? Deep down? How deep? No, don't tell me.
It catches the light like dew on a veil at dawn.
That's very heavy for something so small, isn't it?
Walkers dig for days for those, I hear. All that dark for one bright thing.
Turn it toward the light. Oh. Oh, look at that.
Put it away before the children see. They'll want to hang it over the koi pool.
held.gold: Gold! The weavers thread it through our veils. Only a little; it's heavy.
Pretty, but heavy. Like all the best things from below.
Our circlets are gold, did you know? Just a thin band. You've a whole lump.
Gold catches the dusk beautifully. Bring it to the Evensong and watch.
Too much gold sank the Belltowers, the old ones say. Careful how much you bring up.
Your {item} glows like the Lantern Spire at dusk.
The Skymerchant would like a word with you and your pockets.
held.fire: Put that away! Put it away right now!
Fire? Here? Among the veilcloth and the skywood? Have you lost your mind?
Please, walker, no. Fire is the one thing the sky fears.
Take that {item} back down. Down, down, all the way down.
One spark in the Loom House and a year of weaving goes up in smoke.
My veils! Stay over there. Further. Further than that.
I don't care how careful you are. Fire doesn't care either.
held.lantern: A lantern! The lamplighter would approve. Keep it lit.
Light in your hand, like a little piece of the Lantern Spire.
A lantern is the only fire we trust, and only behind glass.
You'll be easy to find at night. Good. Walkers get lost at night.
Hang that from a bridge post and you'll be one of us.
It's warm, I can feel it from here. Like a pocket of Sefa.
held.bucket: A bucket? Of what? Not for the koi pool, please.
Walkers carry water about in tins. We just wait for a cloud.
If that's milk, don't tell me where it comes from. I've heard, and I'd rather not.
Keep that full, will you? A useful thing to have about, should anyone catch fire.
Don't empty it over the edge. Someone down there will think it's raining.
Is there a fish in there? Not one of ours, I hope. Let me count.
Carrying water up into the sky. That's like bringing a breeze to Borre.
held.food: Was that cooked? Over fire? I'll try not to think about it.
You eat sitting down, I've heard. Just sitting there, on purpose.
Smells strong. Everything walkers eat smells strong.
Your {item} smells very... sturdy. I'll keep to peaches, thank you.
Eat that up here and the crumbs will fall halfway to the ground.
Good. You should eat. You walk such a lot.
Food from below always looks so solid. Do you have to chew it for a long time?
held.peach: A sky peach! Is it ripe? Press it gently. Gently!
That's one of ours! Did a gardener give it to you, or did you pick it yourself?
Eat it in the air, if you can. They taste best with your feet off the ground. Oh. Sorry.
The best ones grow on the very top branches, where Sefa sleeps.
Don't let the koi see that. They'll sulk all afternoon.
Peach juice down your chin. That's the proper way to eat one.
A peach in a walker's hand. That's how friendships start up here.
held.treat: Something sweet! Is it for the Evensong? Everything sweet is for the Evensong.
Is that honey? Oh, please say it's honey.
The children would follow you all the way to the ground for that.
Sweets are the one thing from below I'd fly all the way down for.
You're holding a treat and talking to me as if it's nothing. Cruel.
Keep that out of Sefa's way. The south wind steals sweets; everyone knows that.
held.music: Music! Do you play it, or just carry it about hoping?
Play that {item}! Play it at the Evensong!
Walker music comes in boxes and discs. Ours comes on the wind. Both are good.
The harpists will want to hear whatever that does.
If that's a disc, does it really sing when it spins? How strange and how lovely.
Music from below always has more drum in it. I like the drum.
Careful with that horn. Loud noises frighten the koi, and the whales answer back.
held.flute: A Windsong Flute! Play something. Anything. We'll all come.
That's one of ours, from the Market Pavilion. Do you know how to hold it?
Breathe into it slowly, the way Vell comes in at dusk.
Play that and half the village flies over to listen. It's a promise and a warning.
A walker with a Windsong Flute. The harpists will be thrilled and a little jealous.
The flute sounds different from the ground, I've heard. Lower. Heavier.
You're holding it like a stick. Hold it like a bird. Lighter.
held.harp: Carrying a wind harp about! It's heavier than it looks, isn't it?
Set that down somewhere windy and it'll play itself.
A harp and no veils. That's a whole riddle in one walker.
The Hall of Echoes would want that strung tight before dusk.
Tune it to {wind}. That's who has the sky today.
Pluck one string. Just one. There, see? Everyone turned round.
Who are you going to play for? Oh, tell me it's the Evensong.
held.veil: You're holding a veil like a washcloth. It's a veil! Drape it!
A Cirrus Veil folded up in your hand. Wear it, walker. It wants the wind.
Is that for you, or for someone special? Either way, it's well made.
Shake it out. Go on. Watch how it floats.
Don't let it trail on the ground. The weavers would weep.
A walker with a veil in hand. I'd heard of it. I never quite believed it.
Put it on before you go near the edge. It'll catch you if your feet don't.
held.scale: A Sky Scale! Where did you get that? Who gave it to you?
Keep that close. It's luck, real luck. The koi don't give them up lightly.
Oh, it's a pretty one. Pink at the edge, like the dawn.
Some keep their scale for life. Some give it away. Both are right.
Lose it, and the luck goes to whoever finds it. So don't.
Carry a Sky Scale and you're a friend of the koi, whether you like it or not.
That shimmer! It changes colour when you breathe on it. Try.
held.feather: A feather! The Skymerchant buys those, you know.
From a chicken? They can't even fly. Poor feather.
Feathers are what birds have instead of veils. Clumsy, but they work.
Tickle the koi with it. They pretend to hate it.
Hold it up and let go. See how slowly it falls? That's how falling ought to feel.
A quill for writing, or a feather for luck? Down below I suppose it's both.
I keep a little jar of feathers in my nest. Don't laugh.
held.membrane: A night-moth's wing. Ugh. And also, thank you. We mend our veils with those.
You fought a night-moth? You're braver than you look.
The weavers will want that. There are always torn veils.
It smells of the night and bad dreams. Wrap it up, please.
The worst creature in the sky gives the best mending. The sky has a sense of humour.
Take that to the Market Pavilion. You'll leave richer.
Don't wave it at me! I know it's dead, but still.
held.string: String! The weavers mend veils with string and membrane.
Walkers tie everything up. We tie nothing down. Interesting, isn't it?
From a spider? Spiders spin better than our newest weavers.
A good handful. Bring it to the Loom House.
You could string a harp with that. Badly, but you could.
The children play string games in the air, upside down. You'd lose.
The Skymerchant buys string, if you're looking to part with it.
held.amethyst: Amethyst! The harpists tune by it. It sings when the wind is right.
From a geode, underground? It looks like a frozen bell.
Purple and clear, like the sky just after the Evensong.
Up here amethyst is worth more than gold. Take it to the Market Pavilion.
Tap it. Listen. Hear that little ring? That's why we love it.
So the earth makes music too, deep in its rock. I never knew.
Hold it up to {wind} and listen. Some say it hums.
held.elytra: Wings, in your hand! Put them on. Go on.
Elytra. So that's what walkers borrow. I'd always wondered.
Those came from very far away, didn't they? From the end of everything.
Folded up like a sleeping bat. Unfold them!
The weavers have always wanted a proper look at a pair. Would you show them?
So light! You'd never think they could hold a walker up.
Wings you have to carry. That's a walker idea if ever I heard one.
held.firework: Is that a firework? Put it down. Slowly. Very slowly.
No, no, no. Not here. Not anywhere, but especially not here.
Loud, dangerous and rude. Fireworks are everything the sky hates.
Gunpowder. I can smell it from here. Take it back down.
If that goes off, the koi will hide for a week and the children for two.
That {item} is going straight back down, isn't it? Say yes.
A walker set one off up here once. The bell rang by itself, and no whale came near for a season.
held.breeze: Is that wind? In your hand? Bottled up?
It's humming. It wants to be let go.
Where did you find a wind that small? Was it lonely?
Let me see. Oh, it's spinning. It's alive, in its way.
Walkers have caught the wind. I don't know how I feel about that. Amazed. Worried. Mostly amazed.
Don't throw it at me. Throw it up. Watch where it goes.
Does Borre know you have that? Don't tell Borre.
held.cloud: A piece of cloud! You're carrying a piece of cloud about!
Is it soft? It's soft. I know it's soft. Let me touch it.
That's from our Skymerchant. Don't squeeze it, it'll sulk.
Clouds are for floating on, not for keeping in your pocket.
Put it down somewhere and see if it stays. They usually do.
You're holding that cloud like a loaf of bread. It's not bread!
A little cloud of your own. Every walker should have one.
held.sapling: A sapling! Plant it somewhere with plenty of sky over it.
Skywood? It'll grow peaches one day, if you're patient.
Down on the ground, roots go into the dirt. Up here they dangle. Both are fine.
The gardeners will want to know where you're planting that.
Little tree, little tree, grow tall and stay light.
Plant it near water. Everything grows better near water, even us.
That {item} will be taller than you one day. Then you'll be the one looking up.
held.potion: What's in the bottle? It's glowing. Should it glow?
A potion! Walker magic. Is it for flying? Please say it's for flying.
Slow falling, I hope. Every walker up here should carry one.
Whatever that is, don't drink it near the edge.
That {item} looks like a thunderstorm in a bottle.
The bell-villages below have brewers, I hear. We only have honey.
Colours in a bottle. Like a sunset you can carry about.
held.totem: What a strange little doll. It's looking at me.
A totem, isn't it? A walker's way of not going up past the blue too soon.
Hold on to that. Truly. The sky is wide and the ground is hard.
I've heard of those. They bring you back. Is it true?
Green eyes and gold. It looks like it's keeping a secret.
We keep Sky Scales for luck. Walkers keep these. Yours looks stronger.
Keep it close when you're near the rim. Please.
held.pet: A lead! Where's your friend? Did you leave them on the ground?
A name tag? Who are you naming? A koi? Please let it be a koi.
A saddle! What do walkers ride? Everything?
That {item}: is it for a horse, a wolf, or something stranger?
Don't put a lead on a koi. They won't stand for it.
If you ever saddle a Cloud Whale, I want to be there to see it.
Walkers name everything. I like that. It means you remember.
remember.ground_taste_rain: Rain and dust, you said the ground tastes of. Now when it rains, I think of the ground having a drink.
Since you said the ground tastes of rain, half the village has been catching raindrops on their tongues to compare.
So the ground is where the rain goes to get dusty. Everyone's heard. It's a very good fact.
remember.ground_taste_honey: The ground tastes of honey! That's what you said, and now nobody up here can stop talking about it.
Ever since you said honey, the ground looks much more delicious from up here.
Is it still honey down there? You'd tell us if it went off, wouldn't you? It matters.
remember.walker_trick_cartwheel: Will you do the cartwheel again? Half the village wants to see a walker go round.
Someone tried your cartwheel in the air. It came out as a loop. Yours is still the best.
The ground loop! Everyone up here calls a cartwheel that now, after you.
remember.walker_trick_loop: A walker who can loop! With borrowed wings! You're the talk of the Veil Court.
Next time you bring your wings, loop over the koi pool. The koi have never seen a walker loop.
Loops are for everybody. You proved it.
remember.ground_game_hide_seek: Walker children play hide and seek too! Where do you hide down there? Behind the ground? It's still a puzzle.
We tried hide and seek the walker way, standing still behind things. It was much harder.
Every time someone hides behind a lantern, I think of walker children hiding down below.
remember.ground_game_tag: Ground tag! Someone tried playing it standing on a bridge. Nobody was any good.
Tag on the ground and tag in the sky. The same game everywhere. That makes the world feel small and friendly.
Tag! You're it! That's because you said walkers play it too.
remember.ground_game_sandcastles: Castles made of sand. I've been wondering about them since you said. How do they keep from blowing away?
Bring a sandcastle up one day. A small one. We'll keep it out of the wind.
The weavers want to know how sand stays in a castle shape. So does everyone. You started this.
remember.ground_game_skipping: Skipping stones! Everyone up here wants to try it. There's no water flat enough.
Somebody tried skipping a peach stone across a cloud. It went straight through. You'll have to show us properly.
Bounce, bounce, plop. That's how stones skip, you said. It's fun to say.
remember.koi_name_puddle: Puddle's doing well! Still small, still round. It comes up when you say its name.
You named Puddle! It's the best-named koi in the pool. The others are a little jealous.
Puddle nibbled a veil today. Very bold for something so small. You chose the name well.
remember.koi_name_captain_fin: Captain Fin is bossing the whole pool now. That's your doing.
Captain Fin swims at the front of the school every day. Born to lead, with a name like that.
Captain Fin bumped the gardener's hand for food. Very bossy. Very like its name.
remember.koi_name_peach: Little Peach is getting pinker. You picked the perfect name.
Every time anyone says "peach" by the koi pool, little Peach comes up hoping. You named it too well.
You named Peach! It's grown a whole scale since. Come and see.
remember.night_brave_yes: The walker who isn't scared of the night! You're famous in the nests for that.
When the night-moths are about, I think of you down there being brave.
Still standing up to the night monsters? Tell us if you need help. We'll sing at them.
remember.night_brave_careful: Still staying in when the night's scary? Good. Nests and walker houses are for that.
You stay inside on dark nights. So do we. That makes us neighbours, sort of.
On loud nights I think of you tucked away somewhere safe. It's nice to know.
remember.ground_pet_dog: How's your dog? Does it still run in circles? Tell it a Cirri said hello.
You've got a dog! Can it come up one day? Does it bark at clouds?
A dog was running about on the ground today. Was it yours? It looked very pleased with itself.
remember.ground_pet_cat: Is your cat well? Keep it away from the koi pool if you ever bring it up. Please.
A walker with a cat! The koi have been nervous ever since. They can tell.
Something small and furry was down on the ground today. Your cat, maybe. It didn't look up.
remember.ground_pet_horse: How's your horse? Still carrying you about? That's nearly flying, if it's fast.
You ride a horse! It must be like a very low, very bumpy flight.
Did you leave your horse by the Wind Stone? I hope someone's given it a peach.
remember.first_flight_whale: You'd swim with a whale first, you said. If an Old Singer comes by, we'll call you.
An Old Singer passed over not long ago. I thought of you wanting to swim beside one.
When you get a veil, the whales will be waiting. That's what you wanted, wasn't it?
remember.first_flight_higher: Higher than the village, you said! Up where the blue goes dark. That's a big wish.
Whenever I fly my highest, I think of you wanting to go higher still.
One day you'll fly higher than all of us. You said so, and I believe it.
remember.first_flight_show_off: Straight down to show everybody! It still makes me laugh. Fly over your house and wave.
When you get a veil, you'll go down and show off. I hope they all clap.
Showing off to the ground is the best reason to fly anyone's ever given.
remember.veil_colour_gold: Gold veils! Since you said it, every child in the village wants gold veils for their Lengthening. The weavers are not pleased.
Whenever the bell shines in the sun, I think of gold veils. That was your idea.
All gold, you said. The weavers laughed for a long time. Then they said maybe one gold thread more.
remember.veil_colour_blue: Sky-blue veils, to vanish into the sky! The children practise vanishing every day now. It isn't working yet.
Still the sky-blue plan! The weavers say "we'll see." That's very nearly a yes.
Sky blue all the way. I look up and think how good that would look.
remember.veil_colour_night: Night-coloured veils with stars in! Somebody dreams about them every night now. You started that.
Every night I look up and pick which stars should go on the veils you said.
Veils with stars! The weavers want to know whose idea that was. A walker's, I told them.
remember.walker_age_grown: A grown-up who plays! That's the best kind. Will you play today?
A grown-up walker. Everybody forgets, because you don't act like one. That's meant nicely.
Nobody believed you were a grown-up. You'll have to act grown-up for a bit. Not too long.
remember.walker_age_big_child: A big child! Then you're one of us. Come and play before the bell.
You said you're a big child. That's why you're so much fun.
Big child, little child, grown-up: we're all children at the koi pool.
remember.walker_secret_pickaxe: Does your pickaxe still talk back? I said fair wind to it last time. It didn't answer. Shy, maybe.
Your secret's safe. Mostly. Everyone knows you talk to your pickaxe, but only nicely.
If your pickaxe ever says anything about the sky, tell us. We'd like to know what pickaxes think.
remember.walker_secret_spiders: No spiders up here, you'll be glad to know. Too windy for webs. You're safe in the sky.
Scared of spiders! That's all right. Everybody's scared of something small. And something big.
If a spider ever comes up the Wind Stone, we'll blow it straight back down for you.
remember.walker_secret_lost: Lost for days on the ground! Do you know where you are now? You're here. Good.
Up here nobody ever gets lost for long. You just go up and look. Remember that, after what you told us.
Since you told us about being lost, I've been thinking walkers need a Lantern Spire in every valley.
remember.lengthening_gift_peaches: A whole basket of peaches for a Lengthening! You promised. Nobody has forgotten.
The peach trees are filling up nicely. Ready for that basket you promised.
Peaches for the Lengthening! That's the right present. You understand us.
remember.lengthening_gift_diamond: A diamond for a Lengthening! The weavers say it's too heavy for a veil. They also say they'd like to see it.
You promised a diamond! Everyone's heard. It'll be the shiniest Lengthening there's ever been.
Is the diamond still coming? It can sit on a cushion. Cushions are good at holding heavy things.
remember.lengthening_gift_song: A walker song for a Lengthening! Have you been practising? It's all anyone talks about at the koi pool.
You'll sing at the Lengthening. You said. The harpists want to learn it first.
I hum a bit of nothing sometimes and pretend it's the walker song you promised.
remember.lengthening_gift_myself: You'll come to the Lengthening yourself. You promised. That's the best present, and everyone knows it.
A walker at a Lengthening! Nobody can remember there ever being one. You'll be the first.
There'll be a place saved for you at the Lengthening. Right at the front, where you can see.
remember.walker_lessons_letters: Letters and numbers! Can you show me how walkers write fair wind? I'd like to see it.
Since you said walkers learn numbers too, the counting at the koi pool has got very serious.
Do walker letters look like ours? Draw one in the dust on the bridge. Go on.
remember.walker_lessons_building: You learned to build! Will you build something up here one day? Something light, mind.
A walker who builds. Everyone up here wants to watch, as long as you don't use stone.
Build us a tiny bridge, builder. Just a little one. For the koi.
remember.walker_lessons_monsters: Monster lessons! Everyone up here thinks walker lessons are the bravest lessons in the world.
You learned to face monsters. That's why you came up the Wind Stone without shaking. Well, much.
Do you still remember your monster lessons? Good. We only learned humming. It works on thunder.
remember.scale_wish_peaches: A house full of peaches! Every time a peach falls, I think of your wish.
Have you found a Sky Scale yet? Your house full of peaches is waiting.
If anyone up here finds a Sky Scale, we'll wish your peach house for you. That's a promise.
remember.scale_wish_whale: A whale of your own! Every time an Old Singer passes, I wonder if it's yours.
A whale's too big to keep, you know. You'd have to keep the whole sky as well.
When the next whale comes, I'll tell it you'd like one. It might hum yes.
remember.scale_wish_more_wishes: A hundred more wishes! Everyone's been trying it on their Sky Scales since you said. Nobody knows if it worked.
Still the cleverest wish anyone's ever made. A hundred more! Ha!
If I ever find a Sky Scale, I'm doing your wish. A hundred more wishes. Then I'll think of the rest.
remember.sky_end_never: The sky never ends, you said. So there's always further to fly. I like knowing that.
I flew up as high as I dared and thought of you. It kept going, just like you said.
If the sky never ends, there's room for everyone. You were right, and so was the old saying.
remember.sky_end_stars: The sky ends at the stars, you said. Every night now I look at the edge of the sky.
Stars like lanterns at the end of a bridge. Everyone up here says it now. You started it.
If the stars are the edge, the moon must be the door. I've been thinking about it.
remember.sky_end_the_end: A place called the End! Is it really where the sky stops? What's after the End?
Everyone's been talking about the End you told us of. Nobody wants to go. Everybody wants to hear about it.
If you go back to the End, wave. We'll be at the other end. The beginning, I suppose.
remember.home_built: You built your own house, you said. I keep picturing it. Is there a window that faces up?
I told the weavers you built your home with your own hands. They asked if it sways in the wind. I said houses don't. They didn't believe me.
A walker who builds! If you ever build anything up here, ask the skystone nicely first.
Every time I pass the Loom House I think of your house, the one you made stone by stone.
remember.home_wanderer: Where did night find you last, wanderer? Somewhere with a good view of us, I hope.
You sleep wherever the night catches you. Borre does the same, and nobody minds Borre. Much.
I thought of you at dusk, out there somewhere with no nest. Then I thought: no, the whole world is your nest. Better.
A wanderer like you should have one place to come back to. {village} volunteers.
remember.home_burrow: Still living in your hill? I dreamt about it. There were roots in my hair and I woke up shouting.
You live inside the ground. I told the children. They think you're the bravest walker alive.
How is your hole in the hill? Do you ever poke your head out and look up for us?
I tried to imagine sleeping under all that dirt. I had to go and hover in the open for a while afterwards.
remember.home_sky: You said you'd live up here, if we'd have you. We've been talking it over. We'd have you.
Have you thought any more about a nest in {village}? The weavers already have opinions about cushions.
Every evening I look round the Veil Court and count you in. You're one of ours now; you said so.
Up here, you said. I haven't stopped smiling about it, {player}.
remember.fell_often: Still falling off things? You've a look about you today. A wobbly look.
More falls than you can count, you said. I've been counting the edges near the Lift Dock, just in case.
Keep away from the rim today. I won't say why. You know why.
You've fallen so often, and still you climb. I've decided that's the most admirable thing about walkers.
remember.fell_once: You fell once, you told me. I think about it whenever I see you near the bridges.
Once is enough, you said. I agree. Let's keep it at once.
Did it hurt, that fall of yours? You don't have to say. I only wondered, at dusk.
I flew past the place under the rim where a walker would land, if one fell. I'm glad it's empty.
remember.trait_careful: Careful as ever? Good. Keep it up. I like having you around.
You told me you're careful. I've been watching. You are! You tested every bridge plank with your toe.
The careful ones come back. That's why you keep coming back, I think.
I told the windkeeper you're the careful sort. They were very relieved. You'd be surprised how many walkers aren't.
remember.dreams_falling: Dreamed of falling again? Next time, turn it into flying at the very last moment. We do.
You fall in your dreams, you said. I hummed something toward the ground last night, in case it helps.
The wise ones say a falling dream means you're about to rise. I hope they're right about you.
Sleep well tonight. No falling. That's an order from the sky.
remember.likes_aure: Aure's your wind, you said. I felt dew on my veils this morning and thought, that's the walker's wind.
{wind} has the sky today, but Aure will be back. Aure always comes back for its friends.
Did you feel Aure at dawn? Soft as a whisper. I said good morning to it from both of us.
When Aure has the sky, I'll fly past your way and wave. I promise.
remember.likes_sefa: Sefa's your wind, you said. Lazy, warm and smelling of peaches. That explains a lot about you.
When Sefa has the sky I nap in the air and think, the walker would approve.
I asked Sefa to blow your way. It didn't hurry, but it said yes. Probably.
Warm afternoon, slow clouds, peaches ripening. Your wind's kind of day.
remember.likes_vell: Vell's your wind! It'll carry the Evensong to you tonight, wherever you are.
You picked Vell, the singing wind. I sing a little louder when it blows now, so it has something of mine to bring you.
When Vell comes in at dusk I always think: there goes the walker's wind, right on time.
I asked the harpists to tune to Vell this evening. I didn't tell them it was for you.
remember.likes_borre: Borre's your wind, you said. Cold and wild. I still don't understand you, and I like that.
When Borre howls round the bell at night now, I think: somewhere down there, the walker is smiling.
Next time Borre has the sky, I'm staying in my nest and you're doing the waving.
I told Borre it had a friend now. It didn't answer, but the bell rang once all by itself.
remember.dreams_flying: Did you dream of flying again? Tell me where you went this time.
You dream of flying every night. Then some nights, I think, you must fly right past my nest.
I've been dreaming of walking since you told me your dreams. Fair is fair. It's very bumpy.
Every time you sleep, you come up here a little. That's what you told me. I keep it like a Sky Scale.
remember.dreams_digging: Still digging in your sleep? Find anything good down there?
You dream of digging. I dream of rising. Between us we cover the whole world.
I told the wise one about your digging dreams. They laughed so hard they drifted into a bridge.
Last night I dreamed I had a pickaxe. I woke up very confused, and it's all your fault.
remember.ground_caves: Glowing caves under the ground. I still think about them. Upside-down skies, full of lights.
You told me about the glowing caves. I told the children. Now they want to dig, and I'm in trouble.
Are the caves still glowing down there? Bring me a little of that light someday, if it can be carried.
When I look at the stars now I think: somewhere under the walker's feet, there's another sky, buried.
remember.ground_ruins: Old ruins under the ground, you said. Like our Belltowers, only sunk the other way. I can't stop thinking about it.
Who built the ruins down there, do you think? Did they grow too heavy too?
You told me about the bones and old stones under the ground. I think the ground remembers more than we do.
If you ever find a ruin with a bell in it, tell me. I'll want to sing it something.
remember.ground_warden: That thing in the deep that listens. I keep thinking about it. Can it hear us singing?
You told me about the listener in the dark. I've been humming more quietly ever since. Silly of me.
Promise me you'll stay away from the thing that listens.
I asked the wise one about your listener in the dark. They went very quiet and said some things are better left below.
remember.nest_shared: Is someone keeping your nest warm while you're up here? Tell them a Cirri says fair wind.
You've someone waiting at home, you said. Don't stay too late on their account.
I hope the one in your nest knows how far you walk every day. Somebody ought to rub your feet.
Bring them up someday, the one you share a nest with. We'd like to meet them.
remember.nest_alone: A nest for one, you said. Then you're welcome in ours whenever you like. Bring nothing; we've cushions.
Still nesting alone? I hope it's quiet in the good way, not the heavy way.
Your nest is all yours. Some mornings, with the whole village singing at dawn, I envy that.
You like your nest just for you. I understand. The sky is lovely alone too, sometimes.
remember.nest_cat: How's your cat? Still keeping your nest? Tell it the koi say hello. Well. They don't. But I do.
You've a cat at home, you said. I've been trying to imagine a cat in the sky. It would hate every minute.
Does your cat miss you when you come up here? I'll bet it pretends not to.
Bring your cat up someday. No! Don't. The koi. Forget I said anything.
remember.wants_veil: You'd love a veil, you said. I mentioned it at the Loom House. Nobody said no!
Still wanting veils? I can picture them on you. Sky blue at the shoulders, rose at the tips.
The weavers asked about you. Your height, your shoulders, whether you'd hold still for a fitting. I said probably not.
One day you'll feel the wind take your veils and lift. I hope I'm there when it happens.
remember.fears_heights: Scared of heights, and still you come up. I think of that every time I see you on a bridge.
Don't look down today. Look at me instead. That's what we tell the little ones.
Heights frighten you, you told me. I've been flying a little lower near you. Did you notice?
Everyone's afraid of the drop at first. Even us. It goes, slowly. It goes.
remember.likes_puffy: Plenty of puffy clouds below us today. Look, there's one shaped like a sleeping goat.
I flew over a whole field of puffy clouds this morning and thought of you somewhere under them.
The big puffy ones, you said. From up here they look like cushions you could fall into. Don't.
A fat white cloud drifted under the Veil Court at noon. I waved at it on your behalf.
remember.likes_wispy: Wispy clouds, you said. Our veils are made of them. You've loved us without knowing it.
The weavers combed cirrus at dawn today, your favourite kind. I saved you a wisp. Here, it's gone. They do that.
Look up when you go back down. The thin high clouds will be the same ones on my veils.
I told the Loom House a walker loves cirrus best. They were so pleased they forgot to scold me for being late.
remember.likes_storms: You and your storms. Next time Borre grumbles, go and enjoy it, from somewhere with a roof.
When the bell rings for a storm now, I picture you excited. I'll be in my nest, humming.
I don't understand storm-lovers, but I've decided to like one anyway.
Next time the thunder comes, I'll think of you out there grinning at it, and be a little less afraid.
remember.likes_rain: You love the rain, you said. Every drop that falls past my nest now, I send down to you.
When rain falls past us, I lean over and watch it go and hope it lands on you gently.
I watched a raincloud drift toward the ground today and thought, that one's for the walker.
Rain-lover. I've started to think the rain must be glad, too, to land on someone who wants it.
remember.dislikes_rain: If it rains below today, I'm sorry. I know you'd rather it didn't.
Just wet, you said. I laughed for a whole afternoon. I still do, whenever it rains.
If you hate the rain, come up here. It only ever falls away from us.
I'd blow the rainclouds away from you, if I were a wind. I'm only a Cirri.
remember.likes_cats: A cat lover. I've been keeping you away from the koi pool. Just in case.
I saw a cat on a roof in the bell-village today. It looked up at me as if it owned the sky.
You and your cats. The koi have heard. They're being very polite to you, out of fear.
Do cats ever look up at the clouds? If one does, it's thinking of us. Tell it I said so.
remember.likes_koi: Go and visit the koi pool. The gardeners say the koi have been looking for you.
One of the koi shed a scale this morning. I'd like to think it was showing off for you.
I told the koi what you said about them. I swear the big golden one winked.
A koi lover! They've been leaping higher since you came. Coincidence? The koi say no.
remember.likes_parrots: Parrots, you said! I saw one far below today, red as a lantern. It was shouting. Your sort of bird.
Teach a parrot to say fair wind and bring it up. I'll do anything. Anything.
A bird that talks back. I still can't believe it. I've been talking to the sparrows. Nothing.
You like parrots. Is it because they fly, or because they talk? I think I know which I'd pick.
remember.feet_tired: Are your feet tired today? You told me they get tired every evening. Put them up somewhere.
I've been thinking about your poor feet. Do they ever get a day off?
Rest your feet before you go down. There's a bench by the Cloud Garden, just for walkers.
Every time I see you stomp across a bridge I think, oh, those tired feet.
remember.likes_horses: Walkers that carry walkers. I still think horses are the cleverest thing on the ground.
Did you ride up today? No, of course not. The horse would hate the Wind Stone. Poor horse.
I saw horses running far below. Their manes streamed like little veils. You were right about them.
You love horses, you said. I'd love to see one try a bridge. Just once. From a safe height.
remember.fears_creepers: Watch out for the green hissing ones when you go down. You told me about them. I haven't forgotten.
Creepers, you said. I've added them to my list of rude things, between fireworks and thunder.
Keep your eyes open below. I don't want any of those bursting near you.
No creepers up here. None at all. This is the one place you can stop listening for the hiss.
remember.fears_dark: When it gets dark, take a lantern, or stay near our lights. You said you don't like the dark.
Our nights have stars. Yours have walls. I think about that every time the lamplighter starts on the bridges.
The dark scares you, you told me. That's why I leave the lantern by the dock burning a little longer.
If the dark gets to you down below, look up. The {moon} is ours too.
remember.likes_dawn: Did you see the dawn this morning? Pink and gold all the way to the edge. Your hour, you said.
The bell rang at dawn and I thought, the walker's awake for this, I hope.
You love the dawn. Come up early one day and watch it with me from the Bell Pagoda.
This world has seen {day} dawns, the bellkeeper says. I hope you watched a few of them for me.
remember.likes_evensong: You'll come to the Evensong tonight, won't you? Dusk is your favourite.
You said the Evensong was the sky at its best. I sang the last verse for you yesterday.
Stay for the Evensong. It's better when someone who loves it is listening.
I thought I saw you by the Veil Court at dusk. I can't be sure. I was singing with my eyes closed.
remember.likes_stars: Your sort of night tonight, I hope: clear, with every star out.
You love the stars. I counted them for you last night. I lost count over the koi pool.
The stars are closer up here. Not much, but a little. Come and see.
Did you look up last night? I was looking at the same star. Probably. There are a lot of them.
remember.heard_evensong: You hear the Evensong from down below. I sing it toward the edge now, so it falls your way.
Tonight, when we sing the day down, listen. One voice a little louder than the rest? Me.
All this time we've been singing to the ground and never knew anyone heard. Thank you for telling me.
Did you hear us last night? Vell was carrying it well, I thought.
remember.wants_evensong: You've never heard the Evensong. Tonight, then. Be at the Veil Court when the lanterns light.
Still haven't heard it? Walker! It's every single dusk!
I've told the harpists a walker is coming to hear the Evensong. They've been practising extra.
When you finally hear us sing the day down, tell me how it sounds from where you stand.
remember.likes_peaches: The peaches are ripe on the top branches. Go, before the koi get there.
I saved you a peach. Well, I meant to. It was very ripe. I'm sorry.
Peach-lover! The gardener says this week's are the sweetest yet.
I can always tell a walker who loves sky peaches. They smile at the trees.
remember.likes_bread: Bread. You still like bread better than peaches. I've decided to forgive you.
I asked the Skymerchant about bread. They looked at me as if I'd asked for a firework.
Is bread better with honey? Tell me it's better with honey. Then I'll consider it.
I've been trying to imagine bread. Is it like a cloud you can eat? That's what I'm going with.
remember.cooks_fire: Still cooking over fire? Every day? On purpose? I still lie awake over it.
You smell faintly of smoke today. I won't say anything. I've said something. Sorry.
Fire, every day, and it tastes better, you said. I believe you. I'll never try it.
Keep your cooking fires far from here, please. I know you would. I just like saying it.
remember.cooks_never: Fruit-eater! No fire for you. You're practically one of us.
You don't cook. I tell everyone. The weavers want to adopt you.
Peaches, berries, honey and no flames. You eat like a Cirri. Now you only need to eat in the air.
I picked some berries this morning thinking, the walker would like these. You would, wouldn't you?
remember.told_chickens: Birds that can't fly. I still can't stop thinking about the chickens. Who did that to them?
I told the children about the chickens. One of them cried. Another wants to give them lessons.
Do the chickens at least try? Do they hop? Tell me they hop.
I sang a little song for the chickens at the Evensong. Nobody knew why. I knew why.
remember.lucky_scale: Have you still got your Sky Scale? Keep it near your heart, not in your boot.
Someone up here trusted you with their luck. I'm glad it was you.
I like to think your Sky Scale catches the light even down there, under the clouds.
The koi that shed your scale is still in the pool. I think it remembers you.
remember.lucky_totem: Still carrying your little totem? Good. I sleep better knowing you've got it.
That totem of yours. I hope you never need it. I hope it's very, very bored.
A doll that brings walkers back. I told the wise one. They said every people has its own way of hoping.
Mind the rim today. You've your totem, but I'd rather you never found out if it works.
remember.likes_windstone: The Wind Stone hummed when you came up. I think it's fond of you.
You said you'd rather a Wind Stone than stairs. The windkeeper heard. They've been glowing all week.
The first windkeepers would be so pleased to hear a walker loves their stones. I'm pleased for them.
Every time someone rides the wind up, I think of you and the face you'd make.
remember.travel_far: Past the edge of every map! Where did your feet take you this time?
You've walked farther than most winds blow. Tell me something you saw. Anything.
Restless feet, restless heart. You and our restless ones would talk all night.
When you go past the maps again, look up. There may be a village up there no walker's ever seen.
remember.travel_end: The End and back. I still think about it. What does nothing look like?
You've been to the end of everything. Is there a sky there? Does it have winds?
I told the wise one you've been to the End. They said, then the walker knows how far home is. I think I understand now.
Going back to the End? If you do, come back again. That's the important part.
remember.travel_nether: The land of fire. You went there and came back. I check your sleeves for sparks every time I see you.
Never go back to that burning place. Or, if you must, tell me first, so I can worry properly.
You smell of nothing today. Good. No fire, no smoke. Just walker.
I dreamed of your fire land last night. I woke up and flew straight to the koi pool, just to be near water.
remember.sleeps_stars: Sleeping under the stars again tonight? Then we'll share a sky. You at the bottom, me at the top.
You sleep with nothing over you, like us. I like that very much.
If you sleep out tonight, find the brightest star over the clouds. I'll be curled up just under it.
Out under the stars again? Keep a lantern by you, for the night-moths.
remember.sleeps_little: Did you sleep? Tell me you slept. You've the face of someone the night-moths are watching.
You told me you hardly sleep. Go to bed tonight, walker. For me. For the sky.
I hummed a lullaby at dusk and thought, that one's for the walker who won't sleep.
The night-moths come for the sleepless, the old ones say. I believe them. Please rest.
remember.seen_whale: You've heard an Old Singer. I can tell, now that I know. You listen to the sky differently.
A whale crossed the high sky this morning. I wondered if it was the one that sang to you.
Not everyone is blessed by a whale. You are. Remember that on heavy days.
Hum me what the whale sang to you? No? Too private? I understand. Some songs are.
remember.wants_whale: Still waiting to meet an Old Singer properly? Watch the high sky. They come when you stop looking.
If a whale passes today, I'll come and find you. I'll drag you to the edge myself.
I asked the windkeeper when the next whale might come. They said: when the clouds ask for one.
One day you'll be close enough to hear a whale sing. Then you'll understand why we're all a little odd.
remember.plays_flute: Have you practised your flute? You said you play a little. I want to hear the little.
A walker with a flute! Come and play at the Evensong sometime. The harpists won't mind. Much.
Breathe from low down when you play. That's the secret. Vell taught me that, in a way.
I bought you a Windsong Flute from the Skymerchant. In my head. I'm still saving up for the real one.
remember.plays_noteblocks: How are your singing boxes? The note blocks? I still laugh about hitting a box to make music.
Bring a note block up someday and play it in the Hall of Echoes. The harps will sulk.
I tapped a block of skystone to see if it would sing. It didn't. I'm not sure what I expected.
Walker music, made by thumping. I've decided I love it.
remember.plays_hum: Hum me something? You said you hum. I'll hum the harmony.
I heard someone humming on the bridge this morning and hoped it was you.
A hummer! Every song starts with one of you. Remember that.
The harpists say humming is the oldest music in the sky. You're older than you look, then.
remember.trait_fearless: Not afraid of heights at all, you said. Then come up to the top of the Lantern Spire with me sometime.
Fearless walker! The windkeeper wants to see you lean over the dock. I said no. Please don't.
I keep forgetting you're not afraid. Then I see you strolling the bridges like a Cirri.
A brave stomach and sturdy feet. If you ever get veils, you'll be dangerous.
remember.flower_poppy: You'd bring a friend a poppy, you said. I found one by the koi pool and thought of you.
The gardener planted a row of poppies. Nobody knows why. I know why.
Bright as a lantern and not a bit shy. That's how I think of you and your poppies.
I tucked a poppy petal in my sash today. Don't tell anyone it's for you.
remember.flower_cornflower: Cornflowers! The gardener's been unbearable ever since you said it. There's a whole blue bed now.
A cornflower is the colour of a veil at the root. Did you know that when you chose it?
I wore a cornflower behind my ear today. I don't know why I'm telling you. Yes I do.
A sky-blue flower, chosen by a walker. You'd fit right in up here.
remember.flower_lily: Lily of the valley, you said. The bellkeeper wants to plant some round the bell now.
Little white bells on a stem. I think of them every dawn, when the big bell rings.
The lilies by the Cloud Garden bloomed this week. I'd have picked you one, but they're so small.
Lily of the valley for a friend. That's such a quiet, kind choice. Like you.
remember.food_eggs: Eggs for breakfast, you said. I still haven't told the birds. I'm keeping your secret.
Did you eat eggs this morning? You've the look of someone who did. I forgive you.
A bird flew past and I couldn't look it in the eye. That's your fault, egg-eater.
I can't stop thinking about cooked eggs. In a pan. On a fire. I need to go and lie down in the air.
remember.food_honey: Honey-lover! I saved a little comb for you. It's sticky. Sorry.
The bees are warm today. Good honey weather, I thought, and then I thought of you.
You and me and honey. We should share some one morning, in the air.
Ever since you told me, I think of you every time I lick a sticky finger.
remember.food_stew: Stew in the morning! I told the weavers. One of them dropped a whole comb of cirrus.
Still eating stew at dawn? No wonder your feet are so heavy.
How do you even lift a spoon of stew that early? I'd sink straight through the clouds.
You smell a little like a cooking pot today. A good pot, I'm sure.
remember.wishes_stars: Did you wish on a star last night? What for? No, don't tell me, or it won't come true.
The stars were out thick last night. Your wishes must be piling up somewhere.
The stars know your voice by now, you wish so often. I hope they're listening.
If you see a bright one tonight, wish for something for me too.
remember.wishes_koi: Have you wished on a koi yet? Pick a plump one; they listen better. Still true.
I saw you by the koi pool, moving your lips. A wish, was it? Good.
I made a wish on the koi for you. Don't ask what. A kind one.
A koi leapt clean out of the pool this morning. Somebody's wish came true, I think. Was it yours?
remember.friend_dog: How's your dog? Still running in circles? Give it a scratch from me.
I saw a dog far below today, running after nothing at all. I hoped it was yours.
Your dog would bark at us, I think, if it saw us flying. Tell it we're friends.
A dog for a dearest friend. You must be a good walker. Dogs know.
remember.friend_villager: One of the bell-village folk is your dearest friend, you said. Do they ever look up and wave?
I flew low over the bell-village this morning. Someone waved. Was it your friend?
Tell your friend down below that the Cirri say fair wind.
Next time you visit your friend, take them a peach from us. They've never had one, I'll bet.
remember.friend_cirri: You said I might be your dearest friend. I've been flying higher ever since, {player}.
Dearest friend. I keep saying it to myself. It sounds better every time.
I told {friend} you named me your dearest friend. They were jealous. I was smug.
A walker's dearest friend is a Cirri. Me. I'll try to deserve it.
remember.likes_sky: Sky-lover. You've got cloud in your lungs now. It never comes out.
You belong up here. You as good as said so, and the sky heard.
The ground can have you back when it asks nicely. It hasn't asked.
The weavers took what you said about the sky as a promise. Careful, or they'll start on your veils.
remember.misses_ground: Do your feet still miss the ground? Tell them it's not far. Just a long way down.
I found a patch of grass on the islet by the Lantern Spire. Your feet might like it.
Your feet miss the ground. I've been trying to find them a job up here. Bridge-testing?
Go and see the ground for a while, if you need to. Then come back. The sky is patient.
remember.felt_heavy: How's your heart today? Lighter, I hope. You told me it gets heavy.
I keep thinking of what you said about heavy days. When one comes, come up here. Nothing weighs much up here.
The Evensong last night was for everyone carrying something. I sang it for you, a little.
You don't have to talk about it. Just float about with me a while. Stand. Walk. Whatever it is you do.
remember.felt_light: Not heavy since you came up here, you said. I've told nobody. I've told everybody. Sorry.
Light as a veil today? I hope so. You deserve light days.
You said the sky lifted something off you. That's the best thing anyone's ever said about {village}.
Keep coming up, then. Whatever weighs on you can wait at the bottom of the Wind Stone.
remember.fly_here: Wings for a day, and you'd fly straight to me, you said. I'm still waiting, you know.
If you ever find wings, remember your promise. Straight up. No detours.
I keep a cushion ready in case a walker comes flying in one day. Just in case.
Straight up to me. I think about that more than I should.
remember.fly_ocean: Over the ocean, you said, if you had wings. I flew to the edge of the clouds today and saw blue. Was that it?
The ocean must be wonderful, if a walker with wings would pick it first.
Is the ocean bigger than the sky? You'd know. You chose it.
Glide over the ocean one day and wave up. We'll be up here somewhere.
remember.sings_lullabies: You sing lullabies, you said. Sing one tonight? The children here would listen.
I hummed a walker lullaby to a child today. I made it up. I think it was walkerish.
Walkers and Cirri both sing the little ones to sleep. I've been thinking about that all week.
Teach me a lullaby from below someday. I'll teach you one from up here.
remember.sings_loud: Loud and badly! Come and sing at the Evensong. We could use more of that.
I sang loud and badly this morning, in your honour. The bellkeeper was not amused.
