Smell that? Peaches. Sefa always smells of peaches, even when there isn't one for miles.
Nothing gets done on a Sefa day. The wind's too warm, the honey's too sweet, and everyone's half asleep in the air.
Up from the south comes Sefa, with far-off warmth in it. Today I can smell flowers I've never seen.
My veils hang slack and lovely in Sefa. They don't stream, they float, like weed in a warm pond.
The bees love Sefa. The whole Cloud Garden is humming louder than the harps.
A Sefa day is a gift wrapped in a yawn.
Here's Sefa, dropping in for a light breeze and staying till dark, full of long stories about the south.
Try going anywhere in a hurry on a Sefa day. Go on. Sefa will just turn you round and nudge you toward a nap.
The peaches ripen faster when Sefa blows. The gardeners pick twice as often and grumble the whole time, with their mouths full.
Even the Market Pavilion slows down in Sefa. Walkers arrive, sigh, and forget what they came up to buy.
Sefa makes the whales lazy too. If one passes today, it'll be slow enough to swim beside all afternoon.
Warm wind, warm skystone, warm honey. Sefa days stick to you.
{wind} again! I think it likes us. I think it likes everyone, which is very Sefa.
Sefa carries sound slowly. A laugh from the Veil Court takes its time reaching you, and it arrives all soft round the edges.
wind.vell: Vell has the sky today, the west wind, the song-carrier. Listen: there's singing on it from somewhere too far to see.
Flying in Vell is steady work. It doesn't push and it doesn't drop you. It just goes, all day, like one long note.
On a Vell day the harps play themselves. The harpists only have to keep up.
Vell carries everything: songs, voices, gossip. Say something unkind on a Vell day and three villages will hear it by dusk.
Vell blows out of the sunset. Even at noon it smells a little of evening.
Some days Vell brings a song I almost know. I hum along and lose it halfway, every time.
The Evensong sounds best in Vell. It takes our last note and keeps it going long after we've stopped.
A wistful wind, Vell. It makes everyone think of old friends. I've been thinking of mine all day.
Like an old gossip, Vell brings news from the far side of the sky and never quite gets it right.
When Vell blows, the chimes ring in long rounds, one after another down the bridges, as if they're passing a message along.
Fly with Vell at your back and you'll go east all day without trying. Fly against it and you'll learn some patience.
If an Old Singer is anywhere in this sky today, Vell will bring us its song. Keep your ears open.
Every Cirri child learns to sing in Vell. It holds the note for you when your breath runs out.
With {wind} blowing, every veil in the village streams east together, like a flock that's agreed on something.
Vell's the wind for goodbyes. Whatever you send off on it, a song or a wish or a sigh, it carries gently.
wind.borre: Borre has the sky today, cold and sharp out of the north. My veils keep cracking like flags.
Flying in Borre is hard work. Every gust wants to throw you somewhere you never meant to go.
Borre's air is clean. You can see further on a Borre day than any other. You can also lose your nose to it.
On Borre days somebody is always watching the north, and the bell rope is never far from a hand.
Little veils and a big wind don't mix, so the children are kept close to the nests till Borre moves on.
Borre has no manners, but it never lies. If a storm is coming, Borre tells you first, and loudly.
My cheeks are stinging. Borre's been slapping them all day. It must be fond of me.
I like Borre, mostly. It blows the haze off and the whole world comes up sharp and blue, all the way to the edge.
Walkers who come up on a Borre day arrive at the dock holding their hats and their dignity, and usually only one of them.
Borre is the neighbour who flings the door open, shouts the news and leaves. You're glad of the news. You're glad when it goes.
Keep your veils tight today. Give Borre one loose end and it'll have you mending till the next new moon.
Everyone flies low and close in Borre, in each other's lee. It's the friendliest a village ever gets: we're all hiding behind each other.
The harps don't play in Borre. They argue.
Borre brings the cold lands with it. Even when it isn't snowing, it smells of stone and ice.
Never trust a still day, the old ones say. With {wind} howling round the bridges, I'd trade a peach for one.
routine.work: You caught me mid-task. My hands keep going even when my head turns, so don't mind them.
Work's going well today. That always makes me suspicious.
I've been at my spot since the bell. Talking to you counts as a rest, doesn't it?
I like work you can see when it's done. At the end of the day you can point at it and say, that's mine.
Busy, busy. But there's always a breath of wind for a walker.
My teacher used to say: work as if the whole sky were watching. Up here it usually is.
I've done the hard part. Now I'm on the part that looks easy and isn't.
Sore hands, full head, high heart. That's a good working day.
Work was slow this morning, so I've been doing it twice as carefully. Don't tell anyone, they'll expect it every day.
You're welcome to watch, walker. Most walkers find it very dull, and then stay an hour.
I was just thinking I'd earned a peach. Then a walker came up. Better than a peach. Nearly.
{coworker} and I have been at it since dawn. We stopped talking hours ago. That's how you know it's going well.
Everyone in {village} has their part, and mine was just going rather nicely. Never mind. It'll keep.
Somebody's always needing something. Today it's been everybody, all at once.
A Cirri works light. Pile too much into one day and the whole village sinks; ask the old belltowers. So: a little work, a little song.
routine.gather: I was just over the Veil Court with the others, trading news. You came up in the middle of a very good story.
Half the village is hovering round the court right now. You can't hear yourself think, and that's rather the point.
{neighbour} was telling everyone about a whale they saw. It gets bigger every time it's told.
The court's the place to hear everything: who's mended what, whose peaches are ripe, who's sweet on whom.
We all just drifted together over the court like leaves in an eddy. Nobody planned it. Nobody ever does.
I wasn't really in the gathering. I hover at the edge and listen. It's the best spot. Nobody asks you anything.
A walker at the court! Now there'll be something to talk about. Don't worry, it'll be kind. Mostly.
We were arguing about whether Sefa or Aure is the better wind for napping. It's an old argument. Nobody ever wins it.
Gathering is what we do between doing things. I think it might be the most important thing we do.
Someone brought honey to the court and now everyone's sticky and happy. Mind my veils.
We were just deciding who should go and meet the next walker. And here you are, and I'm closest. Hello!
My favourite part of a gathering is the quiet bit at the end, when everyone's said their news and we just hover together.
I came to the court for a light breeze and I've been here half the day. That's how the court gets you.
You can tell the mood of {village} by how high everyone hovers at the court. Today we're up near the roofs.
Did you see us from the bridge? All in a ring, veils out, nobody left out. The sky is wide enough for everyone, and so is the court.
routine.soar: I was out soaring round the islands. Three long loops and one I didn't mean to make.
You should have seen the light under the far islet just now: all the roots gold, and the cloud beneath lit like a pool.
I've been riding the updraft off the Lantern Spire. It goes up and up, and you just lie on it like a cushion.
My veils are still rippling from the speed. Give them a moment, they'll settle.
I flew so far out that {village} looked like a few pebbles on a cloth. Then I got lonely and came back.
There's a spot past the Cloud Garden where the wind folds over itself. Hit it right and you turn a full circle without trying.
I like to skim right down on top of the cloud sea with my veils trailing in the white. It leaves a wake behind you, like a fish.
Soaring clears my head. I went out with a worry and came back with a song.
A flock of birds went by beneath me, all in a line, all very serious. I tried to join in and was not invited.
Out past the edge of the village the air is wild and clean. It's like drinking from the top of a waterfall.
Round the Bell Pagoda three times for luck. Then a fourth, in case the first three didn't count.
When I'm soaring, the walkers on the bridges look so small and so brave, holding the rails as if the bridge might change its mind.
I was racing my shadow across the clouds. It won. It always wins on a sunny day.
Soaring's the best way to see your own village. From inside, it's home. From outside, it's a wonder.
Did you see me go by, {player}? I waved. You were looking at your feet. Walkers always look at their feet.
routine.chat: I was just talking with {neighbour}. We started on peaches and ended up on what the stars are for. That happens.
{friend} and I have been chatting since the bell. I don't even remember what about. Something good.
You've caught me between conversations. My voice is still warm from the last one.
I was having a long talk about nothing at all. Those are the best kind.
We were talking about you, actually, walker. Only good things. Mostly about your boots.
That was {friend}. We've been friends since our veils were short, and we still finish each other's songs.
I was hearing all about someone's new nest. They want round windows. Everyone wants round windows.
A neighbour was telling me their nightmare: they'd walked. Walked! On the ground! They woke up shaking. Can you imagine?
I was being advised. About my own veils. By {neighbour}. I've flown in them for years, but thank you, {neighbour}.
Talking is half of what we do up here. The other half is singing. The third half is listening.
We were swapping Lengthening stories. Mine was a disaster. I'll tell you someday, when I know you better.
We were trying to remember the third verse of an old wind song, and neither of us could. Do you know any wind songs, walker?
{friend} just went off to the Cloud Garden and left me mid-sentence. That always happens when {friend} is losing an argument.
I've been gossiping. A little. Kindly. That's allowed, as long as you'd say it to their face.
We were planning a trip to a Wind Shrine with gifts for the winds: peaches for Sefa, a song for Vell, and a scarf for Borre, poor cold thing.
routine.evensong: You've caught me between verses. I slipped out of the Evensong to say hello; I'll slip back before the last one.
My voice is still warm from singing. I always feel lighter after the Evensong, as if I'd put something heavy down.
The harps were perfect tonight. Nobody came in early, nobody went flat. That happens maybe twice a year.
I sing the low part. It's not grand, but without it the high voices would float right off into the sky.
Every Evensong I close my eyes on the last note. When I open them, the day's gone, just like that.
My throat's a bit sore. I sang too loud in the second verse. I always do; I can't help it.
The living sing the Evensong, and the ones who've gone up past the blue hum along. That's what I was taught, and tonight I believed it.
The children always rush the ending so they can play in the dusk. We let them. We were exactly the same.
Tonight the whole court sang like one Cirri. Those are the nights you keep.
Singing with everyone makes me feel like one thread in a great weave. Not much alone, but part of something.
My veils are still swaying to it. Look. They don't know when to stop.
I missed my cue tonight because I was watching the sunset. Nobody minded. Everyone's missed one for a sunset.
The harpists slipped an old whale verse in tonight. Somebody must be hoping for a visit.
Evensong-time is the best time for a talk. Everyone's soft and tired and kind, even me.
{player}, did you hear us from the bridge? You were swaying. Don't deny it. I saw.
routine.escort: I've just come back from swimming beside an Old Singer. My ears are still full of its song.
Have you ever been close to something that big, walker? It's like keeping pace with a hill that breathes.
Its cloud brushed my veils as I went past. They're still damp, and they smell of some far-off sky.
I sang back to it. I always do. I don't know if it hears, but once, just once, it turned its eye toward me.
My heart's so high I could float without veils. I swam with a whale!
Up close, an Old Singer's skin is all soft grey ripples, like a cloud remembering it used to be rain.
Five of us flew out and kept beside it until the village was a speck. Then it sang, and we turned for home.
You don't hear a whale song when you're that close. You feel it, in your bones. Mine are still humming.
If a whale sings to you, you'll have fair winds on every journey for a year. That's what we tell the children, and I'm keeping it.
It had little clouds resting along its back, like children asleep on a grown-up's shoulders.
It went on east without us. I wanted to follow. One day I think I just might.
I touched its fin. Very gently. It was warm. Nobody believes me, but it was warm.
We always come back from a whale quiet. There's nothing to say after a thing like that. Except, well, this.
It blew a puff of cloud right over us, and we came out of it laughing and dripping like koi in the rain.
{child} begged to come. Next time, when their veils are long enough to keep up.
routine.shelter: Come in, come in, out of that! A nest isn't much against thunder, but it has walls, and walls are something.
I've been curled up over my cushion humming since the storm peal. It helps. Not much, but it helps.
Every time the thunder goes, the whole nest shivers, and so do I.
I was humming the little ones to sleep. They're not asleep. Neither am I. We're all just humming now.
You came here through that, {player}? You're braver than every Cirri in {village} put together.
Don't stand near the window. Lightning can see you through glass. I don't know if that's true, but I'm not testing it.
I've tucked my veils right in round me. Storms like a loose end. They pull.
It'll pass. They always pass. I tell myself so between every rumble.
I keep counting between the flash and the boom. The gaps are getting longer. That's good. That's very good.
Sorry, I'm not much company. Storms make me small. Stay a moment, though? Talking helps.
{partner} is humming the old storm song beside me. Badly. It's the best sound in the world right now.
In a storm the sky stops being ours. It belongs to the lightning, and we just wait to be given it back.
Honey, a cushion, someone to hum with. That's all you need to outlast a storm. That, and courage, and I'm a little short today.
The thunder is only the sky clearing its throat before a song, my elders said. I wish it would just sing.
Little ones hide under both veils in a storm. I'm grown now, so I only hide under one.
routine.idle: Doing nothing, and doing it very well, thank you.
I was watching the clouds go by underneath. They never come round the same twice.
Nothing much. I let the wind turn me in a slow circle. I've seen the whole village twice.
Thinking, mostly. About what, I couldn't tell you. It drifted off before I caught it.
I've been watching a beetle on the bridge rail for ages. It walks everywhere. Doesn't it get tired?
Just hanging in the air, letting my veils do the work. Some days you need to be carried.
Keep your veil whole and your heart light, we say. Today both are taken care of, so I'm doing nothing about either.
I was seeing how long I could hover without moving at all. Then you said hello, and I wobbled.
Nothing to do, nowhere to be. When that happens up here, we call it a gift and we don't spoil it by rushing.
Four notes, over and over, for an hour now. I don't know what song they're from. Maybe no song yet.
I was looking down at the ground and wondering what it's like to be held by it all the time. Is it nice?
Just drifting. I let {wind} decide where to put me, and it put me here, by you.
I was counting the lanterns on the bridges. Same number as yesterday. Very reassuring.
Mm? Oh, I was miles away, somewhere over the far islands in my head. Hello, walker.
{player}! I was hoping someone would come along and give me an excuse not to do anything useful.
village.whale: Look! An Old Singer, right there past the islands! Every thread in my veils just stood on end.
Hush a moment. Can you hear it? That low sound under everything. That's the whale singing.
A whale, this close to {village}! Everyone will be out to meet it in a breath.
See the little clouds on its back? It carries them like a gardener carries seedlings, off somewhere to grow into weather.
I should be flying out to meet it. Everyone should. Why are we still talking? Come to the rail and watch, at least.
Meeting a whale is a blessing, and seeing one is half a blessing. You've just had half a blessing, walker.
Every time an Old Singer passes, I wonder where it's been. Over seas we've never seen, over lands nobody has named.
Look at the way it rolls, so slow, turning its belly to the sun. It's enjoying the day as much as we are.
As a child I thought whales were islands that had learned to swim. Look at it. Can you blame me?
That's an old one. See how high its clouds are heaped? Somebody far off is going to get rain.
The koi have all gone still. They always do when a whale passes. Even fish know when to listen.
Its shadow just slid over the Cloud Garden. Everything went dim and blue for a moment, as if evening came early.
The children are already flying out to it. Someone go after them, or they'll follow it halfway across the sky.
{player}, you're lucky. Some walkers come up a dozen times and never see an Old Singer.
There! It blew! See that puff of cloud? A brand new little cloud, just born.
village.koi: The koi are out. Look at them, turning in the air like gold leaves that forgot to fall.
See the big white one with the red cap? That's the oldest koi in the garden. The gardeners say it was here before the bridges.
If you're very lucky one of them will shed a Sky Scale while you watch. Keep an eye below them.
The koi always swim toward voices. They know who scatters the peach skins.
A whole school of them, turning all at once. How do they decide? Nobody tells them, and they never bump.
I could watch the koi for hours. I have, actually. The gardeners keep shooing me off.
See how the light comes through their fins? Like veilcloth. Maybe that's where the first weavers got the idea.
The gardeners say each koi has its own name. I've only learned three, and they all answer to "peach".
Walkers keep their fish in water, I'm told, where they never come up. How do you ever get to know them?
A Sky Scale once fell from one of these right onto my veil. It's in my nest still, wrapped in veilcloth.
Watch that little sky-blue one at the back. Always last, always late, always happy. I feel very close to that koi.
The koi love the children. They follow them round the garden in a long gold tail.
The koi pool is the calmest place in {village}. Even on bad days the koi swim their same slow circles.
Look, they're all facing the wind. Koi always swim into it. We read the day by them sometimes.
{player}, hold still. One's looking at you. They're curious about walkers. You're the only thing up here that clumps.
village.children: Listen to them! You'd think there were fifty, and there's only a handful.
They're playing chase round the Lantern Spire. Someone will clip a veil, then there'll be tears, and then they'll go again.
That one there learned to loop yesterday and has done it forty times today. Everyone has had to watch every one.
Children's veils are so short they have to work twice as hard to stay up. That's why they never stop moving.
I used to play that one. Catch-the-Puff: you grab a little cloud and race it home before it melts away.
They'll call you groundling, walker. From them it's a kindness. They're fascinated by you.
Every season somebody gets stuck in a skywood tree and has to be fetched down. I'd bet a peach on that one, today.
Every one of them is counting the days to their Lengthening. Every single day, out loud.
Look how they bob. Little veils, big hearts. We were all that loud once.
Do walker children play like ours? Ours mostly play at dropping and catching themselves at the last moment. It's dreadful to watch.
{child} is in that heap of giggles somewhere. Hear the loudest laugh? That's ours.
If one of them asks you to walk along the bridge so they can watch, humour them. They think walking is the funniest thing in the world.
They're racing the koi round the pool. The koi are winning, and the children are pretending they let them.
I watch them and remember my first loop. I went round once, couldn't stop, and went round eleven more times.
Hear that? That's the sound of nobody doing their chores. Good for them.
village.harp: Hear that harp? Nobody's playing it. That's the wind, practising.
The harps are tuned to {wind} today. Listen to the way the low strings lean.
Put your hand near the strings. Not on, near. You can feel the air shiver.
That harp's been turning over the same phrase all day. The harpists say it's thinking.
The oldest harps in the Hall of Echoes were strung before anyone living was born. They know songs we've forgotten.
Every wind plays a harp differently. Aure plucks. Sefa strokes. Vell sings. Borre slaps.
When a harp goes quiet like that, the wind is holding its breath. Wait. There.
A harp near your nest means good dreams. Bad tuning means very strange ones. Ask me how I know.
A wind harp has no player, walker. You build it and tune it, and then you let the sky decide what it says.
Listen to that little run, going up. That's the harp answering a gust. They talk, wind and harp.
Once I heard two harps on two different islands play the same note at the same moment. I've been waiting to hear it again ever since.
The harps get restless before the weather turns. You'll hear a change before you feel it.
When a walker plays one of our harps, every Cirri in earshot comes to listen. We can't help it. Try it, and watch us come.
That one's a little sour on the top string. Hear it? Don't tell the harpists I noticed, or they'll have me holding the tuning key all evening.
A harp is the only thing in {village} that never sleeps. At night it plays for nobody, very softly.
village.evensong: Listen! The Evensong's begun. I'll go in a moment. I'm not missing the last verse for anything.
Hear the harps leading? Now the low voices. Now everyone. It gives me shivers every single time.
Forgive me whispering. It's rude to talk over the Evensong, but I couldn't let a walker pass without a hello.
This is the part where the children come in. Hear them? A little ahead of everyone, as always.
You can hear the Evensong from anywhere in {village}, but nowhere sounds like right over the court.
The sun's nearly down and so is the song. We time it so the last note and the last light go out together.
Hum along if you like. There are no wrong notes in the Evensong, only ones nobody's used yet.
That high voice floating over everyone? That's {friend}. Showing off. Beautifully.
The whole court is full of veils swaying the same way. From above, it must look like one big cloud breathing.
The song carries out over the cloud sea. Somewhere below, walkers must hear it and wonder where it's coming from.
Every dusk, every village, the same song. Different voices, though, and ours are the best. Don't tell the other villages.
I ought to be in there singing. But the Courtesy says a guest comes first, so I'll sing twice as loud tomorrow.
Watch the bridges: a new lantern wakes with every verse. By the last line the whole village will be lit.
Close your eyes, {player}. Now you're not a walker. Now you're just someone in the sky, listening.
The Evensong is the only time the whole village is in one place. Look at us. That's everyone. Every single one.

ask: Where do you live, walker? Somewhere down under all that cloud?
Do you have a home below? I've always wondered what a walker's nest looks like.

answers.label: A house I built myself
answers.reply: You built it? Stone on stone, with your own hands? No wonder you're so sturdy.

answers.label: Wherever night finds me
answers.reply: A wanderer! You're more like the winds than you know. They never sleep in the same place twice either.

answers.label: In a hole in a hill
answers.reply: Inside the hill? Under the dirt, with the roots and the dark? Oh, you brave, strange thing.

answers.label: Up here, if you'll have me
answers.reply: Here? Oh, walker. Then {village} has one more nest to keep an eye on.

ask: Have you ever fallen? From somewhere really, really high?
Tell me true. Have you ever fallen a long, long way?

answers.label: More times than I can count
answers.reply: More than you can count! And still you come up here. That's either very brave or very forgetful.

answers.label: Once, and never again
answers.reply: Once is plenty for anyone. You landed in one piece, didn't you? You must have. Here you are.

answers.label: Never. I'm careful
answers.reply: Careful! Good. The careful ones get to come back and visit.

answers.label: Only in dreams
answers.reply: In dreams! The kind where your stomach drops and you wake up kicking? We have those too.

ask: If you had veils, which of the Four Winds would you want under them?
Every Cirri has a wind they love best. Which would be yours, do you think?

answers.label: Aure, who brings the dew
answers.reply: Aure! You'd be up before the bell with dew on your eyelashes. I like you already.

answers.label: Sefa, warm and lazy
answers.reply: Sefa! Smells of peaches and never in a hurry. You'd doze in the air all afternoon.

answers.label: Vell, who carries songs
answers.reply: Vell, the evening wind. Then you'd always arrive just in time for the Evensong.

answers.label: Borre, cold and wild
answers.reply: Borre? The storm-bringer? You're a strange one, walker. A strange, brave one.

ask: Do walkers dream of flying? I've always, always wondered.
When you sleep down there, do you ever dream you're up here with us?

answers.label: Every night
answers.reply: Every night! Then some part of you has been flying with us all along, and we never saw.

answers.label: I dream of falling
answers.reply: Of falling. Oh. That's only flying with the ending gone wrong. We'll find you a better ending.

answers.label: I dream of digging
answers.reply: Digging! Even asleep, you go down. Walkers are a marvel and a mystery.

answers.label: I never remember
answers.reply: Then you leave your dreams behind like an empty nest. A little sad. A little restful.

ask: What's under the ground? All the way down, I mean, past the grass.
If I could dig, which I can't, what would I find under the ground?

answers.label: Stone, then more stone
answers.reply: Just stone? All the way down? How does anybody breathe?

answers.label: Caves full of glowing things
answers.reply: Glowing caves! A night sky, turned upside down and buried. I want to see it and I never want to see it.

answers.label: Old ruins and old bones
answers.reply: Ruins? Like our Belltowers, only sunk the other way? Who built them? Did they grow too heavy too?

answers.label: Something that listens
answers.reply: Something that listens? Down in the dark, under everything? Oh, I wish I hadn't asked.

ask: Do you have a nest of your own down there? Someone keeping it warm?

answers.label: A home, and someone in it
answers.reply: Someone waiting for you! Then fly carefully. Walk carefully. You know what I mean.

answers.label: Just me, and I like it
answers.reply: A nest for one. Quiet, tidy, every cushion yours. There's a lot to be said for that.

answers.label: A cat, mostly
answers.reply: A cat keeps your nest! It would hate it up here: so many koi, all out of reach.

answers.label: Not yet
answers.reply: Not yet. That's a good, open sort of word. The sky likes it too.

ask: Would you wear a veil of your own, if the weavers made one for you?
I keep wondering how you'd look with veils. Would you want them?

answers.label: More than anything
answers.reply: More than anything! I'll tell the Loom House. They won't listen to me, but I'll tell them.

answers.label: I'd be too scared
answers.reply: Too scared of the height? Everyone is, at first. Even our children shake before the Lengthening.

answers.label: My feet suit me fine
answers.reply: Your feet suit you. Fair enough. Someone has to keep the ground company.

ask: Which clouds do you like best? The ones you see from underneath, I mean.

answers.label: Big and puffy
answers.reply: The puffy ones! From up here they look like sheep asleep in a meadow.

answers.label: Thin and wispy
answers.reply: The wispy ones are cirrus! That's what veils are woven from. You've liked veils all along and never knew.

answers.label: Pink ones at sunset
answers.reply: The sunset ones are blushing at the Evensong. Everybody knows that.

answers.label: Dark storm clouds
answers.reply: Storm clouds? The ones that grumble? You'd get on with Borre. I'd stay in my nest.

ask: It's raining past us right now. What does rain feel like where it lands?
We only ever watch rain fall away from us. What's it like at the bottom?

answers.label: Cold and lovely
answers.reply: Lovely! I knew it. All those drops couldn't be falling somewhere sad.

answers.label: Like drums on a roof
answers.reply: Drums on a roof! So rain makes music when it lands. Nobody ever told me that.

answers.label: Wet. Just wet
answers.reply: Just wet. Ha! That is the most walker answer I've ever had.

ask: Cats or koi? Everyone in {village} has picked a side, and it's getting serious.

answers.label: Cats
answers.reply: Cats! Fluffy, proud, and they'd eat our koi in a heartbeat. I'll keep it quiet.

answers.label: Koi
answers.reply: Koi! Good. The koi side is winning, I think. They'd thank you, if they could.

answers.label: Parrots, they fly
answers.reply: Parrots! Flying, talking, colourful. That's almost one of us, with feathers.

answers.label: Cats who leave koi alone
answers.reply: There's no such cat. But I like that you believe in one.

ask: Don't your feet get tired? Carrying all of you, all day, everywhere?

answers.label: Every single evening
answers.reply: Every evening! Then put them up somewhere tonight. Up is good for everything.

answers.label: Never, they're strong
answers.reply: Strong feet! I suppose they'd have to be, with all the iron and stone and mud you carry about.

answers.label: That's what horses are for
answers.reply: Horses! Walkers that carry walkers. The ground is full of clever ideas.

ask: What frightens walkers? If I ever go down there, I want to know what to fly away from.

answers.label: Creepers
answers.reply: Creepers? The green ones that hiss and burst? They sound nearly as rude as fireworks.

answers.label: The dark
answers.reply: The dark. I understand. At least our dark has stars in it. Yours has walls.

answers.label: Falling
answers.reply: Falling. Then you're very brave to come all the way up here. Very, very brave.

answers.label: Nothing much
answers.reply: Nothing much? Hm. Either you've seen everything, or you're fibbing a little.

ask: When is the sky at its best, do you think? I need to settle something with a friend.

answers.label: Dawn
answers.reply: Dawn! Pink and gold and quiet, before the bell. That's the right answer. I'll go and tell them.

answers.label: High noon
answers.reply: Noon, when everything shines and nothing has a shadow. Bold.

answers.label: Dusk, at the Evensong
answers.reply: Dusk, when we sing the day down! I hoped you'd say that.

answers.label: Night, with the stars
answers.reply: The stars! You'd be up with the lamplighter, counting them.

ask: Have you ever heard the Evensong? From down on the ground, I mean, at dusk.

answers.label: Faintly, most evenings
answers.reply: You hear it! All the way down! Then we've been singing to you all this time and never knew.

answers.label: I thought it was the wind
answers.reply: The wind? Well, Vell carries it, so you weren't so wrong. Next time, listen for the harps.

answers.label: Never, but I'd like to
answers.reply: Then come up at dusk and stand by the Veil Court with your eyes closed. You'll see. Hear, I mean.

ask: Have you tasted a sky peach yet? Be honest.

answers.label: Yes, and it was perfect
answers.reply: Perfect! Soft, sweet and warm from the sun? That's a sky peach all right.

answers.label: Not yet
answers.reply: Not yet! Go to the Cloud Garden and ask. Nobody ever says no to a peach-asker.

answers.label: I like bread better
answers.reply: Bread? The cooked kind? From a fire? Oh. Well. Everyone's allowed one strange taste.

ask: Is it true walkers cook their food over fire? On purpose? Every day?

answers.label: Yes, it tastes better
answers.reply: Better! Fire, on purpose, every day, and it tastes better. I'll never understand the ground.

answers.label: Only when I have to
answers.reply: Only when you must. A sensible walker. A little sensible, anyway.

answers.label: I eat fruit, mostly
answers.reply: Fruit, like us? Berries and peaches and no flames at all? Oh, I could hug you.

ask: Birds are tiny specks from up here. What are they like close up?

answers.label: Chickens can't even fly
answers.reply: Can't fly? Birds, with feathers and everything, that can't fly? That's the saddest thing I've ever heard.

answers.label: Parrots talk back
answers.reply: They talk? Like us? What do they say? Do they say rude things? I hope they say rude things.

answers.label: Quick, and then gone
answers.reply: Like a breath of Aure. Yes, that's how they look from here too.

ask: Do you carry anything for luck? Up here we keep Sky Scales, mostly.

answers.label: A Sky Scale, now
answers.reply: You do? Someone gave you their luck. That's no small thing, walker. Keep it close.

answers.label: A totem, always
answers.reply: A totem! The little doll that brings walkers back? Then you've more luck than a koi.

answers.label: I make my own luck
answers.reply: Your own luck! The wise ones say that too. They also keep three Sky Scales each, I notice.

ask: Stairs. Please explain stairs to me. Why not just go up?

answers.label: They're slow flying
answers.reply: Slow flying! Oh, that's sweet. Very, very slow flying.

answers.label: Heavy feet need steps
answers.reply: Little steps for heavy feet. So stairs are kind. Who knew?

answers.label: I'd rather a Wind Stone
answers.reply: Wouldn't everyone? The Courtesy is the best gift the first windkeepers ever gave.

ask: How far have you walked? What's the farthest your feet have ever taken you?

answers.label: Past every map I own
answers.reply: Past the edge of every map! You're a wind with boots on.

answers.label: To the End and back
answers.reply: The End? The end of what? Of everything? And you came back to tell us?

answers.label: Somewhere full of fire
answers.reply: A land of fire, and you went in? Walker, you frighten me. You frighten me and I'm proud of you.

answers.label: Here is the farthest
answers.reply: Here! So the farthest anyone has gone is up. I like that very much.

ask: How do walkers sleep? Lying flat on the ground like a dropped glove?

answers.label: In a bed, flat out
answers.reply: Flat on a bed, like a leaf on a pond. And you don't slide off?

answers.label: Under the open stars
answers.reply: Under the stars, nothing over you. Then we sleep under the same sky, just at different ends of it.

answers.label: Hardly at all
answers.reply: Hardly at all? That's how the night-moths find you. Sleep! Please!

ask: Have you ever seen a Cloud Whale? One of the Old Singers, up close?

answers.label: Yes, and I heard it sing
answers.reply: You heard one sing! Then you're blessed, truly. Some wait a whole life for that.

answers.label: Only a shadow, far off
answers.reply: A shadow on the clouds. That's how it starts. Next time you'll be close enough to hear.

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never! Then keep watching the high sky. When it happens, you'll know. Everyone knows.

ask: Do you play anything? A harp, a flute, a drum, a horn?

answers.label: A flute, a little
answers.reply: A flute! Then you've already got half a song in your chest. Breath is everything.

answers.label: Note blocks
answers.reply: Note blocks! The boxes that sing when you hit them? Music you hit! How wonderfully bossy.

answers.label: I hum, mostly
answers.reply: Humming is how every song begins. Even the Evensong started as somebody's hum.

answers.label: Nothing at all
answers.reply: Then you listen, and good listeners are rarer than good players.

ask: Are you afraid of heights? Be honest. I won't tell the windkeeper.

answers.label: Terribly
answers.reply: Terribly, and still you came up. That's the bravest thing I've heard all season.

answers.label: Not one bit
answers.reply: Not one bit! The stomach of a Cirri and the feet of a walker. A fine mix.

answers.label: Only when I look down
answers.reply: Then look up. Up is where all the good things are anyway.

ask: If you brought a friend a flower, which would it be? I'm asking for a gardener I know.

answers.label: A red poppy
answers.reply: A poppy. Bright as a lantern and not a bit shy. I'll pass it on.

answers.label: A cornflower
answers.reply: A cornflower! Sky blue! Oh, the gardener will be unbearable about this.

answers.label: Lily of the valley
answers.reply: Lily of the valley. Little white bells on a stem. The bellkeeper will want some.

answers.label: Any, if it's given kindly
answers.reply: Any flower, given kindly. The gardener will pretend that's not the right answer. It is.

ask: What do walkers eat in the morning? I've heard terrible things.

answers.label: Eggs, cooked
answers.reply: Eggs? Birds' eggs? Cooked over fire? Please don't tell the birds. I certainly won't.

answers.label: Bread and honey
answers.reply: Honey! At last, something sensible. We could breakfast together, you and I.

answers.label: A bowl of stew
answers.reply: Stew, at this hour? Hot, heavy and out of a pot. How do you ever get off the ground after that? Oh. You don't.

answers.label: Nothing, I skip it
answers.reply: Skip it? Walker! Eat something. Even a berry. Promise me.

ask: Do you wish on stars, where you come from? Here we wish on the koi.

answers.label: Every night
answers.reply: Every night! Then the stars must know your voice by now.

answers.label: I'll wish on a koi now
answers.reply: On a koi! Pick a plump one, they listen better. Don't tell the gardeners I said so.

answers.label: Wishing doesn't work
answers.reply: Doesn't it? Then why do I feel lighter every time I do it?

ask: Who's your dearest friend, down on the ground? Tell me about them.

answers.label: My dog
answers.reply: A dog! I've watched them from above, running in circles for joy. I'd love to run in circles.

answers.label: A villager I trade with
answers.reply: One of the bell-village folk! They wave sometimes, when we fly over. You'd be surprised.

answers.label: You, maybe?
answers.reply: Me? Oh. Oh, walker. Yes. Yes, all right. That's settled, then.

answers.label: I'm still looking
answers.reply: Still looking. Look up now and then. That's all I'll say.

ask: Do you miss the ground when you're up here? Even a little?

answers.label: Not at all
answers.reply: Not at all! Careful, or the weavers will start measuring you for veils.

answers.label: My feet do
answers.reply: Your feet miss it! Poor things. They must feel so lost up here with nothing to do.

answers.label: Only the trees
answers.reply: We have trees! Skywood, with peaches on. But I know. Not the same as a forest.

ask: Have you ever felt grounded? Not the walking kind. The heavy kind, inside.
Do walkers ever feel low? The heavy sort of low, where nothing lifts?

answers.label: Yes, for a long while
answers.reply: Then I'm glad you're here, where the air is thin and nothing weighs much. Stay as long as you need.

answers.label: Sometimes, at night
answers.reply: Night is heavy for everyone. That's why we sing the day down first. Come to the Evensong; it helps.

answers.label: Not since I came here
answers.reply: Not since you came here? That might be the kindest thing a walker has ever said to me.

answers.label: I'd rather not say
answers.reply: Then don't. The sky never asks twice.

ask: If you had wings for a whole day, where would you fly first?

answers.label: Straight up to you
answers.reply: To me? Of all the sky? Then I'll be waiting. Don't be late.

answers.label: Over the ocean
answers.reply: The ocean! All that blue with more blue underneath. I've only ever seen it from very far up.

answers.label: Into a storm
answers.reply: Into a storm? Borre would knock you out of the sky and laugh about it. Please don't.

answers.label: Somewhere new
answers.reply: Somewhere new. The restless ones would call that the only right answer.

ask: What do walkers sing? Do you have songs for the evening, like we do?

answers.label: Lullabies
answers.reply: Lullabies! So walkers sing their little ones to sleep too. We're not so different.

answers.label: Loud songs, badly
answers.reply: Loud and badly is how most songs ought to be sung. The harpists would disagree.

answers.label: I don't sing
answers.reply: Not at all? Not even a hum? That's the saddest news I've had all week.

answers.label: Work songs
answers.reply: Work songs! For digging and chopping? I'd love to hear a digging song.

ask: Where do walkers go in a storm? We go to our nests and hum to the little ones.

answers.label: Indoors, quickly
answers.reply: Indoors, quickly. Good. Doors are the best thing about walker houses.

answers.label: I stand right in it
answers.reply: You stand in it? In the lightning? Walker, no!

answers.label: Down a mine
answers.reply: Down under the ground, where Borre can't follow. Clever. Dark, but clever.

ask: What did you think, the first time you looked up and saw a sky village?

answers.label: That I was dreaming
answers.reply: Dreaming! Lots of walkers say that. Then they come up, and they're still dreaming.

answers.label: That it might fall on me
answers.reply: Fall! No, no. We build light so we never fall. That's the whole point of us.

answers.label: That I had to get up there
answers.reply: And here you are. The sky loves a walker who won't be told no.

ask: How did you find your way up? Did someone show you the Wind Stone?

answers.label: I found it myself
answers.reply: Found it yourself! Most walkers stroll right past and never feel the wind in it.

answers.label: I followed a Cirri
answers.reply: You followed one of us! Then we brought you here without even knowing. Lucky us.

answers.label: I built a tower
answers.reply: A tower? Block by block, all the way up through the clouds? I'm speechless. Nearly.

ask: Have you ever licked the ground? What does it taste of? I need to know. It's important.
Does the ground taste of anything? {friend} says it tastes of boots.

answers.label: Rain and dust
answers.reply: Rain and dust! So the ground is where rain goes to get dusty. I knew it!

answers.label: Never licked it
answers.reply: Never? You've stood on it your whole life and never once had a lick? Walkers are very strange.

answers.label: Like honey, secretly
answers.reply: Honey! I knew walkers were keeping the best bit to themselves!

ask: Can you do a loop? Even a little one? Even a wobbly one?
How many loops can walkers do in a row? My best is twenty-three. Twenty-two and a half.

answers.label: I can do a cartwheel
answers.reply: A cartwheel? A ground loop? Do it! ...That's the best thing I've ever seen! Do it again!

answers.label: With wings, yes
answers.reply: With borrowed wings? Then we'll loop together one day. You go first. I'll go second, but better.

answers.label: Not a single one
answers.reply: Not one? I'll teach you. Step one: be up in the air. ...Hmm. We'll skip step one.

ask: What do walker children play down there? We've played everything up here. Twice.

answers.label: Hide and seek
answers.reply: You have hide and seek too? Where do you hide? Behind the ground? Under it?

answers.label: Tag
answers.reply: Tag! Ground tag! I bet it's slower. I bet it's just as fun.

answers.label: Building sandcastles
answers.reply: Castles made of sand? Up here they'd blow away before you finished the door.

answers.label: Skipping stones
answers.reply: You throw stones at water and they bounce? On purpose? That's the best walker thing yet!

ask: There's a new little koi in the pool and nobody's named it yet. You pick! Quick, before the gardener does.

answers.label: Puddle
answers.reply: Puddle! It's perfect. It's small and round and wet. Hello, Puddle!

answers.label: Captain Fin
answers.reply: Captain Fin! It'll be the bossiest koi in the sky. Look at it. It already is.

answers.label: Peach
answers.reply: Peach! Because it's pinkish and round. I won't eat it. I won't!

answers.label: Name it after you
answers.reply: After me? A koi called {name}? That's the best thing anyone's ever done. It's the best koi now.

ask: Are there really monsters on the ground at night? Real ones? With teeth?

answers.label: Yes, but I'm brave
answers.reply: You're brave? Braver than thunder? I'll tell the little ones. They'll want to touch your boots for luck.

answers.label: A few, so I stay inside
answers.reply: Inside's good. We stay in our nests when it's scary too. Walkers and Cirri, the same.

answers.label: Only friendly ones
answers.reply: Friendly monsters with friendly teeth? I don't believe you. I want to, though.

ask: Do walkers keep pets? What's yours called? Tell me everything.

answers.label: A loyal dog
answers.reply: A dog! I've seen them from up here, running in circles. They're like ground koi!

answers.label: A cat
answers.reply: A cat! Do cats like heights? Bring it up! No, the koi would hate it. Maybe don't.

answers.label: A horse
answers.reply: A horse? The kind walkers sit on? Is it like flying, only bumpier?

answers.label: No pets, just me
answers.reply: Just you? Then you can share our koi. All of them. I'll introduce you.

ask: If the weavers made you a veil and you could fly, where would you go first?

answers.label: Swim with a whale
answers.reply: With an Old Singer! I'd come too. We'd hum at it and it would hum back.

answers.label: Higher than this village
answers.reply: Higher than us? Up where the blue goes dark? You're braver than the grown-ups.

answers.label: Straight down, to show off
answers.reply: Straight back down? With a veil? ...Oh, to show everybody! That's a very good reason.

answers.label: Here, to see you
answers.reply: To see me? All that flying, just for me? That's the nicest wish I've ever heard.

ask: When I'm Lengthened, what colour should my long veils be? Everyone has white and rose. I want something different.

answers.label: All gold
answers.reply: All gold! I'll shine like the bell! The weavers will say no. I'll say you said.

answers.label: Sky blue all the way
answers.reply: Sky blue all the way, so I vanish into the sky! Nobody will ever find me at hide and seek.

answers.label: White and rose, like everyone
answers.reply: Like everyone? ...Well, everyone does look very nice. Fine. You're right. Hmph.

answers.label: Night colours, with stars
answers.reply: Night colours with little stars in! I'll be a piece of the night that flies about.

ask: Are you a grown-up or a big child? I can't tell with walkers. You haven't got any veils to measure.

answers.label: A grown-up
answers.reply: A grown-up! But you play with me. Good. Grown-ups should do that more.

answers.label: A big child
answers.reply: A big child! Like me, only bigger. Then we're the same, and we're both allowed to play.

answers.label: A bit of both
answers.reply: Grown-up outside and child inside? Dad's like that. Dad pretends not to be.

ask: I'll tell you a secret if you tell me one first. That's the rule. You first!
Secrets swap! You tell me one, I tell you one. Walkers go first, it's only fair.

answers.label: I talk to my pickaxe
answers.reply: You talk to your pickaxe? Does it answer? Here's mine: I talk to the koi, and one of them answers.

answers.label: I'm scared of spiders
answers.reply: Spiders! Is that a ground thing? Here's mine: I'm scared of the long peal of the bell. Now we're even.

answers.label: I once got lost for days
answers.reply: Lost for days? Here's mine: I got lost behind the Loom House once. For ages. Nearly a whole song.

answers.label: No secrets from me
answers.reply: No secrets at all? Then I'll keep mine too. ...All right, one: I don't like honey. Don't tell anyone.

ask: When it's my Lengthening, will you come? Everyone brings a present. What would you bring me?

answers.label: A basket of sky peaches
answers.reply: Peaches! A whole basket! I'll share them. Some of them. One.

answers.label: A shiny diamond
answers.reply: A diamond? For my veils? ...Is it heavy? It's worth being a bit heavy for one day.

answers.label: A walker song
answers.reply: A walker song, just for me? Sung at my Lengthening? I'll remember it till my veils fray.

answers.label: Just myself
answers.reply: Just you? That's the best present. You'll be the only walker there. Everyone will look.

ask: We have to learn the Four Winds and the whole Evensong and the Courtesy. Do walker children have lessons? What do you learn?

answers.label: Letters and numbers
answers.reply: Letters and numbers! We have those too. I'm very good at the number four.

answers.label: How to build things
answers.reply: You learn to build? Houses and towers and bridges? Build me something! A small thing!

answers.label: How to face monsters
answers.reply: Monsters, in lessons? Walker lessons are much braver than ours. Ours have a lot of humming.

answers.label: I ran off instead
answers.reply: You ran off? From lessons? On your feet? ...Can you teach me how? Don't tell Mum I asked.

ask: If you find a Sky Scale, you get one wish. That's the rule. What would you wish for?

answers.label: A house full of peaches
answers.reply: A house full of peaches! You'd have to eat your way to the door. I'd help.

answers.label: A whale of my own
answers.reply: A whale of your own? Where would you keep it? In the sky, I suppose. It's big enough.

answers.label: Long veils for you, soon
answers.reply: For me? You'd spend your wish on me? I'm not crying. Koi water got in my eye.

answers.label: A hundred more wishes
answers.reply: A hundred more wishes! That's cheating. That's very, very clever cheating.

ask: Where does the sky end? You've been everywhere. You must know.
Does the sky stop somewhere? Grown-ups say no. Grown-ups say a lot of things.

answers.label: It never ends
answers.reply: Never? Then I'll never get bored. That's very good news. Thank you.

answers.label: At the stars
answers.reply: At the stars! So the stars are the edge. Like lanterns on the end of a bridge.

answers.label: At a place called the End
answers.reply: The End? There's a place called the End? That's a very good name for where something stops.

answers.label: I don't know either
answers.reply: You don't know either? Then we'll find out together. You walk, I'll fly.

ask: You're hurt! Come over by the koi pool. I keep a pot of peach-blossom salve for exactly this.
Hold out your arm. A gardener always has something soothing growing nearby.

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: Still now. It smells of blossom and stings for one breath, then nothing at all. There.

answers.label: I'll be all right
answers.reply: Then at least keep it clean. Dirt from below gets into everything.

ask: Oh, you're hurt. Let me see. I've mended worse tears than that.
Hold still a moment. Let me help with that, gently.

answers.label: Thank you
answers.reply: There. Slowly, slowly. Breathe the way Aure blows, soft and early. Better?

answers.label: It's nothing
answers.reply: Nothing, the hurt ones always say. I'll be here when it turns into something.

ask: Look at the state of you. Come here before you fall apart on our bridges.

answers.label: All right
answers.reply: Hold still, hold still. I've seen koi braver than you. There. Whole again.

answers.label: I'll manage
answers.reply: You always manage. I still worry. That's what friends are for, walker: the worrying.

ask: You're hurt. Let me play you something. Music mends more than people think.

answers.label: Please do
answers.reply: Close your eyes. Listen to the low string, and the next one. Feel it? The hurt goes where the music goes.

answers.label: Not now
answers.reply: Not now. Then I'll hum it later, out of earshot, and hope it finds you anyway.

ask: You look hollow, walker. Have a peach, or two. We've more than enough.
When did you last eat? Here, take some peaches before you wilt.

answers.label: Thank you
answers.reply: Eat them slowly. Well, eat them however walkers eat. With both hands, it looks like.

answers.label: I'm not hungry
answers.reply: Not hungry, with that face? Then I'll keep them warm for you.

ask: The top branches are heavy with peaches this week. Take a couple. I insist, and so does the tree.

answers.label: Gladly
answers.reply: Here, two of the sweetest, from up where Sefa sleeps. Juice down your chin is allowed.

answers.label: Save them
answers.reply: Save them? For whom? The koi? They'd eat them, you know.

ask: You're soaked through! Stand still and let me send a warm gust round you.

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: Arms out. A little more. There, feel it? Warm as an afternoon. Now you're only damp.

answers.label: I like being wet
answers.reply: You like it? Then you're stranger than a cloud. Drip happily, walker.

ask: Sefa has the sky today, warm and lazy. Shall I borrow a breath of it for you? You're dripping.

answers.label: Please do
answers.reply: There. Sefa's breath smells of peaches, did you notice? Stay a while, until you've stopped steaming.

answers.label: I'll dry on my own
answers.reply: On your own, slowly, in wet boots. The ground is so patient.

ask: It's dark and you've no light. Take a sky lantern, please. The night-moths hate them.
Wandering about in the dark? Here, take one of our lanterns.

answers.label: Thank you
answers.reply: Hold it high, not low. Light should come from above. That's how the sky does it.

answers.label: I can see fine
answers.reply: Fine, until a night-moth finds you. Keep to the bridge lanterns, then.

ask: I always light one lantern too many. Would you take the spare off my hands before dark?

answers.label: I'd love one
answers.reply: There. Freshly lit. It'll last you all the way down and back up again.

answers.label: Keep it lit here
answers.reply: Then I'll hang it on the bridge by the Lift Dock and call it yours.

ask: You're at the edge without a veil! Let me wrap a breath of wind round you, just in case.
Step back! Or at least let me tie a little wind round you first.

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: There. If you fall now, you'll float down slow as a feather. Still, don't fall.

answers.label: I won't fall
answers.reply: Everyone who ever fell was sure they wouldn't. Please step back.

ask: Keeping the wind is my work, and I'd rather not keep it under you. Let me tie some round you.

answers.label: Go ahead
answers.reply: Done. You'll drift like a dandelion seed for a minute. Don't waste it on falling.

answers.label: I trust my feet
answers.reply: Feet are for the ground, and you're not on the ground. Step back, please.

ask: Your borrowed wings are fraying. Let me look. I mend veils every day; wings can't be much harder.

answers.label: Please
answers.reply: A little membrane, a little thread, a lot of patience... there. Not new, but better.

answers.label: They'll hold
answers.reply: They'll hold until they don't. Bring them back before that, please.

ask: That veil's frayed at the tips. Hand it here; I can mend it in a breath.

answers.label: Thank you
answers.reply: Membrane at the tear, string through the weave, and a little gold if I had it. There. Whole again.

answers.label: I like it frayed
answers.reply: Frayed like an old soul's. All right, I won't fuss. Much.

ask: That {item} of yours is worn thin. Let me see what a weaver's hands can do with it.

answers.label: Go on, then
answers.reply: It isn't cloth, but a tear is a tear. There. It'll last a little longer now.

answers.label: It's fine as it is
answers.reply: As it is, then. Use it gently. Things wear out fast for walkers; you lean on them so.

ask: You're new here, aren't you? Do you know where the Wind Stone is, for getting back down?

answers.label: Tell me
answers.reply: Here, I'll tell you exactly where. Remember it; walkers forget which way the wind goes.

answers.label: I know the way
answers.reply: Then you're quicker than most. Fair wind going down.

ask: Welcome up! Keeping the Wind Stone is my work. Shall I tell you how to find it again?

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: Here's where it stands. On the dock, step into the shaft and crouch, and the wind lowers you gently.

answers.label: I'll find it
answers.reply: Good. And if you can't, ask anyone. The Courtesy is everyone's promise.

ask: The day's going down. Shall I sing you a bit of the Evensong, just us, before the others start?

answers.label: Please sing
answers.reply: Listen. Here's where Vell comes in, and here the harps, and there. You'll feel lighter for a while.

answers.label: Save it for later
answers.reply: Later, then, with everyone. It's better with the whole village anyway.

ask: I've been keeping something for you. A Sky Scale, from our koi. Will you take it?

answers.label: I'd be honoured
answers.reply: Keep it near. It's luck, and it's a little bit of me. That's how scales work.

answers.label: Keep your luck
answers.reply: Keep my luck? You're the only walker who'd say that. That's why I wanted you to have it.

ask: You've been good for trade and better company. Here, take this emerald. Never argue with a merchant.

answers.label: Thank you
answers.reply: A good merchant knows when to give. Spend it somewhere that makes you happy.

answers.label: I can't take that
answers.reply: You can't? Then I'll put it toward your first veil. You can't argue with that either.

ask: Is that a book? Walkers write with feathers, don't they? I've a few spare, if you'd like them.

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: Three good ones. Write something about the sky in it, would you? Something kind.

answers.label: I've got plenty
answers.reply: Plenty! Then you've been writing a lot. I'd love to read it someday.

ask: The Cloud Garden's blooming. Let me pick you something. Which one? No, I'll choose. I'm the gardener.

answers.label: I'd love that
answers.reply: This one. It grows best where it can see the sky. Like someone I know.

answers.label: Leave it growing
answers.reply: Leave it growing? That's a gardener's answer. You'd make a good one.

ask: Would you rather ride an Old Singer's back for a day, or have a Cloud Koi follow you about forever?

answers.label: Ride the whale
answers.reply: Up on its back with the little clouds! You'd hear the weather being sung from the inside.

answers.label: The koi, forever
answers.reply: A koi of your very own, bobbing at your shoulder! It would sulk every time you went indoors.

ask: Would you rather have elytra or a pair of real veils? Think carefully. I'm friends with a weaver.

answers.label: Elytra
answers.reply: Elytra. Fast, sleek and borrowed from somebody else. The weaver will be very quiet at supper.

answers.label: Veils, of course
answers.reply: Veils! Of course veils! I knew there was sky in you somewhere.

ask: Sky peaches forever, or honey forever? You may only pick one.

answers.label: Peaches
answers.reply: Peaches! Soft and warm and straight off the branch. The gardeners will cheer.

answers.label: Honey
answers.reply: Honey! Sticky fingers for the rest of your life. Worth it.

answers.label: A peach dipped in honey
answers.reply: That's not an answer, that's a festival. I'll allow it.

ask: Would you rather fly through one of Borre's storms, or drift through a whole day with no wind at all?

answers.label: The storm
answers.reply: The storm! You'd come out the other side with your hair in knots and a story to tell.

answers.label: The still day
answers.reply: A still day? Never trust a still day, walker. Nothing moves, nothing sings. It's eerie.

ask: Would you rather ring the great bell at dawn, or play a wind harp at the Evensong?

answers.label: Ring the bell
answers.reply: The bell! The whole sky would wake up because of you. The bellkeeper might even let you.

answers.label: Play the harp
answers.reply: The harp! You'd have to learn to listen to the wind first. It takes a while. It's worth it.

ask: Would you rather never come down from the sky again, or never come up?

answers.label: Never come down
answers.reply: Never come down! Then you'll need a nest. I'll ask about cushions.

answers.label: Never come up
answers.reply: Oh. That's honest, and it stings a little. I'd fly down to the bottom of the clouds and wave.

ask: Would you rather sleep on a cloud, or in the softest bed below?

answers.label: On a cloud
answers.reply: On a cloud! You'd wake up damp, but you'd wake up happy.

answers.label: My own bed
answers.reply: Your own bed. I understand. A nest is a nest, even a flat one.

ask: Would you rather be able to talk with the birds, or with the Four Winds?

answers.label: The birds
answers.reply: Birds! They'd only gossip about worms and each other. You'd love every minute.

answers.label: The winds
answers.reply: The winds! Then ask Borre why it's always so grumpy. Nobody has ever dared.

ask: Would you rather rain fell upward, or snow fell sideways forever?

answers.label: Rain falling up
answers.reply: Upward rain! It would land on us instead. I'd have to rethink my whole life.

answers.label: Sideways snow
answers.reply: Sideways snow. It would go on forever and never land anywhere. Borre would adore it.

ask: Would you rather have a lantern that never goes out, or one little star that follows you about?

answers.label: The lantern
answers.reply: The lantern. Sensible and warm, and the lamplighter could finally take a night off.

answers.label: The star
answers.reply: Your own star, bobbing along behind you all night! You'd never be lost again.

ask: Would you rather be as small as a koi, or as big as an Old Singer?

answers.label: Small as a koi
answers.reply: As small as a koi! You could ride along in the folds of somebody's veil.

answers.label: Big as an Old Singer
answers.reply: Enormous! Clouds would nap on your back and you'd hum the weather. I'd visit every day.

ask: Would you rather have a wind named after you, or a koi?

answers.label: A wind
answers.reply: A wind! Then once a day you'd have the sky, and we'd all greet you like a neighbour.

answers.label: A koi
answers.reply: A koi named after you! It would be the greediest one in the pool. I'm teasing. Mostly.

ask: Would you rather meet a night-moth in the dark, or a firework at noon?

answers.label: The night-moth
answers.reply: The night-moth. At least it doesn't bang, and its wings mend veils afterwards.

answers.label: The firework
answers.reply: A firework at noon? We'd all hide in the Loom House for a week. You're braver than the whole village.

ask: Would you rather float a hand's width off the ground forever, or fly as high as you like for one single hour?

answers.label: Float forever
answers.reply: A hand's width, forever. You'd never trip again. You'd never quite land either. I know how that feels.

answers.label: One hour, very high
answers.reply: One hour, as high as you like. You'd remember it all your life. I'd come with you.

ask: Would you rather hear every song the wind has ever carried, or sing one song the whole sky can hear?

answers.label: Hear every song
answers.reply: Every song ever carried! The Evensong a thousand dusks deep. I'd never get you to leave.

answers.label: Sing one song
answers.reply: One song for the whole sky. What would you sing? No, don't tell me. Save it.
